f.main_result: At 4 and 12 weeks there were no statistically significant differences between test and control implants in peri-implant hard and soft tissue height and thickness; test implants tended to have a more coronal free gingival margin and first bone contact.
f.sample_size: 16 test and 16 control implants in 8 dogs
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by a research contract with Sweden & Martina Dental Implants
f.limitations: Animal model with a reduced sample size, so the null hypothesis could not be rejected.

f.population: Nine dogs; mandibular premolar sockets
f.intervention: Immediate one-piece zirconia implant with xenograft (Bio-Oss Collagen) grafted in the buccal gap
f.comparison: Same implant without gap grafting (spontaneous healing)
f.main_result: Xenograft in the buccal gap gave a more coronal marginal mucosa and longer buccal barrier epithelium (shorter connective tissue contact) than control, with no significant difference in total supracrestal soft tissue height; less recession.
materials_brands: Straumann Pure Ceramic one-piece zirconia implant (narrow, 3.3 mm)
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grant 1215_2017

f.population: Partially or completely edentulous patients (and canine preclinical models)
f.intervention: Implants placed in healed ridges with thin or absent buccal bone wall
f.comparison: Thick or present buccal bone wall; augmented buccal wall
f.main_result: Sites with a thin buccal bone wall are more prone to major dimensional changes, vertical bone loss and mucosal recession, with biologic and esthetic complications; simultaneous augmentation of dehiscence-type defects favours stability.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no direct financial interests
f.limitations: Heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis; conclusions rest mainly on preclinical and nonrandomized studies.

f.population: Healthy patients receiving at least one dental implant
f.intervention: Direct measurement of soft tissue thickness at implant placement
f.comparison: Thin (<2 mm) versus thick (>=2 mm) peri-implant soft tissue
outcomes: radiographic marginal bone loss at 12 months or more
f.main_result: Implants with thick soft tissue had less marginal bone loss: WMD -0.80 mm (95% CI -1.18 to -0.42), P<0.0001.
f.sample_size: 8 articles in the review, 5 in the meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by a University of Michigan graduate research fund; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Considerable heterogeneity among studies in all comparisons.

f.population: 42 patients (27 partially edentulous maxilla, 15 edentulous mandible)
f.intervention: Non-submerged one-piece implants placed with the rough-smooth border at varying positions relative to the alveolar crest
f.comparison: Rough-smooth border placed below versus at or near the crest
outcomes: radiographic bone remodeling from implant shoulder to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: Mean bone remodeling was 1.10 mm by 6 months and virtually stable afterwards; it was greater when the rough-smooth border was below the crest (1.72 mm) than at or near it (0.68 mm).
materials_brands: Straumann titanium plasma-sprayed hollow-cylinder and solid-screw implants

f.population: 39 patients with 80 implants restored with single crowns or FDPs
f.intervention: Implant-supported single crowns or FDPs re-examined for interproximal contact loss
f.comparison: Implant sites without ICL
outcomes: plaque control record, BOP, probing depth
f.main_result: Interproximal contact loss occurred in 50% of implants after at least 10 years, mesial contacts more than distal, and was linked to +0.46 mm probing depth.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the University of Zurich clinic

f.population: 51 patients with a single delayed posterior maxillary implant
f.intervention: Platform-switched implants (Shape1, I-RES)
f.comparison: Conventional non-platform-switched implants (Screw Vent Tapered, Zimmer)
outcomes: mesial and distal marginal bone loss at 12 months
f.main_result: Marginal bone loss fell with greater abutment height and was nil at about 2.5 mm (platform-switched) versus 3.0 mm (conventional); control loss was over twice that of the test group.

f.intervention: Esthetic biological contour (EBC) concept: E, B and C zones of the implant emergence profile
f.main_result: The EBC concept divides the emergence profile into esthetic (E), bounded (B) and crestal (C) zones, each with a specific design recommendation.

f.population: 64 patients with edentulous posterior mandible/maxilla sites receiving bone level implants placed 1.5 mm subcrestally
f.intervention: Immediate tissue level (ITL) abutment torqued to the implant at surgery (no abutment disconnection)
f.comparison: Regular healing abutment at implant level with repeated abutment disconnections
outcomes: crestal bone loss at 1 month after prosthesis (T2) and at 1 year (T3)
f.main_result: Early bone loss was 0.14 mm (ITL) vs 0.64 mm (control), a significant 0.5 mm difference; at 1 year the difference was no longer significant (p = .22).
materials_brands: CONNECT immediate tissue level abutment (MIS Implant Technologies)
f.funding_coi: Funded by a grant from MIS Implant Technologies; first author reports study grant and lecture honoraria from MIS
f.limitations: Standardized periapical radiographs were not obtained.

f.population: Published literature on twelve dental implant types (subperiosteal, blade-vent, Brånemark screw, etc.)
f.intervention: Proposed criteria of implant success applied to assess long-term efficacy of each implant type
outcomes: long-term implant success rates by implant type
f.main_result: Review proposes stricter success criteria than the 1979 NIH minimal criteria; the Brånemark osseointegrated screw met the yardstick while e.g. subperiosteal implants showed 54% success at 15 years.

f.population: 50 patients with 119 implants (internal conical connection) supporting screw-retained fixed partial dentures
f.intervention: Implant-level (IL) connection of the screw-retained FPD
f.comparison: Abutment-level (AL) connection with multi-unit abutments
f.main_result: MBL change did not differ between groups at 1, 2 or 3 years (3 years: 0.18 mm AL vs 0.15 mm IL).
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech Implant System, Dentsply Sirona)
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Dentsply Sirona Implants; first author receives a personal fee from Dentsply Sirona

f.population: Premolar extraction sites (P1, P2) in five beagle dogs
f.intervention: Flapless extraction with or without socket preservation (BioOss Collagen plus free soft-tissue graft) versus flap elevation
f.comparison: Extraction without treatment (Tx 1) and with flap elevation/repositioning (Tx 2)
outcomes: volumetric tissue change on scanned casts at 2 and 4 months
f.main_result: Flapless groups showed significantly lower resorption than flap groups, and socket-preservation sites did better than untreated sockets.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: 54 included publications: 2 clinical papers, 8 human histology and 44 animal studies
f.intervention: Systematic review of biologic width structure and function around implants
f.main_result: Knowledge of biologic width around implants derives mainly from animal studies; controlled clinical human studies are insufficient.
f.limitations: Evidence is mainly animal-based with insufficient controlled human studies.

f.population: 103 partially edentulous patients, one internal hex implant each in posterior mandible, grouped by gingival thickness
f.intervention: Thickening of thin mucosa with allogenic membrane before two-stage implant placement (group B)
f.comparison: Thin tissues without thickening (A) and naturally thick tissues (C)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 1 year
f.main_result: At 1 year bone loss was 1.65/1.81 mm (thin), 0.31/0.34 mm (thin thickened) and 0.44/0.47 mm (thick) mesial/distal; thickening matched thick tissues.

f.population: 4 patients with thin mucosa (2 mm or less) receiving 12 two-piece implants
f.intervention: Platform-switching implants (Prevail, 3i Biomet)
f.comparison: Horizontally matching implant-abutment connection (Prodigy, BioHorizons)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 1 year
f.main_result: With thin mucosa, bone loss was about 1.7-1.8 mm for platform-switching implants versus 1.6-1.76 mm for controls, with no significant difference.
f.limitations: Pilot study with small sample, stated within the limitations of this pilot study.

f.population: 26 patients with 64 implants, placed in thin, medium or thick mucosa
f.intervention: Test implants placed about 2 mm supracrestally
f.comparison: Control implants placed at bone crest level
outcomes: crestal bone loss at 1 year by mucosal thickness group
f.main_result: Around supracrestal test implants bone loss was 1.35 mm in thin, 0.32 mm in medium and 0.12 mm in thick mucosa; control implants lost 1.55-1.8 mm regardless of thickness.

f.population: 97 patients with one bone-level implant each in posterior mandible, grouped by mucosal thickness
f.intervention: Thickening of thin mucosa with allogenic membrane during one-stage implant placement (T2)
f.comparison: Thin mucosa without thickening (T1) and naturally thick mucosa (C)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 2 months and 1 year
f.main_result: At 1 year bone loss was 1.22/1.14 mm (thin), 0.24/0.19 mm (thickened) and 0.22/0.20 mm (thick); thickened tissue matched thick tissue.

f.population: 19 partially edentulous patients with 46 implants (23 test, 23 control)
f.intervention: Test implants placed about 2 mm supracrestally, grouped by thin (A) or thick (B) mucosa
f.comparison: Control implants placed at bone level
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss at 1 year
f.main_result: Bone loss around test implants was 1.61/1.28 mm in thin mucosa versus 0.26/0.09 mm in thick mucosa (mesial/distal); controls lost about 1.8 mm.

f.population: 24 minipigs, 96 lateral augmentation sites on the mandible
f.intervention: Lateral GBR with DBBM:particulate autogenous bone ratios 50:50, 75:25, 100:0, or autogenous bone block covered with DBBM, under a collagen membrane
f.comparison: The different graft ratios and the autogenous bone block against each other, at 10, 20 and 30 weeks
f.main_result: After 30 weeks height reduction was about 1.7-1.8 mm (33-38%) for particulate grafts versus 0.2 mm (3.7%) for block graft; volume reduction did not differ at 30 weeks.
f.funding_coi: Grants from Danish Dentist Association, Region Northern Jutland and a foundation; Bio-Oss and Bio-Gide partly sponsored by Geistlich, pins by Dentsply Sirona

f.main_result: Periodontal regeneration evolved from barrier-membrane GTR to papilla-preservation and minimally invasive flaps with biologics, with combined intrabony and soft-tissue approaches.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interests

f.population: 12 systemically healthy patients with Miller class I and II gingival recessions
f.intervention: Porcine collagen matrix placed under a partial thickness flap
f.comparison: Subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Root coverage was 24.7 percent with connective graft and 16.6 percent with matrix; keratinized tissue gain was similar (4.33 vs 4.5 mm).
Four graft classes (autologous, allogeneic, xenogenic, alloplastic) all show bone regeneration; autogenous bone remains the gold standard.
f.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose

f.main_result: No current therapy regenerates the pulp-dentin complex in pulp necrosis; advanced scaffolds, antibiotic-eluting nanofibers and 3D-printed membranes are emerging strategies.
f.funding_coi: NIH/NIDCR grants

f.population: Patients treated with two-stage maxillary sinus augmentation via lateral approach (34 RCTs, 842 sinus augmentations)
f.intervention: Grafting biomaterials for sinus augmentation (xenografts, allografts, synthetic grafts, composites with autologous bone, PRP, BMC)
f.comparison: Autologous bone alone and other biomaterials, ranked by network meta-analysis
f.main_result: Bovine xenograft + bone marrow concentrate ranked highest for new bone (81%); autologous bone alone ranked twelfth (57%), so it was not confirmed as gold standard.
f.funding_coi: Grants (EFOP, GINOP); funders had no role; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 4 mongrel dogs; mandibular premolar extraction sites
f.intervention: Buccal pouch grafting with xenograft, FDBA, or FDBA + DFDBA
f.comparison: Untreated control pouch
f.main_result: Xenograft sites gained ridge width from T1 to T3 while control and FDBA sites lost width, and grafted sites kept soft tissue thickness.
f.funding_coi: University funds; no conflicts of interest

f.main_result: Bovine xenografts and synthetics dominate the cranio-maxillofacial graft market; autografts remain gold standard but no graft has all ideal properties.
f.funding_coi: EU Horizon2020 Eurostars project and Research Council of Norway

f.main_result: Calcium phosphate degradation in vivo occurs through phagocytic cell activity and acidic dissolution with osteoclast resorption, influenced by composition and ion substitution.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.main_result: No marketed bone substitute has all ideal properties; autografts and allografts have donor-site and immune/disease limitations, driving research into synthetic and tissue-engineered substitutes.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.intervention: Geistlich Mucograft collagen matrix for recession coverage

f.funding_coi: Alpha Omega Foundation of Canada, AAID Foundation and NSERC grants; no competing interests

f.comparison: AlloDerm RTM versus Puros Dermis, Mucograft and Perioderm by number of published articles

f.population: Tnfsf11fl/fl;Dmp1-Cre mice lacking osteocyte-specific RANKL and Dmp1-Cre control mice
f.intervention: Calvarial bone disks transplanted subcutaneously or subperiosteally
outcomes: graft resorption and new bone formation
residual graft area, volume and thickness (micro-CT)
f.main_result: Control subcutaneous grafts resorbed, whereas grafts lacking osteocyte RANKL showed neither resorption nor formation; residual graft area differed between sites only in controls (p<.01 vs p=.17).
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation and ITI Foundation grants; no conflicts of interest
NIDCR (NIH) and Medical Research Foundation of Oregon grants

f.population: Human studies of soft tissue augmentation around dental implants and in partially edentulous areas
f.intervention: Apically positioned flap/vestibuloplasty with FGG, SCTG or collagen matrix; SCTG for volume
f.comparison: APF/V alone or no treatment; non-grafted sites
outcomes: papilla fill and marginal mucosal level
f.main_result: APF/V plus FGG/SCTG was the best-documented method to increase keratinized mucosa; collagen matrix gave less gain but less morbidity and surgery time.

f.population: Human liposuction adipose tissue, human adipose-derived stem cells and subcutaneous injection in an in vivo model
f.intervention: Injectable acellular adipose matrix prepared by mechanical delipidation, Tris-HCl/SDS decellularization and homogenization
f.main_result: Mechanical disruption sped delipidation; the matrix showed no cytotoxicity, supported hADSC migration and proliferation, and degraded gradually in vivo with peripheral adipogenesis at 8 weeks.
f.funding_coi: Vietnam National University HCMC grant C2019-18-20; no competing interests

f.population: Six patients with 17 mandibular Class II buccal molar furcation invasions
f.comparison: ePTFE membrane alone (7 control sites)
f.main_result: Adding DFDBA to GTR gave no significant improvement over ePTFE alone; both reduced probing depth and defect depth.
f.limitations: Small sample; examiner was not blinded

f.intervention: Direct posterior composite restoration with flowable and microhybrid composites, progressive curing for dentin, pulse curing for enamel, oblique successive cusp buildup

f.main_result: Nonvital teeth restored with composite resin or composite resin plus fiber posts resisted fatigue tests and are currently the best treatment option
Vitality loss with proper endodontic therapy affected tooth biomechanics only to a limited extent; tooth strength falls in proportion to coronal tissue loss

f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Patients 18+ years with vital molars with large-size class II cavities
f.intervention: Direct class II composite (Vit-l-escence) with stress-reducing layering and pulse/progressive curing, bonded with three etch-and-rinse adhesives
f.comparison: Three adhesives: Opti-Bond FL, Scotchbond 1 XT, PQ1
f.main_result: No failures over two years; no post-op sensitivity in any of the three adhesive groups
f.sample_size: 75 molars in 50 patients (3 groups of 25 teeth)
f.limitations: Longer observation period needed

f.population: Anterior resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses in clinical studies (1 RCT, 4 cohort studies)
f.intervention: Single-retainer cantilever RBFDPs
f.comparison: Two-retainer fixed-fixed RBFDPs
f.main_result: Cantilever RBFDPs had lower failure than two-retainer fixed-fixed RBFDPs (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.19 to 0.94, P = 0.04)
f.limitations: All included studies had high risk of bias; few RCTs

f.main_result: Conventional extension-for-prevention cavities disrupt the peripheral enamel rim and cross-bracing structures, causing compressive/tension fractures and occlusal-effect caries; minimally invasive designs are advised.
Bonded ceramic inlays with enamel margins can be expected to give about 8-10 years of service, with fracture the main failure mode.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared.

f.main_result: Immediate dentin sealing, resin coating and deep margin elevation let the dentin hybrid layer mature before composite is coupled, increasing dentin bond strength (reported +400%).

f.population: Fixed dental prostheses on natural or artificial teeth (4 in vitro studies)
f.intervention: Cementation using preheated restorative composite resin
f.comparison: Cementation using resin cement
f.main_result: Of 2109 retrieved articles, 4 in vitro studies were included; 3 found preheated composite gave greater mismatch than resin cement and 1 found improved adaptation.
f.sample_size: 4 in vitro studies from 2109 retrieved articles
f.limitations: High heterogeneity among studies precluded meta-analysis; all had medium risk of bias.

f.population: Flat occlusal dentin surfaces of human premolars
f.intervention: Resin coating (dentin bonding system Clearfil SE Bond or Single Bond with or without flowable composite Protect Liner F) before cementing indirect composite with Panavia F
f.comparison: Uncoated dentin (control) and direct composite restorations
f.main_result: Resin coating raised Panavia F bond strength to dentin (control 10.3 vs SE+PLF 27.2 MPa); direct restorations were highest (up to 42 MPa).
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in the products mentioned.

f.main_result: Proposes a protocol of adhesive base/liner (dual bonding, cavity design optimization), cervical margin relocation and controlled adhesive cementation; composites and ceramics can both be used on vital teeth.

Preparation design should be similar for all materials (sealed dentin, supragingival margins, minimum restoration thickness 1 to 1.2 mm); CAD/CAM composites and pressed lithium disilicate preferred in bruxism or weakened teeth, without long-term clinical confirmation.
f.limitations: Recommendation for severe bruxism rests on scarce in vitro research; no medium- to long-term clinical evidence.

f.population: Patients with indirect or semidirect composite inlays/onlays
f.intervention: Indirect/semidirect microhybrid or nanohybrid composite inlays and onlays placed with immediate dentin sealing, cavity design optimization and cervical margin relocation
outcomes: margins, anatomy and color quality scores
f.main_result: No clinical failure over 6 to 21 years; only minor marginal discoloration (n=4) or occlusal anatomy change due to wear (n=7), mainly with inhomogeneous nanohybrid composite.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared.
f.limitations: Retrospective evaluation with a low number of controlled restorations.

f.main_result: With adhesive dentistry and minimally invasive preparation, the traditional longevity advantage of indirect over direct posterior restorations no longer holds; guidelines for choosing direct vs indirect are given.
f.funding_coi: No proprietary, financial or personal interest declared.

f.population: Fifty-four intact extracted molars with Class II slot cavities (gingival margin on root surface)
f.intervention: Glass fiber (Ever Stick) or polyethylene (Ribbond-THM) 3 mm fiber inserts at the gingival seat of Filtek P-60 restorations, with three bonding agents
f.comparison: Same restorations without fiber inserts
f.main_result: Fiber inserts significantly reduced gingival microleakage irrespective of adhesive; Clearfil SE Bond with Filtek P-60 gave the lowest scores.

f.population: Two-dimensional finite element models of a molar with a mesial-occlusal-distal restoration, plus laboratory strain-gauge data
f.intervention: Three composites (Filtek LS, Aelite LS Posterior, Filtek Supreme) placed by three filling techniques
f.comparison: Bulk, 2.0-mm and 1.0-mm increment techniques
f.main_result: The 1.0-mm increment filling gave substantially higher stresses and strains in cervical enamel, and post-gel volumetric shrinkage was 0.11% (Filtek LS), 0.51% (Aelite LS) and 0.62% (Filtek Supreme).
f.sample_size: Nine FEA models; post-gel shrinkage n=10 per composite
f.funding_coi: Grants from CNPq and FAPEMIG; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: Extracted caries-free human premolars
f.intervention: Palatal onlay, occlusal onlay and complete veneer preparations, each with standard, thin and ultrathin pressable lithium disilicate ceramic
f.comparison: Different preparation designs and ceramic thicknesses against each other

f.population: Posterior teeth with significant loss of occlusal structure (tooth wear)
f.intervention: Occlusal veneers
f.main_result: Thicknesses of 0.7 to 1.0 mm are recommended for ceramic occlusal veneers, and load resistance exceeded 2000 N in most studies.

f.population: Partially edentulous patients requiring a single implant, placed in healed sites
f.main_result: Cumulative success rate was 91.3% for high IT and 98.2% for regular IT; marginal bone loss and recession at 3 years were greater with high IT and in the mandible.
f.funding_coi: Departmental funding, University of Pisa

f.main_result: Deep margin elevation is needed when healthy tooth is at sulcus or epithelium level; crown lengthening is needed when caries reaches connective tissue or bone crest.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest reported

f.population: Non-carious single-rooted mandibular human premolars with overflared root canals
f.comparison: The four dowel types against each other
outcomes: dye penetration (microleakage) at apical, middle and coronal sections
f.main_result: All dowels leaked considerably; the individually shaped polyethylene-reinforced dowel (Ribbond) showed the least overall leakage.

f.population: A 63-year-old woman with moderate tooth wear
f.intervention: Progressive diagnostic wax-up, transparent silicone templates and heated composite resin for direct full-mouth restoration

f.population: Extracted caries-free human third molars with large Class II MOD cavities
f.intervention: Three composites (Filtek LS, Aelite LS, Filtek Supreme) placed with bulk, eight-increment or 16-increment techniques
f.comparison: Bulk versus 8 versus 16 increments, and low-shrink versus conventional composite
f.main_result: Cuspal strain was higher with 16 increments and lower with low-shrink composites; bond and tensile strength were similar for 8 and 16 increments and higher than bulk.

f.population: Caries-free human third molars (flat dentin and Class I cavity floors)
f.intervention: Z250 composite layered horizontally, vertically, obliquely or in bulk, with or without flowable liner, bonded with three adhesives
f.comparison: Low c-factor flat surfaces versus high c-factor cavities; different layering concepts
f.main_result: Flat-surface groups had higher bond strength than cavity groups, and horizontal layers gave higher bond strength than vertical or oblique layers.

f.intervention: Nonretentive bonded lithium-disilicate partial crown with simplified preparation and adhesive luting protocol
f.main_result: The concept is reported as confirmed by high success and very low fracture and debonding rates in long-term clinical trials.
Most post systems succeed if basic principles are followed; fiber posts are the trend, while titanium, threaded, ceramic and zirconium posts are discouraged.

f.population: Adults with sufficient root canal treatment needing a restoration
f.intervention: Any type of root canal post followed by any type of restoration
f.comparison: Any type of post-free restoration
f.main_result: 10 of 14 included clinical studies showed no positive effect of post placement; an effect is possible when no cavity wall is present.

f.limitations: High-quality evidence in this field is still limited

f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: 2-D finite element model of opposing maxillary and mandibular molars
f.intervention: Working, nonworking and vertical closing micromotions loaded to 200 N
f.main_result: Vertical loading produced no harmful stress; working and nonworking micromotions gave inverted stress patterns, and enamel bridges and crests protected the crown from tensile stress.

f.population: Cylindrical specimens of a dental resin composite
f.comparison: Group cured at full intensity
outcomes: degree of conversion at top and bottom
f.main_result: Curing at less than maximum light intensity significantly reduced polymerization contraction strain without significantly affecting degree of conversion.
f.sample_size: Six samples per group, five groups
f.funding_coi: Funded in part by NIH/NIDR grant R29 DE09431

f.population: Finite element model of a molar
f.intervention: Three restoration configurations (Class I, Class II OM, Class II MOD) with composite and post-gel shrinkage model
f.main_result: Larger restorations gave lower stress in the restoration and interface but higher stress in the tooth; tooth deformation indicated tooth stress.
f.funding_coi: Minnesota Dental Research Center for Biomaterials and Biomechanics, Chulalongkorn University grant, NIH/NIDR R01-DE12225

f.population: Cylindrical specimens (d = 5 mm; h = 2 mm) of five composite resins
f.intervention: Standard (800 mW/cm2 x 60 s) vs exponential ramp photoactivation
f.main_result: Maximum shrinkage stress ranged 0.92-1.51 MPa across composites; exponential ramp reduced MSS by 3.9% and stress rate by 11%.
f.sample_size: Five specimens per material per mode

f.population: Non-carious extracted human teeth (premolars, canines, molars) sectioned bucco-lingually
f.intervention: Moire fringe mapping of in-plane strain in compressed tooth slices, plus Vickers microhardness and back-scattered electron imaging
outcomes: Vickers microhardness of enamel and dentin
f.main_result: Strain in enamel was much lower than in dentin, and a roughly 200 um zone of dentin beneath the DEJ was more strained, softer (about 50 vs 70 kg/mm2) and less mineralized than central dentin.
f.funding_coi: National Institute of Dental Research (DE06954), NIH

f.population: Structurally compromised vital and nonvital teeth (technique description)
f.intervention: Stress-reduced direct composite restorations with 'wallpapering' of cavity walls with Leno woven UHMWPE fiber ribbons
f.main_result: The authors propose that tightly adapted fiber ribbons reduce composite volume at the tooth interface, protecting residual walls from polymerization shrinkage and occlusal stress; no clinical data are reported.
f.funding_coi: Materials donated by Ribbond, Bisco and Ultradent; D. Rudo is president of Ribbond
f.limitations: Long-term clinical studies are required to confirm superiority over traditional strategies.

f.population: Extracted human mandibular molars with Class I cavities (high c-factor) or flattened dentin surfaces (low c-factor)
f.intervention: Flowable composite liner, glass fiber (everStick NET) or polyethylene fiber (Ribbond THM) under composite
f.comparison: Bulk-filled composite without liner or fiber
f.main_result: In high c-factor cavities flowable lining lowered bond strength (6.80 MPa vs 10.67 MPa bulk), everStick NET gave stable values and Ribbond THM raised it (13.80 MPa).
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Selcuk University Scientific Research Projects Center (BAP); materials supplied by manufacturers

f.population: 40 extracted sound human molars with mesial and distal Class II cavities, cervical margins above or below the CEJ
f.intervention: Flowable resin liner alone or combined with polyethylene (Ribbond) or glass (everStick NET) fiber before composite restoration
f.comparison: Bulk composite (AP-X) after SE Bond without liner or fiber
outcomes: microleakage (dye penetration score 0-4) at occlusal and gingival margins
f.main_result: Flowable resin, Ribbond or everStick NET significantly reduced occlusal leakage in cavities with enamel margins, with no difference at cervical dentin margins.
f.sample_size: 40 extracted molars (80 Class II cavities), 4 groups
f.follow_up: 7 days water storage, 300 thermocycles, 24 h dye
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Selcuk University Research Projects Council (BAP); materials donated by manufacturers

f.population: Sixty extracted human mature mandibular molars, root filled with MOD cavities in groups 2 to 5
f.intervention: Flowable composite liner, with or without leno woven polyethylene (Ribbond) fibre, under composite in root filled MOD molars
f.comparison: Intact teeth, unrestored MOD, and MOD restored with bonding system and composite alone
f.main_result: Fibre insertion raised fracture load to 943.63 N versus 733.23 N for composite alone; flowable liner had no effect (786.48 N); intact teeth reached 1676.75 N.
f.follow_up: 1 day storage at 37 C, then single compressive loading
f.funding_coi: Material support from Ribbond Inc. and Kuraray

f.intervention: Biomimetic restorative protocols: 10 stress-reducing and 8 bond-maximizing protocols, illustrated by one case
f.main_result: The authors present biomimetic restorative dentistry as combining stress-reducing and bond-maximizing protocols to increase restoration longevity, supported by 10 to 17 year old cases.

f.population: Extracted sound human premolars and third molars, ground buccal enamel surfaces
f.intervention: Two-step self-etching adhesives with MDP or Phenyl-P functional monomer in primer and/or bond (M-M, M-P, P-M, P-P)
f.comparison: Clearfil SE Bond with MDP in both primer and bond (M-M) as control
f.main_result: An acid-base resistant zone formed with every MDP-containing system but not with Phenyl-P in both (P-P); micro-shear bond strength was highest in M-M (43.08 MPa vs 33.29-36.12 MPa).
f.sample_size: 20 third molars and 30 premolars; n = 10 per group for bond strength
f.funding_coi: Chinese Government Graduate Student Overseas Study Program, GCOE Program (TMDU), JSPS grant

f.population: Experimental barium glass filled Bis-GMA/TEGDMA composite (70 wt% resin, 30 wt% filler) disk specimens
f.intervention: Irradiation for 2, 3, 6, 10 or 60 s at 450 mW/cm2 with simultaneous real-time shrinkage stress and NIR double bond conversion monitoring
f.comparison: Different irradiation times against each other (60 s as full cure)
f.main_result: 60 s irradiation gave the highest conversion (67.9%) and stress (2.9 MPa); stress relaxation occurred only before vitrification (up to about 40% at 2 s) and gave no significant benefit at clinically relevant conversion.
materials_brands: Bis-GMA/TEGDMA 70/30 experimental resin with barium glass filler (Schott)
f.funding_coi: NIH and Department of Education grant DE10959; monomers and filler donated by Esstech and Confi-Dental

f.main_result: Wet bonding, chlorhexidine, rubber dam, 'gold-standard' adhesives, sclerotic dentin roughening and bonding strategy lack RCT support for better restoration longevity, so the null hypothesis should be kept.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts declared

f.population: Extracted caries-free human third molars (occlusal deep coronal dentine), plus processed composite as a substrate
f.intervention: Six single-step adhesives bonded to hydrated dentine, dehydrated dentine or processed composite, with immediate or 20 min delayed light-activation of the overlying composite
f.comparison: Three-step adhesive All-Bond 2 as control; immediate versus delayed light-activation
f.main_result: Delayed light-activation significantly lowered bond strength of all six single-step adhesives on hydrated dentine but not of the control three-step adhesive, nor on dehydrated dentine or processed composite.
f.sample_size: 34 third molars (28 in experiment I, 4 groups of 2 teeth per adhesive subgroup); 20-23 beams per subgroup
f.funding_coi: University of Hong Kong CRC grant, CNPq (Brazil) and NIDCR DE 06427; materials supplied by Sun Medical, Tokuyama, Shofu; one author at Bisco
f.limitations: The 20 min delay is far removed from clinical practice (clinicians rarely leave composite unactivated more than 2-3 min).

f.population: 43 Class II restorations in 22 patients (mean age 30 years), mostly molars
f.intervention: Class II restorations of a fine particle hybrid composite (Tetric) placed with a decoupling incremental technique using polyurethane varnish to separate the gingival increment
f.main_result: 41 of 43 restorations were reviewed at 18 months and 31 at 3 to 4 years; none showed significant deterioration, with no secondary caries or postoperative sensitivity.
f.limitations: Single-center, practice-based explanatory study in selected patients; the authors call for a multicentered randomized controlled trial.

f.main_result: Adhesive developments and adherend modifications allow bonding to metal and porcelain with enamel-like adhesion, with tooth conservation as the main advantage.
f.funding_coi: Author owns stock in Danville Materials Inc.

f.population: Caries-free extracted human premolars (dentin)
f.intervention: Two all-in-one adhesives applied to dentin, followed by an acid-base challenge and SEM/TEM examination of the interface
f.comparison: Clearfil Tri-S Bond versus G-Bond
outcomes: acid-base resistant zone morphology and thickness (SEM, TEM)
f.main_result: An acid-base resistant zone formed beneath the hybrid layer with both adhesives, and its morphology was material dependent (about 300 nm with Clearfil Tri-S Bond versus about 100 nm with G-Bond on TEM).
f.sample_size: 12 premolars for SEM and 6 for TEM
f.funding_coi: Supported by a Global Center of Excellence program and a JSPS grant

f.population: Two clinical cases (posterior teeth with large defects)
f.intervention: First-appointment protocol for bonded indirect restorations: cavity preparation, immediate dentin sealing, impression and provisionalization
f.main_result: Describes an updated first-appointment technique for bonded indirect restorations, sealing dentin with adhesive and a thin composite layer before impression and nonluted provisional placement.

f.population: In vitro studies of universal adhesive bond strength to enamel (shear) and dentin (microtensile) in sound permanent teeth
f.intervention: Etch-and-rinse strategy (prior acid etching) with universal adhesives
f.comparison: Self-etch strategy
f.main_result: Etch-and-rinse improved enamel bond strength of universal adhesives and dentin bond strength for ultra-mild and intermediately strong ones; intermediately strong adhesives lost bond strength after aging while mild adhesives stayed stable (p < 0.05).
f.sample_size: 59 in vitro studies in the meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: Financed in part by CAPES and CNPq (Brazil)
f.limitations: Most included in vitro studies scored poorly on selective reporting and examiner blinding.

f.main_result: The review describes all generations and types of adhesive systems introduced over the last 30 years, from etch-and-rinse and self-etch to universal multi-mode adhesives.

f.population: 60 extracted impacted molars (wisdom teeth) with large occlusal-proximal cavities
f.intervention: Whole-ceramic inlays restored with the biomimetic adhesive method (bio-base of immediate dentin sealing and fluid composite)
f.comparison: Classical method of ceramic inlay restoration; also Variolink Esthetic DC versus Maxcem Elite cement
outcomes: integrity and quality of cementing material
f.main_result: The biomimetic method gave superior layer integrity; defects (microfissures, detached cement fragments) were about 2 times larger with the classical method, and Maxcem Elite showed discontinuities at the cement-inlay interface.

f.population: Partially demineralized collagen matrices prepared from human dentin
f.intervention: Storage of acid-etched demineralized dentin matrices in artificial saliva for 24 hrs, 90 and 250 days
f.comparison: Artificial saliva with proteolytic enzyme inhibitors, or pure mineral oil
f.main_result: Matrices were almost completely destroyed after 250 days in artificial saliva but not with enzyme inhibitors or mineral oil; dentin powder collagenolytic activity was inhibited 73% by protease inhibitors and to near zero by 0.2% chlorhexidine.
f.sample_size: 8 per assay condition for the collagenolytic assay
f.funding_coi: Supported by NIDCR grants and the Faculty of Dentistry, University of Hong Kong

f.population: Composite cylinders (in vitro specimens) of a microfilled hybrid resin
f.intervention: Surface treatments (air abrasion, HCl/HF etching, diamond bur roughening with or without phosphoric acid) before repair with Prime & Bond NT, with the adhesive cured in air or under nitrogen
f.comparison: Different surface treatments against each other, and air versus nitrogen curing of the adhesive
f.main_result: Air abrasion gave the highest bond strength (43.2 MPa in air, 42.4 MPa in nitrogen) while the other treatments were comparable (about 33 to 38 MPa); curing atmosphere had no significant effect.

f.population: Teeth with dentinogenesis imperfecta or dentine dysplasia (37 in vitro studies, 164 teeth)
f.intervention: Systematic review of enamel, dentine-enamel junction and dentine microstructure and properties in dentine disorders
f.comparison: Normal (unaffected) tissue where available; DI versus OI compared by Mann-Whitney U test
f.main_result: Dentine and the dentine-enamel junction are damaged in dentinogenesis imperfecta and osteogenesis imperfecta, and enamel is affected in dentinogenesis imperfecta (p = 0.0013) but not in osteogenesis imperfecta (p = 0.056).
f.funding_coi: No competing interests declared
f.limitations: The recommendations are mostly based on in vitro studies, with very few comparison samples and no blinded testing.

f.main_result: Adhesive systems allow safe bonding of composite to enamel and dentin and more conservative cavities, but technique and ideal bonding conditions remain essential.
f.funding_coi: No financial support and no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Success of adhesive materials in vitro should be supported by clinical follow-up of long-term durability.

f.population: Published dentin bond strength data for six adhesives (147 references)
f.intervention: Literature search pooling dentin bond strength data from shear, microshear, tensile and microtensile tests
f.comparison: The four test methods compared with each other
f.main_result: Bond strength data remain highly scattered whichever adhesive or test is used (coefficients of variation 20-50% even for microtensile), and product ranking depends on the test.

f.population: Dentin surfaces of extracted human third molars
f.intervention: Two-step self-etch adhesives (Clearfil SE Bond, FL-Bond, FL-Bond II) bonded to flat dentin, then acid-base challenge
f.comparison: Fluoride-free Clearfil SE Bond versus fluoride-releasing FL-Bond and FL-Bond II
f.main_result: Clearfil SE Bond had higher microtensile bond strength (46.3 MPa) than FL-Bond (31.3 MPa) and FL-Bond II (34.2 MPa), and an acid-base resistant zone formed in all groups but depended on the material.
f.sample_size: 15 human third molars, 20 specimens per adhesive

f.population: Three-dimensional finite element models of cervical dentine and 12 extracted single-rooted teeth (dentine slabs)
f.intervention: Finite element simulation with or without hydrostatic pressure and elastic modulus gradient, compression testing and FTIR of hydrated dentine
f.comparison: Hydrated versus partially dehydrated dentine; models with versus without hydrostatic pressure
outcomes: principal and von Mises stresses and strains
f.main_result: Partially dehydrated dentine fractured at higher stress (157.8 vs 53.1 MPa, p = 0.014) while hydrated dentine tolerated higher strain at fracture (9.6 vs 3.7%, p = 0.037).

f.population: Bovine incisor crowns, sound or artificially demineralized, with standardized Class V cavities
f.intervention: Selective enamel etching with phosphoric acid for 10, 30, 60 or 120 s before a one-step or two-step self-etch adhesive and composite restoration
f.comparison: Non-etched groups and sound versus demineralized enamel; iBond Self Etch versus Clearfil SE Bond
outcomes: percentage of continuous margins (%CM) on SEM
f.main_result: Phosphoric acid etching significantly increased the percentage of continuous margins in both demineralized and sound enamel, and pre-etched demineralized enamel reached similar margin integrity to sound etched enamel.
f.sample_size: 140 bovine incisor crowns in 14 groups of 10
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: 48 endodontically treated human upper molars
f.intervention: Adhesive overlay or full crown preparation restored with high translucency zirconia or zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate, cemented and fatigue-loaded
f.comparison: Low-retentive overlay versus high-retentive crown design; HTZ versus ZLS
outcomes: three-dimensional external gap progression by micro-CT
f.main_result: External gap progression was lower for the full crown design than the overlay (p < 0.01) and lower for ZLS than HTZ (p < 0.01), the largest value being HTZ overlays (0.16 mm3).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; open access funding by Projekt DEAL
f.limitations: Quantitative gap thresholding was harder in HTZ because of X-ray scatter artifacts.

f.main_result: Resin-dentin bond degradation involves hydrolysis of resin and collagen plus host proteases, and inhibiting collagenolytic activity or cross-linking collagen are the two main strategies to protect the hybrid layer.

f.population: 2,157 dentin bond-strength tests extracted from 298 papers
f.intervention: Systematic collection of dentin bond-strength data for current adhesive classes and neural-network modelling of influencing variables
outcomes: effect of adhesive class, aging, storage time and research group
f.main_result: Research group and adhesive brand were the most determining variables for dentin bond strength; the mean best adhesive was almost twice the least-performing one, and bond strength decreased with water storage.
f.funding_coi: K.U. Leuven Research Grant; authors declare no conflicts of interest

f.population: Extracted human molars with coronal dentine caries (caries-affected vs normal dentine)
f.intervention: Bonding with 2 total-etch and 2 self-etch adhesives, microtensile testing, DIAGNOdent laser fluorescence and Knoop microhardness of the substrate
f.comparison: Normal dentine; total-etch vs self-etch adhesives
f.main_result: All adhesives bonded better to normal than caries-affected dentine (e.g. Prime & Bond NT 56.3 vs 41.3 MPa), significant only for Prime & Bond NT and Clearfil SE Bond; total-etch adhesives outperformed self-etch ones.
f.sample_size: 16 molars, 4 per adhesive, about 10 slabs per group
f.funding_coi: NIDCR grant DEO14911 and CICYT (Spain) grant

f.population: Two functional monomers (4-META, MDP) with atelocollagen as a triple-helical peptide model
f.intervention: Saturation transfer difference NMR spectroscopy of monomer-collagen binding
f.comparison: 4-META versus MDP
outcomes: STD NMR signal intensities per proton
f.main_result: MDP showed high STD intensities in its aliphatic protons (73.9% to 100%), indicating stable hydrophobic interaction with collagen, while 4-META showed no intense STD signals.
f.funding_coi: GCOE program and JSPS grant; no conflicts of interest declared

f.main_result: Self-etch adhesives are promising because they are easy to use, bond chemically to tooth structure and maintain dentin hydroxyapatite, which supports bond durability.

f.population: Simulated restorations: composite cylinders between silane-coated steel disks of 5, 10 or 15 mm
f.intervention: Continuous recording of setting (shrinkage) stress of chemically initiated composites at varying configuration factor C
f.comparison: Various configuration factors C and sample volumes
f.main_result: In most clinically relevant cavity configurations the stress-relieving flow is not sufficient to preserve adhesion to dentin by dentin-bonding agents.
f.sample_size: each experiment repeated at least three times

f.population: Extracted human molars (108) bonded by 12 operators of differing bonding experience
f.intervention: Bonding to enamel and dentin with one 4th-generation and two 7th-generation adhesives, then shear testing
f.comparison: 4th-generation versus 7th-generation adhesives; inexperienced, resident and experienced operators
outcomes: shear bond strength to enamel and dentin
f.main_result: The 4th-generation adhesive performed better than the 7th-generation adhesives even with inexperienced operators; dentin bonds (14.0 MPa) were stronger than enamel bonds (11.9 MPa).
f.funding_coi: Supported by Heraeus Kulzer

f.population: Bovine dentin samples and Class V cavities in bovine teeth
f.intervention: Measuring composite-dentin bond strength over time against developing polymerization contraction stress, in linear and 3-D models
f.comparison: Linear (tensilometer) versus three-dimensional (Class V cavity) model
f.main_result: In the linear model the bond survived contraction stress through flow relaxation, whereas in 3-D Class V cavities flow is limited and contraction stress can exceed bond strength, disrupting the bond.
f.sample_size: 24 Class V cavities (12 per composite); 5 repeats per linear experiment

f.population: 27-year-old woman needing replacement of amalgam fillings in two mandibular molars; 34 restorations in preliminary evaluation
f.intervention: Dual bonding technique: dentin bonding agent applied after preparation and again at final luting
f.main_result: Dual application of the dentin bonding agent considerably increased bond strength values.

f.population: Human dentin disk sandwiches with resin composite from extracted caries-free third molars
f.intervention: Acid-base challenge of two-step self-etch adhesive interfaces after long-term water storage, with SEM
f.comparison: Clearfil SE Bond (fluoride-free) versus Clearfil Protect Bond (fluoride-releasing)
f.main_result: Outer lesion depth rose from about 10 μm to about 30 μm after 6 months; an ABRZ persisted in both adhesives and was thicker and more stable with the fluoride-releasing Protect Bond.
f.funding_coi: Global Center of Excellence Program and JSPS grant

f.population: Box-shaped cavities in bovine root dentin
f.intervention: Restoration with four adhesive/restorative combinations followed by acid-base challenge (demineralizing solution then 5% NaOCl) and SEM
f.comparison: Four adhesive/restorative combinations compared with each other
f.main_result: Self-etch systems SE and ABF showed a thin acid-base resistant zone under 1 μm beneath the hybrid layer, the fluoride-releasing RB/RP showed a thick acid-resistant zone but a partly degraded bonding resin, and the Single Bond hybrid layer was partly degraded.
f.funding_coi: Center of Excellence Program grant (Tokyo Medical and Dental University)
f.limitations: Further studies simulating the oral environment are necessary

f.funding_coi: JSPS KAKENHI grants

f.population: Extracted human premolars with large class II MOD cavities
f.intervention: Class II composite restorations with etch-and-rinse or self-etch adhesives, total or selective bonding, with or without a flowable composite layer
f.comparison: Total bonding technique versus selective bonding; with versus without flowable liner
f.main_result: Selective bonding gave lower cuspal movement than total bonding for all adhesives, and a flowable liner had no influence.
f.limitations: Results should be confirmed by long-term clinical evaluations.

f.population: Primary and young permanent teeth with dentin caries in children
f.intervention: Caries Check (acid red in polypropylene glycol), stained dentin completely removed
f.comparison: Caries Detector (acid red in propylene glycol), pink-stained dentin retained
f.main_result: DIAGNOdent readings after removal were higher with Caries Check than Caries Detector in permanent teeth, with no significant difference in primary teeth.
f.funding_coi: Products donated by Nippon Shika Yakuhin KK

f.population: EDTA-demineralized bovine dentin collagen powder
f.intervention: Treatment with lactic acid at 0.001 to 1 M for 1, 5 or 24 h, then staining with 1.0% acid red in propylene glycol
f.comparison: Untreated dentin powder and intact demineralized collagen controls
f.main_result: Collagen stained only after lactic acid at 0.01 M (pH 3) or higher; 0.001 M and controls stayed unstained.

f.intervention: Differentiated approaches for adhesive restorations with subgingival cervical margins: coronal relocation of the margin, surgical exposure of the margin, or clinical crown lengthening with immediate, early or delayed impression
f.main_result: A two-parameter classification (isolation with dental dam, biologic width) defines three clinical situations with three therapeutic approaches; the combined surgical-restorative approach allows cementation after only 1 week.
f.follow_up: 1 year recall in the illustrated case

f.population: Adult patients with non-carious cervical lesions restored with composite and adhesive systems (randomized trials)
f.intervention: Adhesive strategies: 3-step etch-and-rinse (3ER), 2-step etch-and-rinse (2ER), 2-step self-etch (2SE), 1-step self-etch (1SE)
f.comparison: Different adhesive strategies against each other
outcomes: loss of retention at 12-24, 36-48 and >48 months
f.main_result: No significant differences between any two adhesive strategies except 2ER vs 3ER at the shortest follow-up; 2SE ranked highest but only slightly.
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by CNPq and CAPES; no competing interests declared
f.limitations: Conclusions were based mostly on studies of unclear risk of bias.

f.population: Seven in vitro studies and 5 clinical reports on cervical margin relocation
f.intervention: Cervical margin relocation (deep margin elevation) before adhesive cementation of indirect restorations
f.comparison: Conventional luting directly on dentin
outcomes: bond strength to proximal box floor
f.main_result: No strong scientific evidence supports or discourages CMR; no randomized or prospective/retrospective clinical studies exist, and most in vitro studies found no difference in marginal quality versus conventional luting.
f.sample_size: 7 in vitro studies and 5 clinical reports
f.limitations: No randomized controlled clinical trials or prospective or retrospective clinical studies on CMR could be found.

f.population: 29 subjects with a single tooth requiring subgingival restoration
f.intervention: Deep margin elevation with composite resin, followed by histological evaluation of gingival tissue adjacent to the composite
f.comparison: Gingival tissue adjacent to the natural root surface of the same tooth
f.main_result: Gingival inflammation next to subgingival composite did not differ from that next to natural root surface (3.83 vs 3.71, P=0.36), with plaque, bleeding and probing depth decreasing at 3 months.

f.population: 120 patients with 197 partial indirect restorations (143 molars, 54 premolars) with deep margin elevation
f.intervention: Partial indirect restorations (lithium disilicate or indirect composite) combined with deep margin elevation using resin composite
f.comparison: Subsets by baseline variables (composite vs ceramic, vital vs non-vital, good vs poor DME profile)
f.main_result: Overall cumulative survival was 95.9% (SE 2.9%) up to 12 years with 8 absolute failures; composite restorations degraded more, ceramic caused more antagonist wear.
f.funding_coi: Granted by the University Medical Center Groningen; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Longer follow-up is needed as degradation of the restorations is seen over time.

f.intervention: Adhesive cementation protocol with immediate dentin sealing, flexible base lining, soft light-curing provisionals and highly filled viscous luting composites
f.comparison: Classical approach (adhesive applied at cementation, conventional glass-ionomer base, low-viscosity dual-cure cements)
f.main_result: Immediate dentin sealing with a flexible base lining and highly filled luting composites improves the safety and predictability of luting tooth-colored posterior restorations, reducing postoperative sensitivity and cement-excess problems.

f.intervention: Dental dam (rubber dam) application procedures
f.funding_coi: Published by Coltène/Whaledent, Inc.

f.intervention: Deep margin elevation: modified Tofflemire matrix, immediate dentin sealing and a direct bonded composite base raising the deep margin to a supragingival position
f.comparison: Surgical crown lengthening
f.main_result: Deep margin elevation is proposed as a useful noninvasive alternative to surgical crown lengthening; more research is needed to validate it.
f.limitations: More research is needed to validate the technique.

f.population: Literature on periodontal response to deep margin elevation, plus three illustrative clinical cases
f.intervention: Deep margin elevation instead of crown lengthening for deep cavities
f.comparison: Surgical crown lengthening
f.main_result: DME appears well tolerated by the periodontium with good bonding and isolation; histologically no connective attachment forms on the material, giving a long junctional epithelium and a slight connective attachment on dentin below it.
f.limitations: Further clinical and histologic studies are needed to confirm the conclusion.

f.population: Four all-in-one self-etching adhesives tested on extracted human incisors/molars (enamel, dentin) and cylindrical dentin cavities
f.intervention: Light curing of the adhesives under nitrogen atmosphere
f.comparison: Light curing under ambient air
outcomes: shear bond strength to enamel and dentin
f.main_result: Inhibition layer under air ranged from 4 um (iBond) to 23 um (One-Up Bond F II) and vanished under nitrogen; enamel SBS was unaffected and dentin SBS was higher under nitrogen (p=0.013).
f.sample_size: 3 disks per adhesive for inhibition depth; n = 8 per group for SBS and marginal adaptation

f.population: Thirty noncarious human third molars (hemi-teeth with thick or thin smear layer on flat dentin)
f.intervention: Three self-etching adhesives of different acidity applied to dentin with thick (60-grit) or thin (600-grit) smear layer
f.comparison: Etch-and-rinse controls Single Bond and ScotchBond Multi-Purpose Plus
outcomes: buffering capacity and pH of primers
f.main_result: Smear layer thickness did not affect microtensile bond strength but thick smear layers increased gap width; bond strength depended only on the adhesive, with Tyrian lowest; pH correlated with gap width (R=0.99).
f.sample_size: 30 molars, 6 hemi-teeth per adhesive per smear layer thickness
materials_brands: Tyrian Self Priming Etchant + One Step Plus
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by CAPES and CNPq grants

f.population: 40 extracted human third molars with standardized MOD preparations (mesial box 2 mm below the CEJ)
f.intervention: Cervical margin relocation with a 2-mm layer of conventional or flowable composite before CAD/CAM crowns of pre-cured resin or lithium disilicate
f.comparison: Distal face of the same tooth without CMR
outcomes: marginal quality by SEM of epoxy replicas before and after thermomechanical loading
f.main_result: No significant difference in marginal quality with or without CMR, before or after thermomechanical cycling (p > 0.05).
f.funding_coi: Grants from MIUR (Italy)
f.limitations: Further in vivo studies are needed to validate the technique.

f.population: Fifteen freshly extracted human molars in 3 groups of 5 (flat midcoronal dentin)
f.intervention: Immediate dentin sealing with OptiBond FL immediately after preparation, before impression
f.comparison: Delayed dentin sealing (indirect) and a direct immediate bonding control
f.main_result: Microtensile bond strength of control (55.06 MPa) and IDS (58.25 MPa) did not differ, while DDS was much lower (11.58 MPa, P=.0081).
f.sample_size: 15 molars, 3 groups of 5 teeth, 11 beams per tooth

f.population: Fifty freshly extracted human molars divided into 10 groups
f.intervention: Immediate dentin sealing with Optibond FL or SE Bond, with provisional restorations for 2, 7 or 12 weeks before overlay placement
f.comparison: Direct bonding control and delayed dentin sealing for each adhesive
f.main_result: Control and all IDS groups did not differ and exceeded 45 MPa for both adhesives, whereas delayed dentin sealing groups had lower bond strength (P<.001).
f.follow_up: Restoration placement after 2, 7 or 12 weeks; testing 24 h after restoration
f.funding_coi: Materials provided by 3M ESPE, Kerr and Kuraray

f.population: 40 human molars with Class II MOD cavities, margins in enamel or 2 mm below the CEJ
f.intervention: Proximal margin elevation with composite (one 3 mm or two 1.5 mm layers of Tetric) before adhesive insertion of Cerec ceramic inlays
f.comparison: Enamel-margin positive control and untreated dentin-margin negative control
outcomes: percentage of continuous margin by SEM before and after thermomechanical loading
f.main_result: After loading, margin elevation groups did not differ from the untreated dentin-margin group; only the enamel interface of group EN (90.0%) was better than DE-2In (83.2%).

f.population: 35 patients (aged 27-54) needing one posterior partial crown, with margins below the CEJ
f.intervention: Cervical margin relocation (G-Premio Bond and universal flow composite) in one interproximal box before pressed lithium disilicate crowns
f.comparison: Shoulder preparation
f.main_result: At 12 months CMR sites had more bleeding on probing than shoulder preparation (53% vs 31.5%), with GI and PI not different.
f.limitations: Within the limitations of this study, higher incidence of BoP can be expected around CMR margins and in coincidence with deep margins.

f.population: 20 extracted human third molars with MOD cavities, proximal margins 1 mm below the CEJ
f.intervention: Mesial margin elevation with flowable composite, then CAD/CAM composite overlays luted with a universal adhesive (selective etch) or three-step total-etch adhesive
f.comparison: Non-elevated distal margins in the same teeth; universal vs three-step adhesive
outcomes: microleakage score at mesial and distal interfaces
f.main_result: With the universal adhesive CMR sites leaked more than non-CMR sites, with the three-step adhesive no difference; non-CMR sites leaked less with the universal adhesive.
f.funding_coi: Materials provided by GC Europe; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: More in vitro and in vivo research, especially randomized clinical trials, is needed to validate CMR.

f.population: Technique demonstrated on a Typodont mesio-occlusal inlay preparation with a localized subgingival margin
f.intervention: Matrix-in-a-matrix deep margin elevation: sectional band inside a circumferential matrix with Teflon tape packed between
f.main_result: A modified matrix technique is described to isolate and adapt a subgingival matrix for deep margin elevation, potentially avoiding resective surgery or extraction.

f.population: 39 extracted human molars with MOD cavities, mesial margins 1 mm below the CEJ
f.intervention: Mesial cervical margin relocation with a hybrid composite (Essentia) or flowable composite (G-ænial Universal Flo), then adhesively cemented composite CAD/CAM MOD overlays
f.comparison: No CMR (control)
outcomes: interfacial leakage by silver nitrate penetration depth
f.main_result: Dentin-interface leakage was higher in both CMR groups (mean 2.40 and 2.04) than control (1.18), and higher at dentin than enamel interfaces.
f.funding_coi: Materials provided by GC Europe; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 14 extracted human molars with MOD cavities, proximal margins about 1 mm below the CEJ
f.intervention: Mesial CMR with total-etch adhesive and flowable composite (Group 1) or universal adhesive and bulk-fill flowable composite (Group 2), then CAD/CAM overlays
f.comparison: Non-elevated distal margins
outcomes: marginal integrity by SEM of replicas
f.main_result: Microleakage and SEM marginal integrity were not correlated; CMR margins leaked more than non-CMR margins and Group 2 leaked less than Group 1.

f.population: Canine teeth of five dogs with surgically created buccal bone defects and root cavities
f.intervention: Class V root cavities restored with composite resin or resin-modified glass ionomer cement and covered by a flap
f.comparison: Unrestored cavities as control
f.main_result: Both materials allowed apical epithelial migration and had markedly shorter connective tissue attachment than control (0.52 and 0.37 mm vs 2.22 mm).

f.population: Bar specimens of five ceramic and five resin composite materials
f.intervention: 4-point bending initial strength and staircase cyclic fatigue (10^4 cycles, 0.5 Hz) in water
f.comparison: Ceramics versus resin composites
f.main_result: Zirconia had the highest initial and fatigue strength (768 and 440 MPa); e.max Press and Clearfil Majesty Posterior lost least strength (29.6% and 32%).
f.sample_size: 15 specimens per material for initial strength; 25 for fatigue
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.intervention: Adhesive cementation protocols for hybrid ceramics and CAD/CAM composite resins
f.main_result: Hybrid ceramics should be etched with HF acid plus silane; CAD/CAM composites air-abraded with a universal bonding agent; all luted adhesively with light- or dual-cured resin cement.
f.limitations: Clinical studies are needed on long-term bonding behavior and survival

f.population: Blocks of six CAD/CAM materials (four ceramics, one hybrid ceramic, one composite)
f.intervention: Mechanical and chemical surface treatments before luting with two dual-curing luting composites
f.comparison: Untreated control surfaces and the two cements
f.main_result: Bond strength of six CAD/CAM materials was significantly influenced by surface treatment (p < 0.05); HF+S gave the highest bond for e.max CAD and Vita Enamic.
f.funding_coi: Companies donated materials
f.limitations: The effect of aging needs to be examined in depth

f.population: A 36-year-old woman with severe dental erosion due to gastroesophageal reflux disease
f.intervention: Full-coverage crowns 0.5-1.5 mm thick milled from VITA ENAMIC, adhesively cemented without preparation
f.main_result: At half a year and one year the crowns were still intact and soft tissues appeared healthy.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: No information on durability regarding cervical areas or discolorations; limited shade range

f.population: Laboratory-fabricated nacre-like alumina/polymer composites (ceramic fractions 70-76%)
f.intervention: Bi-directional freeze-casting, sintering, silanisation and UDMA/TEGDMA infiltration of alumina scaffolds
f.comparison: Commercial CAD/CAM composite Vita Enamic
f.main_result: The composites had flexural strength 135.08-172.65 MPa and fracture toughness 2.54-3.19 MPa.m1/2, all superior to Vita Enamic.
f.limitations: Further work is needed to improve physical and mechanical properties and esthetics

f.population: Beams (2 x 2 x 25 mm) of two composite resins, direct and indirect
f.intervention: Pre-tensioned unidirectional glass fiber bundles embedded in the composite
f.comparison: Non-tensioned glass fibers and unreinforced composite
f.main_result: Pre-tensioned fibers raised flexural strength to about 568 MPa in both composites, versus 425-443 MPa with non-tensioned fibers and 81-132 MPa unreinforced.

f.population: Resin composite molds (4 mm deep) and cavities in 24 extracted human mandibular molars
f.intervention: Plasma-treated polyethylene fiber (Ribbond Ultra) increment at the cavity floor under SDR bulk-fill
f.comparison: Bulk placement (BLK), two-increment placement (INC) and an unbonded bulk-filled control
f.main_result: MTBS was 13.8, 31.7 and 28.3 MPa for BLK, INC and FRC; FRC and INC did not differ and both exceeded BLK.
f.sample_size: 24 molars for MTBS; n = 12 molds per group for gap volume

f.population: an endodontically treated posterior tooth (case report)
f.intervention: fiber-reinforced composite (FRC) layer incorporated into the resin coating of the tooth preparation before the final impression
f.main_result: The technique may reduce the risk of catastrophic fractures and improve the success rate of endocrowns on nonvital teeth (no quantitative results)
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial or other interest in any product

f.population: 50 sound extracted human maxillary central incisors with window veneer preparations
f.intervention: Li2Si2O5 (e.max Press) laminate veneers bonded after immediate dentin sealing (IDS) of exposed dentin
f.comparison: delayed dentin sealing (DDS) after 2 weeks, and an enamel-only control group
f.main_result: Mean fracture strength was highest with complete dentin exposure sealed by IDS (576 N) and lowest with complete dentin exposure sealed by DDS (314 N); the overall ANOVA was p = 0.072
f.funding_coi: Materials provided by Ivoclar Vivadent and Kerr

f.population: indirect restorations (in vitro bond strength to human dentin)
f.intervention: immediate dentin sealing (IDS)
f.comparison: delayed dentin sealing (DDS)
outcomes: bond strength to dentin (immediate and long-term)
f.main_result: The in vitro evidence suggests IDS improves the bond strength of dentin to resin-based restorations regardless of adhesive strategy
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 88 articles on the IDS technique, in vitro and clinical studies on human permanent teeth
f.intervention: immediate dentin sealing (IDS) for indirect restorations
f.main_result: IDS seems advantageous for bond strength, gap formation, bacterial microleakage and dentin hypersensitivity
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

f.population: teeth prepared for indirect bonded restorations
f.intervention: immediate dentin sealing (IDS) with a dentin bonding agent before impression making
f.comparison: delayed dentin sealing (DDS)
f.main_result: IDS appears to achieve improved bond strength, fewer gap formations, decreased bacterial leakage and reduced post-cementation sensitivity
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest
f.limitations: more research is required in this field

f.population: extracted third molars with fully developed apices, standard Class II MO cavities
f.intervention: immediate endodontic sealing (IES) of the access cavity before endodontic irrigation
f.comparison: delayed endodontic sealing (DES) after irrigation
outcomes: internal adaptation (percentage of continuous margin, SEM)
f.main_result: IES gave significantly greater internal adaptation than DES (p = 0.000); composite viscosity had no significant effect
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: 104 patients (mean age 42.1 years) receiving 384 feldspathic ceramic laminate veneers on maxillary anterior teeth
f.intervention: laminate veneers with immediate dentin sealing (IDS) when more than 50% of dentin was exposed
f.comparison: veneers on teeth with more than 50% dentin exposure sealed without IDS
f.main_result: In teeth with more than 50% dentin exposure, veneer survival was 96.4% with IDS versus 81.8% without (P = 0.017); overall survival was 95% over 11 years

f.population: deep carious lesions approaching the pulp (23 relevant human studies)
f.intervention: partial caries removal or stepwise excavation
f.comparison: complete removal of infected tissue
f.main_result: There is substantial evidence that removing all infected dentin in deep carious lesions is not required for successful treatment, provided the restoration seals the lesion
f.sample_size: 1,059 reports screened, 23 relevant, 3 randomized controlled trials
f.funding_coi: No disclosures; NIDCR grant support acknowledged
f.limitations: additional clinical trials may be needed

f.population: 60 decoronated endodontically treated bovine incisors without a ferrule
f.intervention: glass-ceramic crowns bonded to composite resin foundation restorations with glass-fiber or titanium posts
f.comparison: two previously published groups (2 mm ferrule with fiber post; no ferrule with fiber post)
f.main_result: No post-and-core foundation matched the ferrule group (72 667 cycles); fiber post with bulk-fill core outperformed titanium post groups
f.sample_size: 60 bovine incisors in 4 groups plus 2 comparison groups
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by CAPES Foundation Brazil; materials provided by several manufacturers

f.population: extracted human third molars ground flat to expose middle coronal dentin
f.intervention: 50 µm aluminum oxide air abrasion of dentin before applying Clearfil SE Bond or One-Up Bond F
f.comparison: no air abrasion
outcomes: microtensile bond strength at 1 day, 3 and 6 months
f.main_result: Air abrasion improved Clearfil SE Bond bond strength at three months; the two adhesives did not differ and bond strengths decreased over time
f.follow_up: 1 day, 3 and 6 months of water storage

f.population: Two commercial CAD/CAM composites (Shofu HC Hard, Cerasmart 300) as bar and plate specimens
f.intervention: Alumina air-abrasion (50 um Al2O3) of the composite surface, with or without silanization and resin-cement bonding, tested by three-point bending and shear bond strength
f.comparison: Specimens without air-abrasion
outcomes: shear bond strength to resin cement
f.main_result: Air-abrasion significantly lowered flexural strength of single-bar specimens, did not change it in bonded-double-bar specimens, and significantly increased shear bond strength to resin cement.
f.funding_coi: JSPS KAKENHI grant; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 32 bovine molar and premolar dentin bars (2 x 2 x 8 mm)
f.intervention: Sandblasting dentin with 50 um aluminum oxide before etching, adhesive and composite
f.comparison: Control bars with no sandblasting
f.main_result: Sandblasted dentin gave higher tensile stress at maximum load (84.3 vs 35.1 MPa, p = 0.033) and fracture strength (18.5 vs 8.2 MPa, p = 0.008) than control.

f.population: 30 patients needing a single implant at a premolar or first molar site, allocated to thin (n = 14) or thick (n = 16) vertical mucosal phenotype
f.intervention: Tissue level implants with a partially smooth collar
f.comparison: Thick (> 2 mm) versus thin (<= 2 mm) vertical mucosa
outcomes: clinical parameters (probing depth, recession, keratinized mucosa width, BOP, plaque, gingival index)
f.main_result: No significant differences between thin and thick vertical mucosa for any clinical parameter or radiographic marginal bone level at one year; 100% implant survival.
f.funding_coi: Osseointegration Foundation grant; implants donated by BioHorizons; one author receives BioHorizons speaker honoraria

f.population: Patients with, or at risk for, MRONJ
f.intervention: MRONJ prevention measures and stage-based management strategies
f.main_result: The committee recommends renaming BRONJ as MRONJ and redefines the case definition (exposed bone for more than eight weeks in patients on antiresorptive or antiangiogenic agents without jaw radiation).

f.population: Patients with, or at risk for, MRONJ
f.intervention: Updated risk estimates, diagnosis and management algorithms for MRONJ
f.main_result: AAOMS maintains the existing MRONJ staging system (including Stage 0) while updating risk, diagnosis and management guidance.
f.funding_coi: Authors disclose consultancies and research grants (Amgen, AAOMS, OMS Foundation and others)

f.intervention: Thione/thiol primers and 4-META/MMA-TBB resin for bonding Ag-Pd-Cu-Au alloy restorations and fixed partial dentures
f.main_result: Clinical performance of Ag-Pd-Cu-Au alloy restorations and FPDs is overall excellent when seated with current noble metal bonding systems.
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by JSPS Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research

f.intervention: Selective and stepwise carious tissue removal with restorative materials over residual carious dentin
f.main_result: Carious dentin can be left under provisional or permanent restoration without risk of caries progression.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.population: In vitro studies of etched and silanized glass ceramics bonded to resin-based materials
f.intervention: Adhesive layer application after HF etching and silanization
f.comparison: Same silane without an adhesive layer
f.main_result: Adhesive layer application did not improve bond strength; shear studies showed no significant difference and microtensile studies showed higher values without adhesive.

f.population: 14 caries-free extracted human upper first premolars
f.intervention: Seventh-generation bonding agent (iBond)
f.comparison: Sixth-generation bonding agent (Adper Prompt L-Pop)
outcomes: penetration depth of bonding resin into dentinal tubules (SEM)
f.main_result: Seventh-generation adhesive penetrated deeper into dentinal tubules than sixth-generation (12.451 vs 9.471 um, p = 0.032).

f.intervention: Contemporary adhesive strategies (etch-and-rinse, self-etch, universal) and the dynamic tooth-adhesive interface
f.main_result: Adhesive interfaces are susceptible to biodegradation by biofilm, bacterial enzymes and activated endogenous enzymes, so adhesive choice and technique affect longevity.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.population: In vitro studies of bond strength to human primary and permanent tooth enamel and dentin
f.intervention: Adhesive bonding to primary teeth
f.comparison: Bonding to permanent teeth
f.main_result: Permanent teeth showed higher bond strength than primary teeth overall (p = 0.0005) and for dentin (p = 0.002), but not for enamel (p = 0.11); most studies had high bias risk.
f.funding_coi: CAPES financial support and scholarship
f.limitations: The majority of the studies had a high bias risk.

f.intervention: Universal bonding agents used in total-etch, self-etch or selective enamel-etch modes
f.main_result: Laboratory and initial clinical studies suggest universal bonding agents are a promising step in bonding to tooth substance.

f.population: CAD-CAM ceramic blocks (2 zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate, lithium disilicate, leucite-based, Y-TZP) bonded to composite resin; in vitro microbars
f.intervention: Six surface treatments (control, universal adhesive, HF, CoJet, HF+Uni, CoJet+Uni), tested with and without 100 000 thermal cycles
f.comparison: Untreated control group
f.main_result: ZLS bonded similarly to lithium disilicate and leucite ceramics and more durably than zirconia after thermocycling; HF plus universal adhesive was the most effective treatment for ZLS.
f.sample_size: n=15 microbars per group (5 ceramics, 6 treatments, with or without thermocycling)
f.follow_up: 100 000 thermal cycles, equivalent to about 10 years of oral aging
f.funding_coi: Guangdong and National Natural Science Foundation of China grants

f.population: Bovine incisor enamel and dentin, resin composite and feldspathic porcelain specimens
f.intervention: Scotchbond Universal in etch-and-rinse and self-etch modes
f.comparison: Scotchbond Multipurpose, Single Bond 2, Clearfil SE Bond; silane + SB and no-treatment controls on composite and porcelain
f.main_result: The universal adhesive was comparable to the other adhesives tested, with performance depending on the substrate.
f.funding_coi: Composite resin donated by FGM; authors declare competing interests

f.intervention: Self-adhesive resin cements for luting and bonding restorations
f.main_result: Self-adhesive resin cements are easy to use and perform similarly to conventional cements in early short-term studies, but clinical evidence is insufficient for robust conclusions.
f.funding_coi: UBC Start-Up grants

f.population: Six commercial universal adhesives tested on films and on dentin from extracted sound human third molars
f.intervention: Evaluation of degree of conversion, oxygen inhibition, hardness, dentin demineralisation and self-etch shear bond strength of six universal adhesives
outcomes: dentin demineralisation and insoluble salt formation
f.main_result: Although all six adhesives were 10-MDP based, they differed in film properties, dentin reactivity and bonding; G-Premio Bond had the lowest degree of conversion (67.2%) and shear bond strength.

f.population: Caries-affected dentin as a bonding substrate
f.main_result: Caries-affected dentin gives lower bond strength and a poorer hybrid layer than normal dentin, which can compromise restoration longevity.
Composite restorations last about 10 years or less on average, failing mainly from secondary caries and fracture.
The relationship between the cement used and crown survival is not well understood.
f.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose

f.population: 19 in vitro studies on repair of direct methacrylate-based resin composites
f.intervention: Silane application combined with adhesive before composite repair
f.comparison: Adhesive alone
f.main_result: Silane plus adhesive gave significantly higher repair bond strengths than adhesive alone (p=0.003), with a larger effect for nonhydrolyzed silanes (effect size 7.30).

f.population: Zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (VITA Suprinity) ceramic discs
f.intervention: HF-acid etching for 20, 40 or 60 seconds, with or without a resin-cement layer
f.comparison: Shortest etching time (20 s) and specimens without resin cement
f.main_result: Without resin cement, flexural strength rose with etching time (250.8 MPa at 20 s to 342.9 MPa at 60 s); a resin-cement layer raised strength at 20 s (341.8 MPa).

f.population: Silver-palladium, gold-silver and cobalt-chromium alloys and titanium disks bonded to acrylic rods
f.intervention: Thiophosphoric methacrylate primer modified with phosphoric methacrylates and/or benzoyl peroxide
f.comparison: Acetone-only and single-monomer primers
f.main_result: A primer mixing thiophosphoric and phosphoric methacrylates with benzoyl peroxide and heat gave bond strengths over 20 MPa that stayed unchanged after 2,000 thermocycles.

f.population: Bovine incisor enamel
f.intervention: Five universal adhesives applied in self-etch or etch-and-rinse mode with immediate air blowing or prolonged application
f.comparison: Immediate air blowing (IA) versus prolonged application (PA), self-etch versus etch-and-rinse mode
f.main_result: Etch-and-rinse mode gave significantly higher SBS and Ra than self-etch mode regardless of application time or adhesive.
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research and the Sato Fund
