f.intervention: Universal adhesives (origin, chemistry, strengths, weaknesses, clinical use)
f.funding_coi: Author declares no affiliation with the companies mentioned

f.population: Disks cast in two type IV gold alloys (Maxgold, Sofard)
f.intervention: Vinyl-thiol (V-Primer) or thiophosphate (Metal Primer) priming before bonding with an adhesive resin
f.comparison: Unprimed control specimens
f.main_result: After 20,000 thermocycles, primed groups had significantly greater shear bond strength than unprimed specimens (p < 0.05).

f.intervention: Bioactive composites and bonding agents with calcium phosphate nanoparticles and antibacterial or protein-repellent resins
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; many cited studies supported by NIH and NSFC grants

f.population: Healthy edentulous individuals or cadavers with atrophic or non-atrophic maxillary/mandibular ridges
f.intervention: Direct bone microstructure assessment (histomorphometry, micro-CT etc.)
f.comparison: Anterior vs posterior, maxillary vs mandibular, atrophic vs non-atrophic sites
f.main_result: Weighted mean total bone volume was 0.365 (95% CI 0.278 to 0.452), higher in anterior than posterior sites, and lower in atrophic than non-atrophic sites.
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest

f.population: 22 patients with at least one implant with a small bony dehiscence defect (≤5 mm)
f.intervention: Guided bone regeneration with DBBM and a native collagen membrane
f.comparison: Spontaneous healing without treatment
f.main_result: Between implant placement and 6-month reentry, buccal vertical bone changed by -0.17 mm in the spontaneous healing group and +1.79 mm in the GBR group (p=0.017).

f.population: Partially edentulous patients receiving implants in healed sites with native bone
f.intervention: Implants placed with different residual buccal bone thickness (BBT) at placement
f.comparison: Group 1 BBT ≤0.5 mm vs Group 2 >0.5 and <1.5 mm vs Group 3 ≥1.5 mm
outcomes: buccal gingival margin change (tooth height) at 1, 2 and 3 years
f.main_result: At 3 years the buccal gum receded 1.22 mm for BBT ≤0.5 mm and 0.64 mm for 0.5-1.5 mm, but grew coronally 0.77 mm for BBT ≥1.5 mm (p ≤ 0.01).
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest

f.population: healthy patients with at least one dental implant
f.intervention: implant placement and soft tissue healing, grouped by initial soft tissue thickness (>=2 mm)
f.comparison: soft tissue thickness <2 mm
f.main_result: Thicker (>=2 mm) soft tissue was associated with significantly less marginal bone loss than thin tissue (0.54; p = .027), confirmed by trial sequential analysis.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Half of the included studies came from the same group, and implant types, abutment geometry and positioning varied, giving high heterogeneity.

f.population: clinical studies of soft tissue augmentation around dental implants
f.intervention: soft tissue augmentation procedures (bilaminar or apically positioned flap techniques with CTG, CM, ADM or FGG)
f.comparison: non-augmented sites
f.main_result: Bilaminar CTG or ADM gave the highest mucosal thickness gain, APF with FGG the greatest keratinized mucosa gain.
f.sample_size: 52 articles, 23 RCTs in the network meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: No financial interests; partly supported by a University of Michigan graduate student fund

f.population: patients receiving dental implants at a university implant center (maxilla and mandible, some with bone augmentation)
f.intervention: implant placement with resonance frequency analysis at surgery (primary stability) and after osseointegration (secondary stability), related to preoperative CT cortical bone thickness
f.comparison: non-augmentation versus augmentation, 1-stage versus 2-stage surgery, maxilla versus mandible
f.main_result: Mean ISQ was 69.34 at surgery and 75.99 after osseointegration, with a weak positive correlation between cortical bone thickness and stability.
f.funding_coi: Supported by JSPS KAKENHI; no conflict of interest reported

f.population: predominantly white male patients (mean age 62.9 years) at 30 VA medical centers and two university clinics, with more than 3,000 root-form implants
f.intervention: measurement of residual facial bone thickness at implant insertion and facial bone height change at uncovering
f.comparison: HA-coated versus non-HA-coated implants
outcomes: facial bone response (loss or gain) between insertion and uncovering
f.main_result: Mean facial bone response was -0.7 mm for 2,685 implants; bone loss decreased as facial bone thickness approached 1.8 to 2 mm, and failed implants lost more bone (-2.8 mm).
f.follow_up: uncovering at 3 to 4 months (mandible) and 6 to 8 months (maxilla)

f.funding_coi: No external funding

f.population: clinical trials of bone-level and tissue-level dental implants reporting bone-level changes
f.intervention: bone-level versus tissue-level implant designs
f.main_result: Methodology, follow-up and multifactorial causes of bone loss varied so widely that direct comparison of bone loss around the implant types was impossible.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest reported
f.limitations: Short-term results, limited sample size and radiographic measurement of only mesial and distal crestal bone loss.

f.population: edentulous or extraction sites with insufficient bone for implant placement
f.intervention: guided tissue regeneration with non-resorbable e-PTFE membranes, classified by timing relative to extraction and implant placement (immediate, recent, delayed, mature sites)
f.main_result: Sites are classified as immediate, recent, delayed or mature; the recent site is preferred over the immediate one because membrane coverage is more predictable.

f.population: BOPT crowns over truncoconical implant abutments without finishing line, prepared on the working model
f.intervention: analogical (plaster model reduction) and digital (intraoral scan, designed and printed prototype model) workflows for designing the BOPT emergence profile
f.comparison: analogical versus digital workflow
f.main_result: The analogical workflow gives satisfactory and predictable outcomes, but the digital workflow is developing rapidly and is considered the most realistic option.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Long-term data on the approach are lacking and warranted in future studies.

f.funding_coi: Author is a key opinion leader for Sweden & Martina, supplier of the burs

f.intervention: horizontal (finish line) versus vertical (shoulderless and edgeless verti prep) tooth preparation for crowns
f.main_result: No single preparation type is recommended for all cases; the finish line choice depends on pulp vitality, tooth location, material and other factors.
f.limitations: Few clinical studies assess the efficacy of vertical preparation, so further research is needed.

f.population: patients with a single missing molar or premolar, treated with single implants
f.intervention: screw-retained CAD/CAM crown, cemented crown without finishing line (BOPT), or conventional cemented crown with finishing line on single implants
f.comparison: screw-retained (GS) versus cemented BOPT (GBOPT) versus conventional cemented crown with finishing line (GCC)
f.main_result: After 3 years bone loss was 0.10 mm with cemented BOPT crowns, 0.35 mm with screw-retained and 0.67 mm with conventionally cemented crowns (BOPT least, p < 0.01).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

outcomes: soft tissue stability at the prosthetic/tissue interface
f.main_result: The authors report that BOPT maintained pericoronal soft tissue stability in anterior and posterior areas in 15 years of clinical experience.
f.limitations: More clinical and biological studies are needed to give the technique scientific value.

materials_brands: BOPT diamond drill assortment with stainless steel holder (code Z4999)

f.population: A 58-year-old patient without medical problems with missing upper posterior teeth and an old anterior fixed prosthesis
f.intervention: Three tissue-level conical PRAMA implants with BOPT abutments without finish line, plus BOPT preparation of anterior teeth, restored with metal-ceramic and zirconia prostheses
f.main_result: At 6 months the peri-implant mucosa showed excellent health with stable volume and shape, and no complications occurred over 24 months.
f.limitations: Medium- to long-term prospective studies are needed to confirm clinical behavior.

f.intervention: BOPT feather-edge flapless preparation with provisional relining and a prosthetic margin placed in the sulcus
f.comparison: Horizontal preparations with finishing lines (chamfer, shoulder)

f.population: Adult non-smoking patients with old fixed restorations in the esthetic zone needing replacement
f.intervention: Full-coverage zirconia-core restorations on teeth prepared with BOPT
f.comparison: Single crowns versus fixed partial dentures
f.main_result: At 4 years, 98.6% of teeth had stable margins, gingival thickness increased by 32.5%, and restoration survival was 96.6%.

f.population: One beagle dog, mandibular third and fourth premolars (four implant sites)
f.intervention: Socket-shield technique: buccal root fragment retained with immediate titanium implant placed lingual to it
f.comparison: Implant placed with versus without contact to the buccal tooth fragment
f.main_result: All four implants osseointegrated without inflammation, and the tooth fragment showed no resorption and was attached to the buccal bone by a physiologic periodontal ligament.
f.funding_coi: Funded by an unconditional research grant from Thommen Medical; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 5 bilayered porcelain-zirconia specimens (in vitro)
f.intervention: Four-point bending interfacial delamination test of VITA VM9 porcelain on Y-TZP
f.main_result: Mean strain energy release rate was 12.4 J/m2 with adhesive failure along the interface, indicating relatively poor adhesion.

f.population: 36 metal-porcelain specimens in three groups
f.comparison: Gold alloy with Vita Omega 900 ceramic (control)
f.main_result: Titanium groups (63.54 and 68.17 MPa) had significantly higher shear bond strength than gold alloy (40.55 MPa), with no difference between milled and cast-and-milled titanium.
f.funding_coi: Financial support from FAPESP
L. Fung is a paid consultant for SprintRay 3D printing technologies

f.population: Maxillary partially edentulous typodont with 3 implant replicas
f.intervention: Additively manufactured casts from three scan body and digital implant replica systems
f.comparison: Conventional polyvinyl siloxane open-tray impression with stone cast
outcomes: linear discrepancy on x, y, z axes
f.main_result: AM casts had lower 3D discrepancies than conventional casts; conventional was better on the apicocoronal position.

f.intervention: Additive manufacturing technologies (stereolithography, material extrusion, powder-based fusion, inkjet printing, binder jetting) for all-ceramic crowns
f.comparison: Subtractive CNC milling of ceramics (discussed as background)
f.main_result: AM has shown promising experimental outcomes for all-ceramic crowns but has not yet reached a commercial breakthrough.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest disclosed
f.limitations: Literature on AM of ceramic crowns is scanty and dispersed; heterogeneity makes outcomes hard to standardize.

f.population: 41-year-old male with a fractured left maxillary second premolar
f.intervention: Milled CAD/CAM Ti-6Al-4V coping veneered with porcelain, cemented with self-adhesive resin cement

f.population: four labside and two production center dental NC milling machines
f.intervention: mechanical-engineering comparison of technical and economic criteria of labside and production-center milling machines
f.main_result: Production-center machines offer a wider range of materials and restoration shapes than labside machines, which offer more than chairside; more complex solutions need more skilled users and cost more

f.intervention: VM9 veneering porcelain on zirconia frameworks (Vita YZ), with layering technique
f.comparison: Other veneering porcelains and ceramics (VM7, Omega 900, MKII, Mz100, etc.) and enamel
f.main_result: Fine-microstructure veneering porcelains such as VM9 and VM7 showed low opposing enamel wear and improved flexural strength compared with older porcelains.
f.limitations: Long-term clinical data on zirconia as a replacement for metal ceramics are unavailable.

f.population: Partially dentate and edentulous patients with cancer on high-dose antiresorptive medication
f.intervention: Straumann Roxolid Bone Level implants placed without augmentation, restored with crowns or overdentures
f.main_result: Implant survival and success after 2 years of loading were 100% and 97.4%, and OHLQoL increased in all groups.
f.sample_size: 22 patients with 39 implants completed treatment; 13 patients (23 implants) completed 2 years
f.funding_coi: Amgen, Institute Straumann AG, Tandlægeforeningen; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Feasibility study with few patients and a high dropout rate because patients died from cancer progression.

f.population: Partially edentulous patients with implant-supported FDPs with cantilever extension in posterior areas
f.intervention: Implant-supported fixed dental prostheses with mesial or distal cantilever extension (1 premolar unit), re-evaluated after at least 10 years
f.comparison: Implant surfaces adjacent to versus distant from the cantilever extension
f.main_result: Patient-based implant survival was 96.2% and marginal bone level change was not significant (1.2 to 1.6 mm) after a mean 13.3 years; loss of retention occurred in 34.6% of patients.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' own institution; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Partially dentate patients with implant-supported FDPs or single crowns in the posterior maxilla or mandible
f.intervention: Implant-supported FDPs with cantilever extension
f.comparison: Implant-supported crowns or FDPs without cantilever
f.main_result: Mean peri-implant bone loss was 0.23 mm with cantilevers versus 0.09 mm without after 5.3 years, not significantly different.
f.limitations: Study results are limited by the small number of patients and diameter-reduced implants (3.3 mm) that fractured under cantilevers.

f.population: Patients with single or partial edentulism treated consecutively with sintered porous surface implants
f.intervention: SPS implants restored with single crowns or partial fixed dentures, grouped by crown-implant ratio
f.comparison: Implant groups with different crown-implant ratios
f.main_result: Overall implant success was 98.1% with mean peri-implant bone loss of 0.48 mm at 36 months; success and bone loss correlated with C/I ratio, with thresholds of 3.10 (anatomical) and 3.40 (clinical).
f.sample_size: 259 SPS implants in 136 patients followed up
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in any company or product mentioned

f.population: Subjects with implant-supported single crowns or two-implant FDPs with one cantilever extension in the posterior maxilla or mandible
f.intervention: Implant-supported single crowns or short-span FDPs with one mesial or distal cantilever extension
f.comparison: Implants of FDPs adjacent to versus distant from the cantilever extension
f.main_result: No implant loss (100% survival) and no significant differences in marginal bone level change or PPD between the three groups after a mean 5+ years
f.sample_size: 19 SC implants and 21 two-implant FDPs in 38 subjects
f.follow_up: mean 78.2 months for SCs and 67.8 months for FDPs
materials_brands: Straumann Dental Implant System, SLA tissue-level implants
f.limitations: Small sample size and follow-up from prosthesis delivery meant early failures could not be accounted for

f.population: Patients with partial fixed implant-supported prostheses
f.intervention: Presence of a cantilever
f.comparison: Absence of a cantilever
f.main_result: Cantilevers did not compromise marginal bone loss or prosthesis survival, while minor complications were more frequent in groups without cantilevers (P = .008).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: All included studies were low-quality by the Jadad scale and not randomized.

f.population: Patients with fixed complete dental prostheses with distal cantilevers on implants
f.intervention: Distal implant-supported cantilever prostheses
f.comparison: Traditional tooth-retained distal cantilever prostheses
f.main_result: Weighted prosthesis survival was 95% over 7.3 ± 2.6 years; the most frequent complication was screw loosening.
f.limitations: The majority of studies lacked specific data.

f.population: Partially edentulous patients with implant-supported cantilevered fixed restorations (at least 10 patients, mean follow-up 5 years or more)
f.intervention: Implant-supported cantilevered fixed dental prostheses
f.main_result: Estimated 5-10 year survival was 98.4% for implants and 99.2% for rehabilitations, with cumulative complication rates of 28.66% (patients) and 26.57% (prostheses).
f.sample_size: 9 papers selected for partially edentulous patients
f.follow_up: Mean follow-up of at least 5 years in included studies
f.limitations: Retrospective and prospective studies of different designs were analysed together.

f.population: Patients with implant-supported fixed partial dentures with or without cantilevers, at least one year of loading
f.intervention: Cantilever FDPs
f.comparison: Non-cantilever FDPs
f.main_result: Implant survival and success were 96.7% and 87.9% for cantilever FDPs versus 99.5% and 92.6% for non-cantilever FDPs, with no overall difference in bone loss (0.58 vs 0.59 mm).
f.sample_size: 107 subjects with 128 cantilever FDPs on 132 implants and 99 subjects with 144 non-cantilever FDPs on 203 implants

f.population: One 67-year-old female patient with three implants in the mandibular left second premolar, first molar and second molar regions
f.intervention: In vivo 3D load measurement with piezoelectric transducers under four implant configurations supporting a three-unit FPD
f.comparison: Three-implant prosthesis vs central pontic, posterior cantilever and anterior cantilever two-implant prostheses
outcomes: 3D load on each implant during maximum voluntary clenching
load on implants during chewing gum
f.main_result: Highest load was on the first molar implant in the posterior cantilever during chewing (318.90 ± 70.71 N); three-implant prosthesis and central pontic distributed loads more equally than cantilever designs.
f.sample_size: 1 patient, 3 implants; MVC n = 5 and 17 chewing strokes per configuration
f.follow_up: Implants functioning 3 years since prosthetic restoration
materials_brands: Brånemark System MKIII RP implants (Nobel Biocare)
f.funding_coi: Grants-in-aid for Scientific Research (Japan MEXT); no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Single patient; results interpreted within the limitations of the study.

f.population: Six longitudinal studies of implant-supported cantilever FDPs in partially edentulous patients
f.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses (ICFDPs)
f.main_result: Estimated 5-year implant survival 98.9% and ICFDP survival 97.1%; biological complications 5.7% at implant level; veneer fracture was the commonest technical complication
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no potential conflicts
f.limitations: Limited literature with non-homogeneous study design and follow-up

f.population: Standardized partially edentulous maxillary models (D2 bone) with 4 mm, 8 mm and >12 mm residual bone height and flat or oblique sinus floors
f.intervention: Static computer-assisted implant placement (sCAIP)
f.comparison: Free-handed implant placement
f.main_result: sCAIP gave higher 3D accuracy independent of bone height and sinus morphology, whereas free-handed accuracy depended strongly on alveolar bone height and on sinus morphology.
materials_brands: Straumann TLX S 4.5 × 10 mm RT tissue-level implants
f.funding_coi: University of Bern, Department of Oral Surgery and Stomatology; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: In vitro design, other instruments and implant designs not evaluated, and only single-tooth replacement scenarios.

f.intervention: Review of CBCT use in preoperative implant planning
f.comparison: Conventional lower-dose dental radiography
f.main_result: CBCT should not be used routinely for initial implant site assessment; use it only when clinical and conventional radiographic information is inadequate, with the field of view limited to the area of interest.
f.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose

f.population: 72 standardized stainless steel dies simulating a first mandibular premolar
f.intervention: Cementation and hydrothermal aging (5 and 20 h) of CAD-CAM metal-ceramic, veneered zirconia and monolithic zirconia crowns
f.comparison: Uncemented vs cemented crowns; non-aged vs aged zirconia
materials_brands: Z-CAD HD / Z-CAD HTL zirconia (Metoxit) with IPS e.max Ceram
f.funding_coi: Research grant between University Complutense of Madrid and AVINENT Implant System SL

f.population: Ten ITI hollow screw implants (3.8 mm) in acrylic blocks with solid titanium abutments and cast noble alloy copings
f.intervention: Cementation of castings with six luting cements followed by pull-out retention testing
f.comparison: Six cements compared with each other (Temp Bond NE, IRM, Hy-Bond, Protec Cem, Durelon, Panavia 21)
outcomes: load required to de-cement each coping
f.main_result: Mean de-cementation load ranged from 3.18 kg (Temp Bond) to 36.53 kg (Panavia 21), with Durelon 23.55 and Protec Cem 18.98 kg.
f.limitations: In vitro study; results with natural teeth abutments may not transfer to implant abutments.

f.population: Titanium (grades 1-5) and Ni-Cr discs cemented to sliced extracted maxillary first molars
f.intervention: Cementing titanium discs with zinc polycarboxylate, glass ionomer or zinc phosphate cement, then shear testing and SEM
f.comparison: Ni-Cr control and the three cements against each other
f.main_result: Mean shear bond strength ranged 0.31 to 15.6 MPa; zinc polycarboxylate cement was highest but corroded the titanium alloy.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Short one-week duration, no time-dependent actions and no titanium surface treatment.

f.population: Silver-palladium complete metal crowns on metal dies of a prepared dentoform premolar with three finish lines
f.intervention: Cementation with zinc phosphate or glass-ionomer at seating forces of 25, 100 and 300 N on chamfer, shoulder or beveled-shoulder margins
f.main_result: Higher seating forces improved seating but not retention; shoulder margins and glass-ionomer gave greater retention than chamfer and zinc phosphate
f.sample_size: Crowns for three dies; each combination repeated 10 times

f.population: Twenty stone dies (10 from a shoulder die, 10 from a shoulder-bevel die) with nonprecious alloy cast crowns
f.intervention: Crown cementation with die spacer, 5 or 30 lb seating force, two cements and two seating aids
f.comparison: No die spacer vs die spacer; zinc phosphate vs glass ionomer; 5 vs 30 lb; shoulder vs bevel
outcomes: crown seating discrepancy measured with micrometer
f.main_result: Die spacer, 30 lb seating force and glass ionomer cement each significantly improved crown seating; the bevel improved seating under heavy force or glass ionomer.

f.intervention: Literature analysis and market research on definitive resin composite cements to propose a classification
f.main_result: Proposes classifying resin cements as adhesive/multi-step, self-adhesive/one-step, or universal (one- or multi-step); only three products meet the criteria for universal cement.
materials_brands: RelyX Universal with Scotchbond Universal Plus
Panavia SA Universal with Clearfil Universal Bond Quick
f.funding_coi: Open access funding by Universita degli Studi di Bologna (CRUI-CARE); authors declare no financial interest in the companies
f.limitations: Despite promising in vitro results, clinical trials and long-term laboratory studies are needed to confirm universal cements.

f.population: Eighteen caries-free human molars (flat dentin) bonded to CAD/CAM resin blocks
f.intervention: Novel experimental light-cured resin cement HL-100C
f.comparison: Panavia V5 dual-cured resin cement and Clearfil AP-X composite
outcomes: microtensile bond strength at 24 h and 7 days
f.main_result: Resin cement type significantly affected µTBS, and the experimental light-cured cement HL showed better bonding performance and higher KHN than Panavia V5.
f.funding_coi: Grant in aid for scientific research, Ministry of Education of Japan; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: In vitro study limitations (not itemised).

f.population: Fifty Co-Cr CAD-CAM implant abutment replicas with matching crowns
f.intervention: Precementation of crowns on CAD-CAM precementation abutments with 25, 50, 75 or 100 µm reductions before definitive cementation
f.comparison: Conventional cementation with glass ionomer cement (G0)
f.main_result: Precementation with a 50 µm abutment (A50) reduced subgingival residual cement without affecting retention; cement weight G50 7.2 ±0.6 mg vs G25 6.0 ±1.1 mg.
f.funding_coi: Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission grant 2018KY059
f.limitations: In vitro study; limitations not itemised.

f.population: Healthy patients aged 20 to 50 with single titanium implants in the premolar region
f.intervention: Cementation of a modified metal-ceramic crown on a titanium abutment with three luting cements at three peri-implant collar heights, retrieving and measuring residual cement
f.comparison: Low (<2 mm), medium (2-4 mm) and high (>4 mm) collar height groups, and resin vs glass ionomer vs zinc oxide noneugenol cement
f.main_result: Residual cement increased with collar height (high collar about 2.1-2.3 mm3 vs low collar 0.08-0.33 mm3) and zinc oxide noneugenol cement left significantly less than resin or glass ionomer cement, which did not differ.
f.sample_size: 30 implant sites (10 per collar-height group), each tested with 3 cements
materials_brands: GC Gold Label 1 glass ionomer cement
RelyX Temp NE zinc oxide noneugenol cement
f.funding_coi: No specific grant funding

f.main_result: Current dental ceramics (glass-ceramics, polycrystalline ceramics, PICNs) have improved in strength and optical properties, and color-gradient/strength-graded blocks, CAD-CAM and 3D printing are advancing restoration production.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

outcomes: development, strengthening, strength, color and aesthetics of all-ceramic systems
f.main_result: No single universal all-ceramic material or system exists for all clinical cases; choice must follow indications, contraindications, laboratory and clinical evidence and patient aesthetic needs.
f.funding_coi: Grant from the University of Malaya (PG179-2014B); scholarship from the Iraqi government

f.main_result: Fabrication technology of dental ceramics has advanced greatly, with a ten-fold increase in flexural strength and fracture toughness.
Dental ceramics have reached a stage where long-span metal-free posterior FPDs can be made.

f.intervention: Proposed classification of ceramic and ceramic-like materials into glass-matrix, polycrystalline and resin-matrix ceramics
f.main_result: Ceramic and ceramic-like materials are organized into three families: glass-matrix, polycrystalline and resin-matrix ceramics
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq grant; authors reported no conflicts of interest

f.intervention: Fabrication of porcelain veneers and crowns on platinum foil
f.main_result: Platinum foil restorations showed excellent esthetic results and good fit with shorter production times; thermal-expansion porcelain cracks are unheard of with the technique.

f.intervention: Twin foil technique: inner unplated 0.025 mm platinum foil as matrix plus outer tin-plated oxidized foil bonded to aluminous core porcelain
f.main_result: Aluminous porcelain crowns bonded to thin tin-oxide-coated platinum foil need metal linings under 0.05 mm, cutting cost and improving aesthetics, and allow a porcelain butt fit.
f.funding_coi: Work done on behalf of the National Research Development Corporation

f.population: Aluminous porcelain bonded to platinum foil and other metal substrates
f.intervention: Coating the metal with a thin oxidisable metal layer (tin, indium, others) before firing porcelain
f.main_result: Tin coating of 0.2-2.0 µm before firing gave good porcelain-platinum bonding; tin and indium were the acceptable coatings for dental use.
f.sample_size: Bond strengths are means of at least eight tests
f.funding_coi: Grants from the Department of Health and Social Security and the National Research Development Corporation

f.main_result: Short-term clinical performance of zirconia-reinforced lithium silicates and lithium-aluminium disilicates is comparable to lithium disilicate.
f.funding_coi: First author funded by a Saudi Arabian Cultural Bureau scholarship; funder had no role; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: LSC strength remains inadequate for multiunit prostheses in the molar region

f.population: Aluminous porcelain disks (15 mm diameter, 2.0 mm thick) fired on platinum foil
f.intervention: Platinum foil bonded to the porcelain via tin oxide coating
f.comparison: Disks fired on pure (uncoated) platinum foil
outcomes: breaking stress in disk rupture test
f.main_result: Mean breaking stress rose from 70.48 to 128.96 N/mm2, about 83% stronger with bonded platinum foil.
f.limitations: Reduction of subsurface pores could not be confirmed by direct observation (micrography and SEM inconclusive).

f.main_result: Silicate ceramics have the best esthetics but are weaker than polycrystalline and resin-based ceramics, so they are mainly used as veneering ceramics.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts declared

f.main_result: Successful ceramic restorations depend on material selection, manufacturing technique and restoration design
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.population: 22 participants (110 implants) with full-arch mandibular prostheses re-examined at 25 years
f.intervention: Three implants placed alternately between the mental foramina: microtextured 3.6 mm internal-connection machined collar, microtextured 1.2 mm external-connection collar, machined 1.2 mm external-connection collar
f.comparison: Shorter (1.2 mm) vs longer (3.6 mm) machined collar; microtextured vs machined surface
f.main_result: Microtextured implants with the 3.6 mm collar lost 1.77 mm of bone versus 0.85 mm (machined) and 1.00 mm (microtextured) with the 1.2 mm collar (p<.001).
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Faculty of Dental Medicine, Université de Montréal; authors report no conflict of interest

f.population: Human studies reporting bleeding on probing, probing depth or case definitions of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
f.intervention: Design elements of the implant supracrestal complex: emergence profile and angle, tissue height, neck design, abutment/prosthesis material, retention and connection type
f.main_result: With bone-level implants, a wide emergence angle combined with a convex emergence profile was linked to peri-implantitis; evidence on abutment/prosthesis material and retention type was limited or inconclusive.
f.limitations: Limited by lack of consensus definitions, validated outcome measures and diverse methods

f.main_result: Proposes a two-part definition of attached gingiva, measured from the sulcus base to the MGJ when the biologic width is supracrestal and from the bone crest to the MGJ when it is subcrestal.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 45 patients needing a single ceramic crown
f.intervention: Digital shade selection with a smartphone (iPhone XS) and a light-correcting device with a cross-polarizing filter, and with a digital camera
f.comparison: Visual shade selection with a shade guide
outcomes: color difference (DE) between crown and adjacent tooth
f.main_result: Mean DE was 5.32 for visual selection versus 2.75 for digital camera (P=.002) and 2.34 for smartphone (P=.001); the two digital methods did not differ (P=.857).
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by Fondecyt

f.population: Maxillary and mandibular complete dentures fabricated on edentulous models
f.intervention: CAD-CAM-milled versus 3D-printed dentures with 90- or 45-degree build angles and light polymerization with or without the reference model
f.comparison: CAD-CAM-milled dentures versus four 3D-printed subgroups
f.main_result: CAD-CAM-milled dentures had the smallest dimensional deviations; in 3D printing a 90-degree build angle with additional light polymerization on the cast was most accurate
f.sample_size: 10 sets per group (milled and four printed subgroups)
f.funding_coi: Grants from National Taiwan University Hospital and Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau, Ministry of Science and Technology

f.population: Published clinical case reports of floor-of-mouth hematoma after implant placement (1986-2010)
f.main_result: Reported studies were mostly case series showing hematoma is a very rare complication; dental CT planning and accurate implant length are recommended to avoid it.
f.limitations: No randomized controlled trials exist; all reports were case series

f.population: 27 reported cases of life-threatening bleeding during or after implant placement
f.main_result: Most of the 27 cases bled in the anterior interforaminal region, and most needed intubation or tracheotomy.

f.population: 596 patients with implant-supported reconstructions, randomly sampled from a Swedish registry
f.main_result: 42% of patients (251 of 596) had at least one technical or biological complication over about 9 years; extent of therapy and periodontitis were risk factors.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Swedish public and research grants; two authors report fees from Dentsply Sirona and/or Straumann outside the work

f.main_result: Every study of dental-office curing lights found most were poorly maintained and delivered inadequate output, risking undercured resin.

f.population: Patients undergoing gingival augmentation procedures with or without gingival recession defects, in 105 RCTs
f.intervention: Gingival phenotype modification with autogenous (CTG, FGG), allogeneic (ADM) or xenogenic (collagen matrix) grafts, with coronally advanced flap or apically positioned flap
f.comparison: Flap alone (root coverage) or apically positioned flap alone / untreated sites (non-root coverage)
f.main_result: All grafts increased gingival thickness versus flap alone; keratinized tissue increased significantly only with CTG or ADM in root coverage; autogenous grafts (CTG/FGG) were superior in all comparisons.
f.sample_size: 105 RCTs (95 root coverage with 3,539 treated recessions; 10 non-root coverage with 699 sites)
f.follow_up: At least 12 months for root coverage, 6 months for non-root coverage
f.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund

f.population: One 23-year-old woman with gingival recession on the mandibular left canine
f.intervention: Single-incision technique to harvest subepithelial connective tissue grafts from the palate
f.main_result: A single incision parallel to the gingival margin yields grafts of variable size and the palatal donor site heals by primary intention; the case showed root coverage and resolved hypersensitivity at 4 months
f.limitations: Reduced visibility of the donor site during graft preparation

f.population: Patients with buccal soft tissue dehiscence around single implants in the esthetic area
f.intervention: Crown removal, abutment reduction, coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft and final restoration
f.main_result: Mean dehiscence coverage was 99.2% with 79% complete coverage at 5 years, with increases in soft tissue thickness (0.3 mm) and keratinized tissue height (0.5 mm) versus 1 year.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: 20 patients with buccal soft tissue dehiscence around a single implant in the esthetic area
f.intervention: Crown removal, abutment reduction, coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft and final restoration
f.comparison: Unrestored contralateral tooth used as reference
f.main_result: One-year mean dehiscence coverage was 96.3% with complete coverage in 75% of sites; tissue thickness increased by 1.54 mm.

f.population: 20 subjects with Seibert class I ridge defects (single tooth gaps) in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Vascularized interpositional periosteal-connective tissue graft (pediculated)
f.comparison: Free subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Both techniques augmented the ridge; after 6 months the pediculated graft showed significantly less shrinkage (P = 0.03).
f.funding_coi: Ege University Research Foundation grant; no conflict of interest

f.main_result: Soft tissue grafting at implant sites is advocated; increasing keratinized mucosa width benefits peri-implant health and soft tissue thickness helps prevent mucosal recession.

f.population: 20 patients with Miller Class I or II recession defects (52 teeth)
f.intervention: Coronally advanced flap with subepithelial connective tissue graft using full-thickness flap reflection
f.comparison: CAF with SCTG using partial-thickness flap reflection
f.main_result: Mean root coverage was 97% (full-thickness) versus 95% (partial-thickness); no significant difference in GR reduction, KT gain or PD.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: More expanded studies are needed to confirm the findings

f.population: seven monkeys
f.intervention: Free connective tissue grafts from keratinized gingiva transplanted into alveolar mucosa pouches, then exposed to epithelialize from surrounding alveolar mucosa
f.comparison: Alveolar mucosa connective tissue grafts (controls)
f.main_result: Gingival connective tissue grafts became covered with keratinized epithelium like normal gingiva, whereas alveolar mucosa grafts were covered by non-keratinized epithelium

f.population: Patients needing single-tooth replacement in the anterior maxilla after extraction (48 in final sample)
f.intervention: Immediate-load post-extractive implant with subepithelial connective tissue graft placed by tunnel technique
f.comparison: Immediate-load post-extractive implant without raising a flap (no graft)
f.main_result: Grafted sites gained 35% in thickness versus -10% in non-grafted, and had higher mean PES (8 vs 6.65) at 2 years.
materials_brands: Straumann Tapered Effect / Bone Level SLActive implants

f.population: 33 stone casts from 30 patients with single posterior tooth defects
f.intervention: Digital design and 3D thickness analysis of individual soft tissue substitutes with clustering to derive average shapes
f.main_result: Three average STS shapes were identified (maxilla square n=13, rectangle n=11; mandible n=9) with highest thickness in the buccal portion (median 2 mm).
f.funding_coi: Funded by Geistlich Pharma AG; one author is a Geistlich employee; no conflicts declared

f.population: Patients with dental implants treated with soft tissue augmentation, from prospective clinical studies
f.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation (bilaminar or apically positioned flap) with FGG, CTG, ADM or collagen matrix
f.comparison: Non-augmented implants where reported
f.main_result: Augmented implants showed high survival and low peri-implantitis incidence (0-7.14%) medium and long term, with stable soft tissue margin and CTG sites gaining KMW and MT over time.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Limited number of studies, their design, and lack of information on implant location; results qualitative only

f.population: Systemically healthy humans with dental implants
f.intervention: Connective tissue graft to increase peri-implant soft tissue thickness
f.comparison: No grafting, or soft tissue substitutes
f.main_result: Thick mucosa tended to give superior esthetic outcomes; connective tissue graft remains the standard of care for increasing mucosal thickness.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest reported

f.population: Patients with buccal soft tissue dehiscence around loaded dental implants, without peri-implantitis
f.intervention: Soft tissue augmentation procedures (connective tissue graft or acellular dermal matrix with flaps) to cover BSTD
f.comparison: Baseline or any other augmentation procedure
f.main_result: Complete coverage of BSTD was achieved in about 70% of cases at 1 year (2 studies, n=36) and at 5 years (3 studies, n=54).
f.sample_size: Seven articles from five investigations; 6 to 22 patients per group
f.follow_up: At least 6 months; meta-analyses at 1 and 5 years
f.funding_coi: No competing interests declared
f.limitations: Only one RCT with high risk of bias, high heterogeneity and limited sample sizes

f.population: systemically healthy patients with dental implants
f.intervention: soft tissue grafting to increase keratinized tissue width or mucosal thickness at implant sites
f.comparison: no grafting (maintenance) or a different graft type
f.main_result: Grafting for gain of mucosal thickness gave significantly less marginal bone loss (WMD 0.110 mm, p<.001); for keratinized tissue gain, autogenous grafts gave higher final bone levels (WMD -0.175 mm) and better gingival index (WMD 0.863).
f.sample_size: 10 controlled clinical studies (4 on keratinized tissue gain, 6 on mucosal thickness gain)
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant; authors report no conflict of interest

f.population: 88 patients in need of soft tissue volume augmentation at single implant sites, recruited at nine centers
f.intervention: soft tissue volume augmentation with a cross-linked volume collagen matrix (Geistlich Fibro-Gide)
f.comparison: autogenous subepithelial connective tissue graft
f.main_result: Crestal mucosal thickness gain at 120 days was 0.3 ± 2.1 mm with the collagen matrix vs 0.8 ± 1.6 mm with the graft (p = .455); noninferiority was not shown, while PROMs including pain favored the matrix.
f.sample_size: 88 patients (one implant each), 79 attended the one-year follow-up
f.follow_up: 1 year after insertion of the final restoration (360 days)
f.funding_coi: Funded by Geistlich Pharma AG and the University of Zurich clinic
f.limitations: Heterogeneity of results between centers

f.population: six beagle dogs with surgically created gingival recession defects
f.intervention: subepithelial connective tissue graft harvested from the palate and placed over denuded root surfaces under a coronally repositioned flap
f.main_result: The graft was completely vascularized by 14 days, its blood supply arising from the periodontal plexus, supraperiosteal plexus and overlying flap; attachment was by epithelial downgrowth plus connective tissue, with little new bone or cementum.

f.population: patients with a failing maxillary anterior tooth treated with immediate implant placement and provisionalization (24 without graft, 31 with graft)
f.intervention: immediate implant placement and provisionalization with a subepithelial connective tissue graft (CT group)
f.comparison: the same procedure without a connective tissue graft (NCT group)
f.main_result: At prosthesis delivery mean FGTT was greater with the graft (2.61 mm) than without (1.42 mm); mean change was 1.43 mm vs 0.32 mm (P<.01).

f.population: systemically healthy patients receiving at least one dental implant, with at least one year of follow-up
f.intervention: soft tissue augmentation (keratinized mucosa or volume), alone or combined with hard tissue augmentation
f.comparison: no soft tissue augmentation, or hard tissue augmentation alone
f.main_result: Soft tissue augmentation inconsistently affected marginal bone level changes versus none but consistently improved secondary outcomes; combined soft plus hard augmentation did not differ in bone level from hard augmentation alone but gave less soft tissue recession.
f.limitations: Studies varied considerably so only two meta-analyses could be performed

f.intervention: PDP management triad (implant position, implant design, prosthetic design) to increase peri-implant soft tissue thickness
f.comparison: Thin versus thick tissue biotypes
f.main_result: A thick soft tissue biotype positively affects the esthetic outcome of implant-supported restorations; biotype can be modified through the PDP triad.
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund
f.limitations: No definitive clinical trial has examined the influence of peri-implant tissue biotype on implant esthetics; few trials exist

f.population: single implants adjacent to teeth and two adjacent implants in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: vertical distance from bone crest to interproximal contact point (single implants) and horizontal inter-implant distance (adjacent implants)
f.main_result: For single implants papilla fill was partial or complete in 56.5% to 100% of cases and depended mainly on the tooth's clinical attachment level; for two adjacent implants an optimal horizontal distance could not be defined.
f.sample_size: two systematic reviews (12 studies on single implants, 4 on adjacent implants)
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant
f.limitations: Heterogeneity of study design, population and assessment prevented meta-analyses

f.population: Five patients aged 32-53 years with hyperplastic tissue response after connective tissue grafting
f.intervention: Corrective surgery: internal in-toto excision of hyperplastic tissue while preserving the overlying mucosa
f.main_result: Follow-up of 1-5 years showed stable results with no relapse or recurrence of tissue overgrowth.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no financial interest in companies whose materials are included
f.limitations: Authors acknowledge conclusions hold only within the limits of a small case series.

f.population: patients in need of soft tissue augmentation around single or multiple implants
f.intervention: soft tissue substitutes (volume stable collagen matrix, acellular dermal matrix or other)
f.comparison: autogenous connective tissue graft, free gingival graft, or no graft
f.main_result: Soft tissue substitutes significantly reduced pain perception, painkiller use and surgery time compared with autogenous grafts, with similar satisfaction and no impairment of clinical outcomes.
f.limitations: Risk of bias of included studies ranged from low to high, so results should be interpreted with caution

f.population: 92 clinical studies of peri-implant soft-tissue augmentation published in the last 10 years (39 RCTs, 20 non-RCTs, 33 case series)
f.intervention: soft-tissue augmentation interventions in the context of dental implant therapy
f.main_result: Most frequent primary outcomes were facial mucosa thickness by clinical methods (22.83%), keratinized mucosa width (19.57%) and mucosal margin position (18.48%); clinical outcomes dominated, digital methods are increasing and PROMs are underreported.

f.population: 44 patients undergoing epithelialized gingival graft harvesting from the palate
f.intervention: palatal wound treated with a hemostatic collagen sponge plus cyanoacrylate
f.comparison: hemostatic collagen sponge alone
f.main_result: Pain was significantly lower in the cyanoacrylate group on every day studied and analgesic consumption was lower; graft width < 14 mm was associated with less discomfort.

f.population: clinical studies of soft tissue augmentation around dental implants reporting PROMs
f.intervention: autogenous grafts (free gingival graft, connective tissue graft), acellular dermal matrix and xenogeneic collagen matrix
f.comparison: autogenous grafts versus substitutes, and non-grafted sites
f.main_result: Most studies found no significant differences in patient morbidity and painkiller intake between autogenous grafts and substitutes; grafting improved satisfaction and aesthetic evaluation compared with non-grafted sites.

f.population: 16 patients with small buccal bone dehiscences (<=3 mm) after single implant placement, plus 6 negative-control patients without dehiscence
f.intervention: Subepithelial connective tissue graft (SCTG) for small peri-implant dehiscence defects
f.comparison: Guided bone regeneration (GBR)
outcomes: buccal bone and soft tissue thickness
f.main_result: Buccal contour changed by 0.45 mm (SCTG) versus -0.94 mm loss (GBR) between T2 and T7; SCTG had more stable profilometric outcomes and GBR was favored by PROMs.
f.sample_size: 16 randomized patients (SCTG 9, GBR 7) plus 6 negative controls
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech, Dentsply Sirona)
f.funding_coi: Mainly financially supported by the Clinic of Reconstructive Dentistry, University of Zurich
f.limitations: Pilot study with failed randomization of two patients causing unbalanced groups

f.funding_coi: Proceedings supported by the Osteology Foundation, Lucerne, Switzerland

f.population: Patients with a single implant in the esthetic zone (15-25) placed with simultaneous guided bone regeneration
f.intervention: Subepithelial connective tissue graft 4-6 weeks before abutment connection (test)
f.comparison: No additional soft tissue augmentation (control)
f.main_result: Median mean-distance loss at 12 years was -0.81 mm with grafting versus -0.56 mm without, not significantly different (p = .607).
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Clinic of Reconstructive Dentistry, University of Zurich; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Retrospective design without a priori power analysis, small sample size and no PROMs.

f.population: Published studies on soft tissue metric parameters, methods and aesthetic indices in implant dentistry
f.intervention: Review of five metric parameters, their registration methods and 15 aesthetic indices
f.main_result: Intra-oral registrations were least accurate and profilometric changes on digital surface models most accurate; PES qualified best for single implants and no index suited multiple implants.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; authors declare no conflicts, though Prof. Cosyn has collaboration agreements with Nobel Biocare and Straumann
f.limitations: Validity data depend on available literature, rater experience may bias reliability scores, and PROMs were out of scope.

f.population: Single case: maxillary right central incisor lost in a bicycle accident
f.intervention: Slim healing abutment with a thick connective tissue graft, preferably from the maxillary tuberosity, at implant placement
f.main_result: The Slim concept creates an abundance of soft tissue volume early to support long-term esthetic stability; the case was stable at 1 year.

f.population: 37 patients with 114 bilateral single Miller Class I and II gingival recession defects
f.intervention: Coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft (CAF+CTG)
f.comparison: Coronally advanced flap alone (CAF)
f.main_result: CAF+CTG gave significantly better recession reduction, keratinized tissue gain and root coverage than CAF alone at all follow-ups up to 60 months.
f.funding_coi: Croatian Ministry of Science grant; no conflicts of interest

f.population: 19 young patients (mean age 22) with tooth agenesis in the anterior maxilla receiving single-tooth implants with bone grafts
f.intervention: Facial connective tissue graft harvested from the palate at implant sites (test, n=10)
f.comparison: Implant sites without soft tissue graft (control, n=23)
f.main_result: At five years survival was 100% and success 93.9%; CTG sites had more facial dimensional gain (p = .010 at 3 mm) and better mucosa colour match (p = .035) than controls.
f.funding_coi: Financial support from the KOF/Calcin Foundation of the Danish Dental Association; no conflict of interest

f.population: Patients treated with flapless maxillary immediate implant placement
f.intervention: Customized healing abutment plus connective tissue graft (test)
f.comparison: Customized healing abutment alone (control)
f.main_result: No significant overall differences between groups at 1 year; with buccal bone thickness <=1 mm buccal volume change was -14.18% (control) vs -8.30% (CTG).
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Soft and hard tissue variations were not separated and no esthetic score such as PES was recorded.

f.main_result: Bacterial penetration at the implant-abutment interface may relate to early crestal bone loss, but an association with peri-implant diseases is not demonstrated.
f.limitations: Limited clinical evidence linking bacterial infiltration at the interface to crestal bone loss and peri-implant disease.

f.population: 50 consecutive partially edentulous patients with 69 implants
f.intervention: Two-part implants placed non-submerged with the implant-abutment junction 1-2 mm subcrestal
f.main_result: Mean marginal hard tissue loss was 0.11 mm at 1 year with 100% survival; hard tissue covered the implant shoulder in 69%.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; two authors received honoraria from DENTSPLY Friadent

f.population: 3D finite element models of an implant, crown and mandibular first molar bone
f.intervention: Varying implant diameter (3.5, 4.0, 4.5 mm), connection type and bone density under 200 N axial and 100 N oblique load
outcomes: Von Mises stress in implant and abutment
f.main_result: Connection type affected implant and abutment stress more than diameter, tissue-level being more favorable, and bone density most influenced bone strain.
f.funding_coi: Korean National Research Foundation grant

f.population: Patients with 143 two-stage implants placed at delayed stage
f.intervention: Implants grouped by vertical position of the implant-abutment interface (above, at, below bone level)
f.comparison: Groups A, B and C compared with each other
outcomes: Marginal bone level change on panoramic radiographs
f.main_result: At 36 months marginal bone loss was 0.99, 1.13 and 1.76 mm in groups A, B and C, significantly greater when the interface was below bone level.
f.funding_coi: Wonkwang University funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: 30 patients needing single-tooth implant rehabilitation
f.intervention: Platform-switched Morse taper implants placed with the IAI 1 mm or 2 mm below the buccal alveolar crest
f.comparison: Implants placed with the IAI at bone level (group 0)
f.main_result: Group 0 lost 0.27 mm of bone below the platform at 12 months while groups 1 and 2 lost none; bone covered the platform in 90% versus 35% of surfaces.
materials_brands: Ankylos CX implants and Ankylos standard/C abutment (Dentsply)
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by Dentsply; no conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 30 healthy adults with a single-tooth gap (one implant each)
f.intervention: Ankylos CX platform-switched Morse taper implants placed with the implant-abutment interface level with, 1 mm or 2 mm apical to the buccal alveolar crest, restored with screw-retained single crowns at 4 months
f.comparison: Implant-abutment interface at crest level (group 0) versus 1 mm (group 1) and 2 mm (group 2) apical to the buccal crest
f.main_result: At 12 months buccal bone remodeling was -0.08 mm (group 0), -0.65 mm (group 1) and -0.85 mm (group 2), with no difference in first bone-to-implant contact between groups.
f.funding_coi: Sponsored by DENTSPLY Implants Manufacturing; authors reported no conflicts of interest

f.population: 428 patients with 898 internal conical connection implants (Oneplant FIT, Warantec) treated 2006-2014 at Seoul National University Dental Hospital
f.intervention: Implant-supported metal-ceramic restorations (cement- or screw-retained, titanium or gold components) on internal conical connection implants
f.comparison: Risk indicators compared within the cohort: location, splinting, screw material, sex, implant diameter
f.main_result: Mechanical complications occurred in 47.9% of implants (screw loosening 46.4%, abutment fracture 11.4%); molars and male sex raised risk, splinting and gold screws (for loosening) lowered it.
materials_brands: Oneplant FIT (Warantec) internal conical connection implant
f.funding_coi: Korea Medical Device Development Fund grant (Korean government ministries)

f.population: Four designs of direct-to-implant BTI butt-joint restorations (specimens)
f.intervention: Axial fatigue tests per ISO 14801 varying implant body diameter, platform diameter and internal vs external connection
f.comparison: Pairwise comparison of 4.5 vs 5.5 mm body, 4.1 vs 5.5 mm platform, internal vs external connection
f.main_result: A 1 mm larger body diameter gave about 3.5-fold and a 1.4 mm larger platform about 7-fold longer screw fatigue life, with no significant difference between internal and external connections.
materials_brands: BTI implants with Ti CP4 bodies and Ti6Al4V ELI prosthetic screws
f.limitations: Platform-diameter comparison relied on linear extrapolation of the fatigue model

f.population: 18 patients with edentulous mandibles (107 implants)
f.intervention: Immediate loading of three ANKYLOS plus implants on one side, splinted with a cemented provisional prosthesis
f.comparison: Certain PREVAIL implants (B-implants) placed on the contralateral side
f.main_result: At 24 months bone loss of at least 2 mm occurred at 11% of A-implants versus 70% of B-implants, a success rate of 88.63% versus 29.78%.

f.population: 85 patients with 228 delayed-loaded Ankylos implants
f.intervention: Subcrestal placement (shoulder at least 0.5 mm below bone crest) of platform-shifted implants
f.comparison: Crestal placement (within 0.5 mm of the crestal bone level)
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone loss
f.main_result: Mean mesial bone loss was 1.84 mm (subcrestal) versus 1.41 mm (crestal) with no significant difference (p = .130), and cumulative survival was 97.8%.
f.funding_coi: Self-supported; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Platform-shifted implants only and prosthetic components not removed; further long-term studies needed

f.population: 52 in vitro and in vivo (human and animal) studies on implant-abutment connections
f.intervention: Conical (Morse Taper) implant-abutment connection systems
f.comparison: Non-conical implant-abutment connection systems
f.main_result: Conical connections showed superiority in seal performance, micro-gap formation, torque maintenance and abutment stability in vitro, with comparable survival and in most cases less marginal bone loss in vivo.
f.funding_coi: First author supported by a Bavarian Association for Scientific Dentistry grant; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Heterogeneous data, methods and implant types precluded meta-analysis

f.population: External hexagon implants with conical abutments (in vitro assemblies)
f.intervention: Abutment tightening torques of 10, 20 and 32 Ncm with E. coli inoculation
f.comparison: Different bacterial suspension volumes (phase 1) and torque groups compared with each other
outcomes: bacterial microleakage by broth turbidity over 14 days
f.main_result: Tightening torque did not significantly affect microleakage; 2/9 T10 and 1/9 T20 samples leaked and none at 32 Ncm.
f.sample_size: 36 implant/abutment assemblies (9 in phase 1, 27 in phase 2)
materials_brands: Neodent external hexagon implants and conical abutments (3.75x11 mm)
Escherichia coli ATCC 35218 in BHI broth
f.funding_coi: Neodent donated the implants and abutments
f.limitations: In vitro methodology has limitations and operator-dependent variables should be minimized

f.population: Human osteoblastic cells in culture
f.intervention: Culture media containing Ti, Al, V, Co, Cr and Mo ions at concentrations released by platform-matched and platform-switched implant-abutment couples
f.comparison: Metal ion-free culture medium
outcomes: IL-6, IL-8, COX-2, caspase-8, OPG and RANKL expression
f.main_result: Metal ions at platform-matched concentrations reduced osteoblast viability up to 7 days, increased early apoptosis and up-regulated IL-6, IL-8, COX-2 and RANKL dose-dependently, most strongly for platform-matched couples.
materials_brands: Ti6Al4V and cobalt-chrome abutment ion conditions; Lonza Clonetics NHOst osteoblasts
f.funding_coi: Funded by a King Saud University scholarship

f.population: Cast, laser-welded and milled frameworks in vitro, osteoblast-free epithelial cells and fibroblasts, and 80 implant patients
f.intervention: Cobalt-chrome frameworks (and implant-level porcelain-veneered CoCr prostheses)
f.comparison: Commercially pure titanium frameworks and acrylic-veneered abutment-level CNC-milled titanium prostheses
f.main_result: No significant difference in cumulative implant survival between implant-level CoCr/titanium prostheses and abutment-level titanium prostheses after five years (98.6% vs 97.6%).
f.sample_size: Test group n=40, control group n=40
materials_brands: Cresco CoCr and Procera CP titanium frameworks

f.population: Eight commercial dental alloys (four high-noble, two noble, two base metal)
f.intervention: Electrochemical polarization resistance and static immersion elemental-release tests in acidified artificial saliva
f.main_result: Polarization resistance and elemental release were inversely correlated (R2 = 0.886; F about 44 vs critical F 13.7).

f.population: Seven dental alloys coupled with titanium and Ti6Al4V implant specimens
f.intervention: Electrochemical measurement of galvanic coupling in artificial salivas plus Auger surface analysis
f.main_result: All implant-alloy couples showed very low galvanic corrosion rates, confirmed by surface analysis.

f.population: 198 patients with 270 implant-supported fixed prostheses on 1117 implants
f.intervention: Cast cobalt-chromium frameworks veneered with ceramic or prefabricated acrylic teeth
f.comparison: Type 3 gold alloy frameworks veneered with ceramic or acrylic
f.main_result: Success, survival and complication rates were similar for cobalt-chromium and type 3 gold frameworks, and biomaterial combination did not influence implant survival.

f.population: Titanium discs coupled with dental alloys (gold-based, palladium-based, non-precious) in artificial saliva
f.intervention: Galvanic coupling of titanium with 15 types of dental alloy, measuring electrochemical parameters
f.main_result: Galvanic currents remained low for all couples; Ti/gold and Ti/palladium couples caused negligible galvanism with no crevice-corrosion risk, while Ti/non-precious couples risked crevice corrosion.
f.funding_coi: Metalor Metaux Precieux SA provided the laboratory and materials

f.main_result: Titanium in the oral environment can degrade progressively by combined wear and corrosion (tribocorrosion), affecting implant and prosthesis performance and releasing potentially toxic debris and ions.

f.population: Eight CAD/CAM implant bars (six Co-Cr, two titanium) milled from the same design on reproduction casts of a mandibular edentulous master cast with four implants
f.intervention: Profilometric roughness measurement of three regions of each bar and dental technicians' rating of rework time and quality
f.comparison: Bars from different manufacturers (laboratory vs central production) compared with each other
outcomes: surface roughness (Sa, Ra) in transmucosal, labial and basal regions
f.main_result: Three centrally produced bars (ZDC, ZST, ZCC) had acceptable transmucosal roughness and little rework, while four bars needed extensive manual rework; the LAC bar was up to 7 times (Sa) and 8 times (Ra) rougher than ZST.
f.sample_size: 8 bars (6 Co-Cr, 2 titanium), 3 areas measured per region, 8 dental technicians
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: One leading academic expert in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery or Oral Surgery per European country
f.intervention: Anonymous online 10-item survey on safety of dental settings, PPE and patient-related measures during COVID-19
outcomes: settings for treating COVID-19 positive patients
f.main_result: Transmission risk of SARS-CoV-2 for aerosol-generating procedures was rated high by 25 of 27 experts; all recommended limiting aerosol-generating procedures and hand hygiene for patients.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest

f.population: Staff, air and surfaces of two Ohio dental practices (one general, one pediatric)
f.intervention: Air and surface sampling and staff nasopharyngeal swabs tested for pH1N1 and seasonal influenza viruses, plus a flu symptom survey
outcomes: influenza virus in air and surface samples
f.main_result: No pH1N1 virus was found in any air or surface sample; seasonal influenza A (H3N2) was found in air near exam chairs at the pediatric practice on one visit.
f.sample_size: Two practices; 48 air samples at each practice, 52 and 54 surface swabs
f.follow_up: Four visits per practice over 6 weeks
f.limitations: Methods could not determine whether detected viruses were viable

f.population: 28 adults seeking dental treatment at Ohio State University College of Dentistry
f.intervention: Aerosols collected during ultrasonic scaling, implant osteotomy and restorative procedures, analysed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and 16S sequencing with source tracking
outcomes: microbiota composition of aerosol vs saliva
f.main_result: 78% of the microbiota in aerosol condensate came from the dental irrigant and saliva contributed a median of 0%; SARS-CoV-2 found in saliva of 19 participants was undetectable in aerosol.
f.funding_coi: No financial support

f.main_result: COVID-19 has had many immediate complications for dentistry, with possible long-term effects on clinical practice, dental education and dental research.
f.funding_coi: No special funding; no conflict of interest

f.main_result: Interim ADA recommendations cover patient screening, reception, chairside and staff protection measures for resuming non-emergent care during COVID-19.
f.limitations: It is interim, short-term guidance and details not addressed are left to each dentist's judgment

f.population: European national dental COVID-19 guidelines (EU countries, Switzerland, UK, Scotland) and European academic oral surgery experts
f.intervention: Consensus statements on infection control and prevention in dentistry derived from a guideline comparison and an experts' follow-up survey
f.main_result: All 27 EU countries plus Switzerland, UK and Scotland published adapted dental ICP guidelines, with a lack of quality control of cited literature; experts scored overall transmission risk lower in the second wave but AGP risk still high.
f.sample_size: 26 of 27 contacted European experts responded to the follow-up survey
f.limitations: Authors note that the guidelines lacked solid scientific evidence and were frequently not uniform.

f.population: 27 leading European academic experts in Oral (and Maxillofacial) Surgery, 26 of whom responded
f.intervention: Anonymous online 14-item questionnaire on dental setting safety, PPE and patient-related measures during the second COVID-19 wave
f.comparison: First survey (April-May 2020)
f.main_result: Overall transmission risk was scored significantly lower than in the first survey, though AGP risk was still considered high; most experts still recommended FFP2/FFP3 masks (80.8%) and face shields or goggles (88.5%) for AGP.
f.follow_up: Data collected November 2020 to February 2021, about 7 months after the first survey
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: National COVID-19 dental infection-control guidelines from EU countries, Switzerland, UK and Scotland
f.intervention: Summary of recommendations on triage, mouth rinse, PPE and treatment of potentially infectious patients
f.comparison: Recommendations from international organizations (WHO, ECDC, CDC)
outcomes: PPE recommendations for AGP and non-AGP
f.main_result: All 30 countries recommended triage and postponing non-urgent care; hydrogen peroxide 1-1.5% was the most recommended mouth rinse (24/30); FFP2/FFP3 masks (25/30) and face shields (24/30) for AGP.
f.sample_size: 52 national guidance documents from 30 countries plus 5 from ECDC, WHO and CDC
f.funding_coi: Self-funded by the authors; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Guideline quality of cited references was not assessed and missing data do not mean a measure was not recommended

f.intervention: Infection control measures in dental practice: patient evaluation, hand hygiene, PPE, mouthrinse, rubber dam, anti-retraction handpiece, clinic disinfection, waste management
f.main_result: 2019-nCoV spreads through droplets, contact, saliva and contaminated surfaces, so dental practice carries high exposure risk and needs layered infection control measures.
f.funding_coi: Sichuan University emergency project; no competing interests

f.intervention: Disinfection and sterilization of patient-care items by Spaulding risk category
Special infection-control precautions in dental care during the COVID-19 outbreak (screening, hand hygiene, PPE, pre-procedural rinse, rubber dam, air filtration, surface disinfection)
f.main_result: Most dental procedures generate droplets and aerosols that risk transmission; the review proposes special precautions beyond standard ones, e.g. pre-procedural mouth rinse reduced dental aerosol CFU by a mean 68.4% and rubber dam cut microbial spread by 90%.
f.funding_coi: Zhejiang Province science foundation; authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: Disc-shaped Y-TZP zirconia specimens, 60 per material (fine and coarse grained)
f.intervention: Dry grinding, wet grinding, sandblasting, and their sequential combinations
f.comparison: As-sintered control group
f.main_result: Sandblasting significantly increased flexural strength in both materials, grinding reduced strength of fine grained Y-TZP, and all surface treatments lowered the Weibull modulus.
materials_brands: Tosoh TZ-3YB and TZ-3YSB Y-TZP powders

f.population: Laboratory ultrasonic scaler on a ceramic plate and scaler/drill use in clinic on a dental mannequin
f.intervention: Irrigation water made viscoelastic with high molecular weight polymer additives (PAA, xanthan gum)
f.comparison: Plain water irrigation
f.main_result: Viscoelastic polymer additives markedly suppressed or completely eliminated aerosol from the ultrasonic scaler and dental handpiece compared with water.
f.funding_coi: UIC College of Dentistry discretionary funds; provisional patent application filed

f.population: Manikin simulation with E. coli aerosol, then 24 dental procedures (14 restorative, 10 ultrasonic scaling) on human subjects
f.intervention: Modified extra-oral vacuum aspirator made from a household vacuum cleaner
f.comparison: Same procedures without the EOVA running
f.main_result: The modified EOVA significantly reduced both E. coli aerosol (mean 29.26 vs 17.26 CFU) and oral bacterial aerosol during scaling and restorative work.
f.sample_size: 24 procedures on human subjects plus 38 manikin estimations
materials_brands: 1,100 W wet-dry-blow household vacuum cleaner modified as EOVA

f.population: 80 patients with chronic generalized periodontitis undergoing ultrasonic scaling
f.intervention: Piezoelectric ultrasonic scaling with a high-volume evacuator
f.comparison: Scaling without high-volume evacuator
outcomes: colony forming units on agar plates at 12 and 20 inches
f.main_result: No significant CFU difference with vs without the high-volume evacuator (11.08 vs 12.14, P=0.248).
f.limitations: Authors acknowledge the findings hold within the limitations of the study; HVE tested as a separate unit without modification.

f.population: Twelve adult subjects scaled in a split-mouth design
f.intervention: Ultrasonic scaling for 5 minutes with an aerosol reduction device (high-volume suction tube on the scaler handle)
f.comparison: Ultrasonic scaling for 5 minutes without the device
outcomes: CFU on blood agar 6 inches from mouth
f.main_result: Mean CFU 6 inches from the mouth were 45.1 without vs 2.6 with the device (P<0.001); face-shield CFU did not differ.

f.population: Dental clinics (three) with patient episodes for four procedures
f.intervention: Commercial Air Cleaning System (ACS) operated before and during treatment
f.comparison: Same procedures without ACS operation
f.main_result: ACS lowered mean bioaerosol, e.g. 23.9 vs 105.1 cfu/m3 for cavity preparation and 41.9 vs 70.9 for ultrasonic scaling.
f.sample_size: 5-9 bioaerosol samples per treatment; 15 baseline samples

f.population: 45 male patients with localized mild to moderate chronic periodontitis
f.intervention: Scaling and root planing plus 1.5% hydrogen peroxide mouthwash twice daily for 10 days
f.comparison: SRP alone, and SRP plus 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate mouthwash twice daily for 10 days
f.main_result: Both mouthwashes reduced the gingival index more than SRP alone and similar to each other; pocket depth reduction was 38.09% with CHX, 24.77% with H2O2 and 21.30% with SRP alone.
materials_brands: Colgate Peroxyl Mouth Sore Rinse (1.5% H2O2)
f.funding_coi: Funded by Al Jouf University; no conflicts of interest

f.population: 68 ICU patients
f.intervention: 3% hydrogen peroxide mouthwash twice a day
f.comparison: 0.9% normal saline mouthwash twice a day
f.main_result: VAP occurred in 14.7% of the hydrogen peroxide group versus 38.2% of the saline group (RR 2.60, 95% CI 1.04-6.49).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Bronchoalveolar lavage was not used for VAP diagnosis, and ventilator settings and oral health were not assessed.

outcomes: safety of hydrogen peroxide in oral hygiene and bleaching
f.main_result: Daily 3% H2O2 use for up to 6 years caused only occasional transitory irritation in a few subjects with preexisting ulceration.

f.intervention: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) as an office disinfectant against the CoVID-19 virus
f.main_result: The review concludes HOCl can be used with high predictability to disinfect against the CoVID-19 virus.

f.population: Klebsiella pneumoniae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, influenza A (H1N1) and rotavirus in suspension tests
f.intervention: 7% PVP-I gargle/mouthwash diluted 1:30 (0.23% PVP-I), contact time from 15 s
f.comparison: Untreated control with distilled water in place of product
f.main_result: At 0.23% PVP-I all viral titres fell by 4.40 to 6.00 log10 TCID50/ml within 15 s, and bacteria by more than 5 log10.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Mundipharma Research; one author is an MRG employee

f.population: COVID-19 patients and the healthcare workers attending them (proposed protocol)
f.intervention: Protocolised intra-nasal and oral application of povidone-iodine
f.main_result: The authors recommend considering immediate PVP-I use in healthcare workers and patients as an adjunct to PPE, based on in vitro virucidal evidence.
f.limitations: The proposal extrapolates in vitro findings to the in vivo setting.

f.population: Periodontally healthy patients with thick gingival biotype and intact buccal bone wall, single failing tooth in aesthetic zone (15-25)
f.intervention: Single immediate implant with flapless surgery, DBBM socket grafting and immediate provisional crown
f.comparison: Outcomes at 5 years compared with 10 years
f.main_result: Mean outcomes were stable between 5 and 10 years, but six implants (33%) showed 1 mm or more mid-facial recession.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; Nobel Biocare Belgium supplied free materials; one author has collaboration agreements with Nobel Biocare and Straumann

f.population: 47 patients with a single implant in the anterior region
f.intervention: Implant provisional and crown with a convex emergence profile
f.comparison: Concave-profile provisional and crown, and a control with no provisional
f.main_result: Recession frequency was 64.3% (convex), 14.3% (concave) and 31.4% (control); a convex profile had an odds ratio of 12.6 for recession versus concave.
f.sample_size: 47 patients with 47 implants; 44 available at 12 months
materials_brands: OsseoSpeed EV implants (Astra Tech, Dentsply Sirona)
f.funding_coi: Funded by the University of Zurich clinic, SSRD and Dentsply Sirona Implants; no conflict declared

f.population: 25 single maxillary anterior implant sites (patients aged 23-38, thick biotype)
f.intervention: Two-stage adaptive pressure contouring with a screw-retained interim restoration
f.comparison: Gingiva of the adjacent natural tooth as colour reference
outcomes: gingival colour change (L*a*b*, delta E) over 15 minutes
f.main_result: Peri-implant mucosa blanching recovered within 10 minutes, with colour difference from the adjacent tooth within the acceptable 3.7 limit.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 169 patients with 349 implants treated at Seoul National University Dental Hospital 2002-2012
f.intervention: Radiographic assessment of prosthetic features (emergence angle, emergence profile, crown/implant ratio, splinted position) at 1 and 5 years after prosthesis insertion
f.comparison: Emergence angle <30 vs >=30 degrees; concave/straight/convex profile; single vs splinted positions
f.main_result: Peri-implantitis prevalence was higher with emergence angle >=30 degrees, convex profile and implants splinted to both neighbours in bone-level implants; crown/implant ratio had no effect.
f.funding_coi: Seoul National University Dental Hospital Research Fund; no conflict of interest declared

f.intervention: Abutment and crown contour modifications in critical and subcritical zones of implant restorations
f.main_result: Alteration of critical or subcritical contour can modify the peri-implant soft tissue profile; only subcritical contour changes enhance soft tissue without altering crown shape.
f.limitations: The authors state the findings are preliminary observations and the exact critical-contour dimension is yet to be determined.

f.population: Randomly selected Swedish patients provided with implant-supported restorative therapy in 2003 (2,765 patient files; 596 examined clinically)
f.intervention: Implant-supported restorative therapy provided in routine care by over 800 clinicians; early and late implant loss assessed
outcomes: patient and implant factors associated with loss
f.main_result: Early implant loss occurred in 4.4% of patients (1.4% of implants) and late loss in 4.2% of examined patients (2.0% of implants); 7.6% of examined patients lost at least 1 implant.
f.sample_size: 2,765 patients (11,311 implants) from files; 596 patients (2,367 implants) examined
f.funding_coi: Swedish Social Insurance Agency, Swedish Research Council, TUA research Gothenburg and Swedish Dental Society; some authors report fees from Dentsply Implants IH

f.population: 15 3D-printed mandibular models with missing first molar and single implant analog, cleaned by 30 volunteers (periodontists, hygienists, laypersons)
f.intervention: Cleaning of artificial biofilm from implant crowns with five interdental cleaning aids
f.comparison: Concave (15 degrees), straight (30 degrees) and convex (45 degrees) crown contours; different cleaning tools
f.main_result: Concave crowns had the greatest artificial biofilm removal; dental floss (43.0%) and superfloss (42.5%) were the most effective tools and none removed all biofilm.
f.funding_coi: Rackham Graduate Student Research Grant; no financial interests in the tested products
f.limitations: Only three crown contours were tested in vitro with artificial biofilm, so results cannot be generalized to real clinical scenarios.

f.population: Three clinical cases of patients with overcontoured implant crowns and peri-implantitis or high risk of it
