outcomes: influence of initial buccal plate width
f.main_result: About 0.5 mm mean loss in height and width at 6 months, with no significant difference between flap and flapless.

f.population: Patients needing extraction of premolar or molar teeth and later implant
f.intervention: Ridge preservation with porcine bone and collagen membrane using a flapless procedure with secondary soft tissue closure (test)
f.comparison: Same ridge preservation with full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap and primary soft tissue closure (control)
f.main_result: No histological or histomorphometric difference between flap and flapless: new bone 22.5% vs 22.5%, marrow spaces 59.3% vs 59.4%, residual graft 18.6% vs 18.2%.
f.follow_up: 3 months to bone biopsy at implant placement

f.population: Six Labrador dogs, implants in distal alveoli of second mandibular premolars
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement without flap elevation (flapless, test site)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with full-thickness mucoperiosteal flap (control site)
outcomes: remaining gap between implant and socket wall
f.main_result: Buccal crest resorption was 1.7 mm (flap) and 1.5 mm (flapless), with no significant differences between approaches.

f.population: Patients with a non-restorable single tooth in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Flapless immediate implant placement with provisionalization
f.comparison: Flap-involving immediate implant placement with provisionalization
f.main_result: Flap elevation caused more mesial and distal gingival margin recession at 3 months (p=0.02 and p=0.01), with no other significant differences up to 12 months.
f.funding_coi: Implants and abutments supplied free by Biomet 3i; conflict of interest: none

f.population: Adults needing a single maxillary anterior or premolar tooth extraction with intact buccal plate
f.intervention: Immediate implant with minimal split-thickness envelope flap (MSTEF), with GBR and connective tissue graft
f.comparison: Immediate implant with conventional flap (control)
f.main_result: No significant differences between flap and MSTEF: PES 10.54 vs 10.80, WES 6.97 vs 6.95, survival and success 100%; esthetic failures were common in both groups.

f.population: Adult patients with a single immediate implant in incisor, cuspid or premolar position
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement without flap elevation (flapless)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with flap elevation
outcomes: papillary and midfacial soft tissue change
f.main_result: Flapless surgery gave 0.48 mm less horizontal buccal bone change (95% CI 0.13-0.84, p = .007) with no difference in implant survival (RR 1.00).
f.sample_size: 5 RCTs, 140 patients with 140 implants (68 flapless, 72 flap)
f.limitations: Scarce data prevented meta-analysis of secondary outcomes; three RCTs at high risk of bias.

f.population: Eight beagle dogs, mandibular premolar sockets with thin buccal bone
f.intervention: Flapless extraction with socket filled with deproteinized bovine bone mineral (MinerOss X), no membrane
f.comparison: Sockets left with a blood clot only
outcomes: socket composition (bone, connective tissue, residual graft)
f.main_result: Grafted sockets had a better buccal crest level (0.09 vs 0.51 mm apical to lingual), wider ridge (5.08 vs 3.88 mm) and more total bone (73.51% vs 45.84%) than blood clot sockets.
materials_brands: MinerOss X (BioHorizons) deproteinized bovine bone mineral
f.funding_coi: CNPq and FAPESP funding; BioHorizons donated the graft material

f.population: Three beagle dogs with surgically created dehiscence defects around implants
f.intervention: Bilayer bone augmentation: autogenous particulated bone inner layer plus xenogenous bone outer layer
f.comparison: Autograft alone, xenograft alone, and untreated control
f.main_result: Mean bone volume was 11.08 mm3 (xenograft), 10.42 mm3 (BBA), 8.1 mm3 (control) and 7.01 mm3 (autograft) with no significant difference between the 4 groups.
f.sample_size: 19 implants analysed in 3 dogs (24 sites planned)
f.funding_coi: No financial conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Preliminary study; larger sample size required

f.intervention: Bone grafting of the buccal gap at immediate implant placement, with membrane, flapless, socket shield and immediate dentoalveolar restoration options
f.main_result: Grafting the buccal void preserves, at least in part, ridge dimensions after immediate implant placement, mainly in the anterior maxilla; no graft material is clearly superior and membranes do not seem to improve outcomes in intact sockets.
f.limitations: Evidence for immediate dentoalveolar restoration is limited and needs controlled studies.

f.population: Eight beagle dogs with surgically created semi-saddle peri-implant bone defects
f.intervention: GBR with equine bone block + collagen membrane, bovine DBBM block + CM, or particulated DBBM + CM
f.comparison: Empty control defects
outcomes: horizontal thickness of augmented region and mucosa
f.main_result: All GBR groups gave larger augmented area than empty control (equine block 11.2, DBBM block 9.5, particulated DBBM 7.9 vs 2.4 mm2), with no significant differences between GBR groups.
materials_brands: Bio-Oss granules and Bio-Oss spongiosa block (Geistlich)
f.funding_coi: University of Zurich clinic plus a research grant from Geistlich Pharma

f.population: 18 patients needing single tooth replacement in compromised maxillary esthetic-zone sockets
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate dentoalveolar restoration (IDR) of facial bone defects using maxillary tuberosity graft
f.main_result: Mean soft tissue dimension was 12.85 mm at baseline and 12.79 mm at final follow-up (no recession), and papillary heights increased slightly.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 61 patients receiving immediate implants in fresh extraction sockets with intact buccal bone
f.intervention: Static guided immediate implant placement with R2Gate teeth-supported surgical guides
f.comparison: Freehand immediate implant placement
f.main_result: Static guided surgery had lower crestal mesiodistal (0.34 vs 1.13 mm) and angular deviation (0.83 vs 6.09 degrees) than freehand; depth deviation did not differ (p=0.09).
f.follow_up: Implant position scanned 6 weeks after placement
materials_brands: R2Gate surgical guides and Anyridge implants (Megagen)

f.population: Patients receiving dental implants, studies reporting planned versus placed implant position
f.intervention: Computer-aided implant surgery (pilot-drill, partially and fully guided static, and dynamic navigation)
f.comparison: Freehand implant placement
f.main_result: Mean angular, entry and apex deviations were 7.46 deg, 1.56 mm and 2.22 mm for freehand versus 2.57 deg, 0.72 mm and 0.88 mm for fully guided static CAIS.
f.sample_size: 55 studies in the data extraction/meta-analysis (1609 initial articles)

f.population: 18 patients needing posterior implant-supported single crowns
f.intervention: Digitally static guided implant placement 1 mm subcrestal by a non-expert operator
f.comparison: Freehand placement by a skilled operator
outcomes: marginal bone level change at 3 years
f.main_result: The difference in marginal bone level change between guided and freehand groups was 0.11 mm at 3 years, not statistically significant (p=0.61).

f.population: Patients in 10 RCTs receiving implants by static computer-aided, partially guided or free-handed placement
f.intervention: Static computer-aided implant placement (sCAIP)
f.comparison: Partially guided (PGIP) and free-handed (FHIP) implant placement
f.main_result: sCAIP had lower angular (MD 4.41 deg), coronal (0.65 mm) and apical (1.13 mm) deviation than free-handed placement, and lower angular deviation than partially guided placement (MD 2.11 deg).
f.sample_size: 10 RCTs (14 articles); 8 studies, 383 patients, 878 implants in the main accuracy comparison
f.follow_up: Survival assessed up to 12 months post-loading

f.population: 41 patients undergoing extraction of all remaining teeth for full-arch fixed implant prostheses
f.intervention: Implants placed immediately into fresh extraction sockets
f.comparison: Implants placed in healed bone
f.main_result: Success rate was 97.8% in both immediate and non-immediate groups, with no significant difference.
f.sample_size: 512 implants in 41 patients (93 immediate, 419 in healed bone)
f.limitations: Immediate-placement sample was significantly smaller than the healed-bone sample

f.population: 13 patients (20 teeth with infection) scheduled for single-rooted tooth extraction
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement in infected fresh sockets with bone graft and membrane
f.main_result: All 20 implants osseointegrated with no infection at 12 months; mean CAL 0.8 to 0.9 mm and DIB increased 0.5 mm.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Hypothesis must be verified by additional comparative trials

f.population: 28 patients (33 immediate implants) with posterior compromised sockets
f.intervention: Reactive soft tissue raised as pedicled primary wound closure over the implant
f.comparison: Reactive soft tissue elevated but failed to cover the site
outcomes: buccal and lingual bone height and width (CBCT)
f.main_result: 100% implant survival; buccal bone height loss 0.80 vs 1.78 mm (EG vs CG, P=.018) and keratinized mucosa recession 0.78 vs 1.65 mm (P=.021); MBL did not differ.
f.funding_coi: Funded by National Natural Science Foundation of China and National Key R&D Program; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Small patient group; larger and longer studies needed

f.intervention: A three-type (A, B, C) classification of molar extraction sockets with treatment protocols for immediate implants
f.main_result: Immediate implants can be placed predictably in molar sockets when primary stability is achievable within septal bone (types A, B) or by engaging the socket periphery (type C); otherwise a delayed protocol is used.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest

f.population: 82 patients (42 males, 40 females) needing molar extraction, recruited in 8 centers
f.intervention: Immediate transmucosal placement of tapered implants (4.8 mm, shoulder 6.5 mm) into molar sockets with GBR of marginal defects
outcomes: mesial and distal crestal bone level change
f.main_result: All 82 implants healed uneventfully (100% survival) with healthy soft tissue at 12 months; crestal bone levels changed significantly from baseline (P<0.0001).

f.population: 30 subjects: 15 with molar extraction sockets with buccal dehiscence (test) and 15 with healed molar sites (control)
f.intervention: Immediate transmucosal tapered implants in molar sockets with buccal dehiscence, treated with GBR
f.comparison: Implants in healed molar sites with intact buccal walls
f.main_result: All 30 implants survived (100%); PPD and CAL were significantly higher at test sites than control sites (e.g. buccal PPD 3.7 vs 2.2 mm).

f.population: 139 patients with implants in premolar/molar region adjacent to a tooth, loaded at least 3 years
f.intervention: Vertical implant position more than 3 mm apical to the CEJ of the adjacent tooth
f.comparison: Vertical position 3 mm or less from the CEJ
outcomes: peri-implant marginal bone loss (mesial and distal)
f.main_result: Implants placed more than 3 mm apical to the adjacent CEJ had 0.57 mm (mesial) and 0.83 mm (distal) more peri-implant bone loss.
f.funding_coi: Grant from the American Academy of Implant Dentistry Foundation; no financial interests declared

f.population: 26 patients with single-tooth implants in the anterior maxilla (52 papillae)
f.intervention: Modified uncovering technique designed to generate papilla-like formation
f.comparison: Standard uncovering technique
outcomes: distance from contact point to bone crest
f.main_result: Papilla present almost 100% of the time when contact point to bone crest was 5 mm or less, and 50% or less when 6 mm or more.
f.follow_up: mean 35 months since crown insertion (6 to 75)
f.limitations: Small sample prevented statistical analysis

f.population: 40 patients with single-tooth implants in the anterior maxilla and a natural contralateral tooth
f.intervention: Single-tooth implants in anterior maxilla, analysed for factors affecting mucosal and papilla level (observational)
f.comparison: Natural contralateral tooth
f.main_result: Thin biotype was the most significant factor for apical facial mucosal level; increased contact point to bone crest distance was the only factor associated with less papilla fill (half or more fill in 89%).
f.follow_up: implants in function for at least 6 months
f.funding_coi: Supported by the 90th Anniversary of Chulalongkorn University Fund
f.limitations: Cross-sectional design; mucosal level referenced to contralateral tooth; factors analysed separately though inter-related

f.population: 46 patients (46 teeth) scheduled for extraction in need of single-tooth replacement
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement into fresh sockets, restored with single crowns after 4 months
f.main_result: 100% implant survival at 12 months; papilla significantly present when inter-implant-tooth distance was 3-4 mm (84.2% present) and contact point to bone distance 3-5 mm.

f.population: Patients (10 or more per study) with a single implant-supported crown in the anterior maxilla, at least 12 months follow-up
f.intervention: Single implant-supported crown; vertical distance from interproximal bone level to prosthetic contact point
outcomes: vertical distance from bone crest to contact point
f.main_result: 12 papers included; bone-to-contact-point distance ranged 2 to 11 mm and partial or complete papilla fill ranged 56.5% to 100% of cases
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Search limited to English-language articles and two databases; heterogeneous reference points prevented pooling of data

f.population: 59 titanium implants in edentulous mandibular areas of 5 foxhounds
f.intervention: Six implant types (A-F): 1-piece or 2-piece, non-submerged or submerged, with the rough/smooth border or the implant-abutment microgap at, above or below the bone crest
f.comparison: Side-by-side comparison of the six implant types (non-submerged vs submerged, 1-piece vs 2-piece)
outcomes: distance from rough/smooth border and microgap to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: In 1-piece implants the first bone-to-implant contact lay within about 0.2 mm of the rough/smooth border; in 2-piece implants the microgap position determined crestal bone loss, greatest (2.25 mm) when it lay 1 mm below the crest (type F).
f.follow_up: 6 months (abutment connection of submerged implants at 3 months)
materials_brands: Straumann grade IV commercially pure titanium implants, machined coronal part and SLA apical part
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation, Swiss Society of Periodontology, Swiss National Science Foundation and a Swiss stipend foundation; Straumann manufactured the implants

f.population: 59 titanium implants placed at different levels to the alveolar crest in 5 foxhounds
f.intervention: Six types of unloaded titanium implants (1-part or 2-part, nonsubmerged or submerged, microgap and rough/smooth interface at different levels) followed with standardized radiographs
f.comparison: Side-by-side comparison of the implant types
outcomes: distance from implant/abutment top to most coronal bone-to-implant contact (DIB)
f.main_result: In 2-part implants the most coronal bone-to-implant contact lay about 2 mm below the microgap whether non-submerged or submerged; in 1-part implants it followed the rough/smooth interface; changes occurred within the first month.
materials_brands: Straumann grade IV commercially pure titanium implants with SLA surface
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation, Swiss Society of Periodontology, Swiss National Science Foundation and a Swiss stipend foundation

f.population: Patients with at least two adjacent implant-supported crowns in the anterior maxilla (4 studies, 114 patients)
f.intervention: Multiple adjacent implant-supported crowns in the anterior maxilla
f.comparison: Radiographic horizontal distance between the outer surfaces of the two adjacent implants
f.main_result: No precise threshold for the optimal horizontal distance between adjacent implants could be defined; incomplete inter-implant mucosa fill tended to occur at distances under 3 mm in 3 of 4 studies (one significant, p = .008).
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant supported the consensus meeting
f.limitations: Few studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria and heterogeneity prevented meta-analysis

f.population: 30 partially edentulous patients receiving two adjacent implant-supported crowns (60 implants)
f.intervention: Two adjacent implants placed at a horizontal interimplant distance of about 2 mm, 3 mm or over 4 mm, restored with single crowns after 3 months
f.comparison: 2-mm vs 3-mm vs over 4-mm interimplant distance groups
outcomes: probing depth, bleeding on probing, plaque
f.main_result: No statistically significant differences in marginal and midproximal bone crest loss between the 2-mm, 3-mm and over 4-mm groups at any time point (marginal bone loss at 24 months 0.27, 0.23 and 0.44 mm).

f.population: 41 pairs of platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart in 37 patients
f.intervention: Platform-switched implants placed less than 3 mm apart, evaluated radiographically
outcomes: height of the interimplant bone peak relative to the line connecting implant-abutment interfaces
f.main_result: Mean vertical bone resorption was 0.62 mm and horizontal 0.60 mm; the interimplant bone peak stayed on average 0.24 mm above the line connecting the two implant-abutment interfaces (preserved in 64% of pairs).

f.intervention: Four-dimensional (timing) concept and classification of extraction sites for immediate implant placement in the esthetic region
f.main_result: Timing of extraction and implant placement is added as a fourth dimension to 3D implant positioning, with a four-class site classification guiding when immediate placement is indicated.

f.population: 93 adults needing a maxillary tooth (15-25) replaced by an immediate implant
f.intervention: Immediate placement of OsseoSpeed implants in fresh extraction sockets, without additional grafting
f.comparison: Cylindrical (3.5/4.0 mm) vs conical/cylindrical (4.5/5.0 mm) implant configuration
f.main_result: After 3 years the mean gingival zenith change was 0.23 mm (not significant) and 79% mesial and 72% distal papillae were more than half-filled or complete, independent of implant configuration, tooth category, smoking and buccal wall thickness.

f.population: 40 subjects with a hopeless maxillary anterior or premolar tooth
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate provisionalization (non-occluding temporary crown)
f.comparison: Immediate placement with a healing abutment (no immediate provisionalization)
f.main_result: At 12 months mucosal level, papilla height and marginal bone changes did not differ significantly between groups; implant survival was 90% (test) vs 100% (control); immediate provisionalization did not improve the esthetic outcome.
f.follow_up: 12 months after permanent restoration (placed at 4 months)
f.funding_coi: University of Michigan Graduate Student Research Grant and a Neobiotech gift (implants provided); one author received speaking honoraria from Neobiotech
f.limitations: Two test implants failed early, possibly leaving the marginal bone analysis underpowered

f.population: 40 patients with a failing tooth in the maxillary anterior region
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement (NobelActive) with immediate provisionalization (group A)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with delayed provisionalization (group B)
f.main_result: After 5 years mean marginal bone level change was about 0.71 mm (group A) vs 0.49-0.54 mm (group B), not significantly different; implant and restoration survival was 100%.
f.sample_size: 40 patients (20 per group); 35 analysed at 5 years
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Nobel Biocare Services AG; implant materials provided
f.limitations: Fewer patients analysed at 5 years (35 of 40) reduced power; university setting with selected patients

f.population: 70 patients with a failed maxillary anterior tooth
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (screw-retained provisional crown)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement without provisionalization (healing abutment)
f.main_result: Marginal bone loss did not differ significantly between groups and survival was 100%; Group A had significantly higher ISQ at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months.

f.population: Participants with a failing tooth in the maxillary aesthetic zone needing a single implant restoration
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (IP), grafted gap, NobelActive TiUnite implant
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement with delayed provisionalization (DP) after free gingival graft closure
f.main_result: After 10 years mean mesial/distal marginal bone level change was 0.47/0.49 mm with IP and 0.58/0.41 mm with DP, with no significant difference (p = .61; p = .71)
f.funding_coi: Nobel Biocare provided implant materials/grant; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: University setting with experienced clinicians; unequal buccal defect distribution between groups and different wound closure methods in the two groups

f.population: 49 patients with a single failing tooth in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with instant connection of a provisional crown (immediate restoration)
f.comparison: Submerged healing with a removable partial denture, provisional crown after 3 months (delayed restoration)
f.main_result: Delayed restoration caused initial papilla loss and midfacial recession 2.5-3 times higher (about 0.75 mm additional loss) than immediate restoration at 1 year

f.population: Adult patients receiving single immediate implants (323 patients in 7 RCTs)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement with immediate provisionalization (IIP + IP)
f.comparison: Immediate implant placement without immediate provisionalization
f.main_result: In intact alveoli, IIP + IP gave 0.87 mm (95% CI 0.57; 1.17) less apical migration of the midfacial soft tissue than IIP alone; survival, papillae, bone level, probing depth and BOP were unaffected
f.sample_size: 7 RCTs, 323 patients with 323 single immediate implants
f.funding_coi: No conflicts declared; senior author has collaboration agreement with Nobel Biocare and Straumann
f.limitations: Risk of bias raised some concerns in five RCTs and high risk in two; GRADE strength of conclusion rated low; insufficient data for horizontal changes and PES

f.intervention: Tooth extraction without flap, 3-D implant placement, contour augmentation with connective tissue graft and heterologous bone chips, with provisionalization

f.population: 7 patients (mean age 59) with 11 Straumann SLA implants placed in soft bone without primary stability
f.intervention: Straumann tissue-level SLA implants placed with insertion torque below 10 N/cm and slight mobility, left to heal 4-6 months
f.main_result: All 11 implants lacking primary stability osseointegrated, were restored, and remained functional at a mean of 28.5 months after restoration
f.funding_coi: Authors claim no financial interest
f.limitations: Small number of implants prevented statistical analysis; short period since restoration

f.population: Patients with single dental implant restorations in eight included studies
f.intervention: Screw-retained single implant restorations
f.comparison: Cemented single implant restorations
f.main_result: BOP and MBL did not differ significantly between cemented and screw-retained implants (p = 0.8093 and 0.5813)
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Adults needing implants to replace teeth to be extracted in the maxilla, region 15-25
f.intervention: Immediate placement into the extraction socket of a cylindrical implant (group A)
f.comparison: Immediate placement of a tapered implant (group B)
outcomes: buccal and palatal crest dimension change
f.main_result: Over 16 weeks the buccal ridge dimension fell 43% (cylindrical) and 30% (tapered) and the horizontal gap closed 80% and 63%; differences between implant shapes were not significant
f.sample_size: 93 implant sites in 93 subjects (45 cylindrical, 48 tapered)

f.population: 93 subjects with single maxillary teeth (15-25) extracted and replaced by immediate implants
f.intervention: Immediate single-tooth implant placement, sites stratified by location, cause of extraction, buccal wall thickness and horizontal gap size
f.main_result: Implant location, buccal bone thickness and horizontal gap size significantly influenced hard tissue change over 4 months; premolar sites showed more gap fill and less vertical crest reduction than incisor-canine sites
f.limitations: Some stratified samples were too small, and no adjustment for multiple tests was applied

f.population: Eighteen female beagle dogs with surgically created non-contained mandibular buccal bone defects
f.intervention: Augmentation of healed defects with DBBM-collagen graft alone (T1), collagen membrane alone (T2) or both (T3)
f.comparison: The three augmentation modalities compared with each other
f.main_result: Mineralized tissue proportion was significantly larger with membrane alone (T2) than with graft alone or combined; with larger defects the graft-containing groups gave a larger total ROI
materials_brands: Bio-Gide native bilayer collagen membrane, Geistlich
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by a research contract with Geistlich Pharma AG

f.population: Eight Labrador dogs; distal alveoli of fourth mandibular premolars after hemisection
f.intervention: Implants placed immediately into extraction sockets, tilted toward the buccal wall (B-sites) or lingual wall (L-sites)
f.comparison: Buccal versus lingual implant position within the same animal (split-mouth)
f.main_result: Buccal vertical resorption was 1.6 mm at B-sites versus 0.4 mm at L-sites, and lingually placed implants were about 1 mm deeper; BIC was similar (31.2-35.2%).
materials_brands: Alvim CM implants (Neodent), sandblasted and acid-etched, 11.5 x 3.5 mm
f.funding_coi: Grant from Ariminum Research and Dental Education Center; implants provided by Neodent

f.population: 21 patients receiving single-tooth implant replacement in maxillary sites distal to the canine (27 implants, 23 biopsies)
f.intervention: Experimental abutment connected at implant placement, with soft tissue biopsies after 2, 4, 8 or 12 weeks of healing for histological and ESEM analysis
f.comparison: Different healing times (2, 4, 8, 12 weeks)
f.main_result: At 8 weeks the soft tissue was about 3.6 mm (barrier epithelium 1.9 mm, connective tissue 1.7 mm), similar at 12 weeks; differences across healing times were not significant.

f.population: 36 non-grafted immediate implant sites in the esthetic zone (maxillary second bicuspid to second bicuspid) from an RCT
f.intervention: Immediate single implant placement with immediate screw-retained provisional crown, with or without flap elevation; no bone graft
f.main_result: Gingival phenotype was the only parameter associated with both buccal gingival recession and buccal ridge dimensional reduction; mean mid-buccal recession was 0.32 mm at 12 months.
f.sample_size: 36 implants with radiographs, 34 with gingival and ridge measurements, of 39 placed
materials_brands: Super T Temporary Crown & Bridge Material (AMCO)
f.funding_coi: Implants and provisional abutments provided free by Biomet 3i; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 97 patients (60 females, 37 males; mean age 51) with a single implant in the anterior maxilla placed in 2006-2007
f.intervention: Single implant in the anterior maxilla via flap surgery with or without ridge re-contouring (GBR or onlay block grafting)
f.comparison: Surgery with versus without ridge re-contouring
f.main_result: Ridge re-contouring (OR 3.4) and pre-operative tooth bone level (OR 2.1) predicted mesial papilla recession; a buccal shoulder position predicted midfacial recession (OR 17.2).
f.follow_up: On average two and a half years of function (restorations 31 months in function)
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest; supported by the Department of Dentistry of the Free University of Brussels (VUB)

f.population: 86 subjects, one immediate implant each in the anterior maxilla (15-25)
f.intervention: Grafting the gap between implant and socket walls with demineralized bovine bone mineral with 10% collagen (Bio-Oss Collagen)
f.comparison: Immediate implants with the gap left ungrafted
f.main_result: Buccal horizontal crest reduction was 1.1 mm (29%) with DBBM-C versus 1.6 mm (38%) without graft (P = 0.02).

f.population: 113 patients needing single anterior maxillary implants: 55 in fresh sockets, 58 in healed ridges
f.intervention: Immediate provisionalization of single OsseoSpeed implants in extraction sockets
f.comparison: Implants placed in healed ridges
f.main_result: Survival was 94.6% in sockets and 98.3% in healed ridges (not significant), with mean crestal bone levels of 0.43 and 0.38 mm at 5 years.
f.sample_size: 113 patients (55 sockets, 58 healed ridges); 45 and 49 remained at 5 years
materials_brands: Bio-Gide/Bio-Mend collagen membrane (Osteohealth) for grafted sites

f.population: 38 subjects needing a single extraction (premolar to premolar), 32 completing 3-month follow-up
f.intervention: Immediate (Type 1) implant placement
f.comparison: Early (Type 2) implant placement
outcomes: probing pocket depth, modified plaque index, modified sulcus bleeding index
f.main_result: No significant differences at 3 months after crown delivery: 100% survival, mid-facial soft tissue loss about 0.5 mm in both groups, PES/WES 13.7 vs 12.5.
f.sample_size: 32 patients completed follow-up (Type 1 n = 17, Type 2 n = 15)
f.funding_coi: Other authors report no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Preliminary short-term results that need long-term confirmation

f.population: 50 periodontally healthy non-smoking patients with a failing anterior maxillary tooth (15-25) and high aesthetic risk (42 without, 8 with mid-facial recession)
f.intervention: Flapless extraction with ridge preservation (collagen-enriched bovine xenograft), flapless NobelActive implant, screw-retained provisional, connective tissue graft and permanent crown (M.I.S.I.T.)
f.main_result: At 12 months all implants survived, papillary recession was at most 0.3 mm, mid-facial recession 0.1 mm in the non-recession group, and PES/WES were 10.9/14 and 8.2/10.
f.funding_coi: Biomaterials supplied by Geistlich Pharma and components by Nobel Biocare; Cosyn has a collaboration agreement with Nobel Biocare, De Bruyn with Dentsply Implants and Southern Implants
f.limitations: Short-term prospective study offering a proof of principle

f.population: 30 patients with 30 immediate transmucosal implants in maxillary anterior extraction sites
f.intervention: Grafting the marginal defect with Bio-Oss, alone or with a resorbable collagen membrane, at non-submerged immediate implants
f.comparison: No graft (control)
outcomes: vertical defect height and horizontal defect depth reduction
f.main_result: Horizontal buccal bone resorption was 48.3% in controls versus 15.8% (BG) and 20% (BG+M); 33.3% of sites showed mucosal recession.
f.sample_size: 30 implants in 30 patients (10 per group); 19 patients followed long term
f.follow_up: 3-4 years after restoration (mean 4.0 years in 19 patients)
materials_brands: ITI Implant System, sand-blasted and acid-etched (Straumann)

f.population: Animal and human studies of implants placed immediately into sites with periapical, endodontic, perioendodontic or periodontal infection
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement into infected extraction sockets after site decontamination
f.main_result: High implant survival in several studies supports successful osseointegration after immediate placement into sites with endodontic and periodontal lesions when appropriate site decontamination is performed.
f.sample_size: 21 human case series and 7 animal studies (from 706 references, plus 5 hand-searched)
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq (Brazil); no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: More RCTs with longer follow-up are needed; infection classification was vague and varied among studies

f.population: 270 patients needing an implant-supported partial fixed prosthesis or single crown
f.intervention: Two-piece platform-switched Morse taper implants (Osseothread, ImplaDent) placed in a two-stage submerged protocol
outcomes: crestal bone level change at 60 months
influence of biological, anatomical and implant-related variables
f.main_result: At 60 months mean marginal bone remodelling was -0.59 ± 1.34 mm; bone loss was significantly higher with subcrestal and anterior implants.
materials_brands: Osseothread implants (ImplaDent), SLA surface, Morse taper connection
Ketac Cem glass ionomer cement (3M Espe)
f.funding_coi: No funds for the research

f.population: 12 male Hound Labrador mongrel dogs with surgically created critical-size supraalveolar peri-implant defects in the mandibular premolar region
f.intervention: Three 10-mm titanium implants per jaw quadrant placed 5 mm into premolar extraction sites, leaving 5 mm supraalveolar, flaps advanced for primary closure, 8 weeks healing
outcomes: buccal bone resorption (incandescent vs fluorescent microscopy)
f.main_result: Buccal bone resorption was significantly greater when the buccal ridge width was under 2 mm; the association with ridge width was about twice as strong below 2 mm (beta 1.62 vs 0.80) and fluorescence microscopy showed more resorption than incandescent light.
f.sample_size: 12 dogs, three implants in one jaw quadrant each
materials_brands: TiUnite porous oxide titanium implants (Nobel Biocare)
f.funding_coi: Co-author Jan Hall works in Research & Development at Nobel Biocare AB; no funding statement in extracted text

f.population: Animal and human studies of implants placed immediately into infected extraction sites (periapical or periodontal infection)
f.intervention: Immediate implant placement into infected sites after debridement, usually with antibiotics and GBR
f.comparison: Pristine or non-infected sites
f.main_result: Implants can be placed into infected sites with survival similar to non-infected sites, though animal data suggest bone-to-implant contact may be impaired.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Evidence limited to few studies and patients; infection classification vague.

f.population: Patients treated with implant-supported full-arch fixed prostheses at one specialist clinic (1980-2018)
f.intervention: Implant-supported full-arch fixed dental prostheses
f.main_result: Cumulative prosthesis survival was 93.3% at 10 years and 87.1% at 20 years; bruxism raised risk of failure (HR 3.276) and technical complications.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Folktandvården Skåne AB; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Retrospective design with incomplete records; non-standardized treatment and bruxism diagnosis by self-report.

f.intervention: ACP classification system (Class I-IV) for diagnosis of the completely dentate patient
f.main_result: The ACP defines four classes of completely dentate patients, from uncomplicated (Class I) to most complex (Class IV), using diagnostic criteria for tooth condition and occlusal scheme.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the American College of Prosthodontists

f.population: Patients with at least one edentulous jaw, tooth loss mainly due to periodontitis
f.intervention: Fixed or removable full-arch implant-supported prostheses
f.comparison: Fixed versus removable full-arch designs
f.main_result: Cumulative implant loss at 5 years was 1.85% for fixed versus 4.45% for removable prostheses; 1-year loss was similar (0.64% vs 0.71%).
f.follow_up: At least 12 months; analysis up to 5 years
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Limited low-quality data; no assessment beyond 5 years.

f.population: Adults with an edentulous mandible undergoing implant treatment
f.intervention: Three implants supporting a fixed mandibular prosthesis
f.comparison: Mandibular fixed complete prosthesis with more than three implants
f.main_result: Mean cumulative implant survival was 96.2% over 3.35 years, with mean marginal bone loss of 1.25 mm and high patient satisfaction.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests
f.limitations: Longer-term comparative data lacking.

f.population: Patients with complete edentulism treated with full arch immediate implants
f.intervention: Full-arch immediate implant placement and loading with PRF and i-PRF (Simonpieri technique)
f.main_result: Author reports over 98% success in full-arch immediate loading with PRF over 14 years.

f.population: Critical-sized dehiscence defects in mandibular canines of dogs
f.intervention: β-TCP alloplast with modified perforated collagen membrane
f.comparison: β-TCP alloplast with occlusive collagen membrane
f.main_result: Both groups regenerated periodontal tissues, but the perforated membrane gave higher bone surface area (70.9% vs 44.5% at 1 month; 82.5% vs 73.2% at 2 months).
materials_brands: BioTECK equine type I collagen membrane
f.limitations: Small sample; further larger studies needed.

f.population: Mouse ST2 bone marrow stromal cells (osteoblast lineage) in culture
f.intervention: DBBM particles pre-coated with bone-conditioned medium (BCM)
f.comparison: DBBM particles alone
f.main_result: BCM coating increased cell adhesion 2-fold, raised COL1A2, ALP and OCN mRNA, and gave 3-fold more alizarin red staining.
f.funding_coi: DBBM supplied by Geistlich AG; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: In vitro only; animal study needed.

f.population: Patients receiving posterior implants with small non-contained buccal bone dehiscences (≤5 mm)
f.intervention: Spontaneous healing of the dehiscence
f.comparison: Guided bone regeneration (DBBM + collagen membrane)
f.main_result: Survival was 100% in both groups at 7.5 years; remaining buccal dehiscence was larger with spontaneous healing (2.51 mm) than GBR (1.66 mm, p=0.02), with no difference in marginal bone levels.
f.sample_size: 22 patients with 28 implants; 20 patients with 26 implants recalled
materials_brands: Deproteinized bovine bone mineral with collagen membrane (GBR group)
f.funding_coi: Implant material from Oral Reconstruction Foundation grant; three authors report grants and fees from Geistlich Pharma outside the work
f.limitations: No power calculation possible due to lack of data

f.population: Experimental (mostly animal) studies of bone regeneration with cortical perforations in the recipient area
f.intervention: Cortical perforations combined with GBR, autologous bone blocks or periosteal distraction
f.main_result: Evidence that cortical perforations increase bone formation in GBR and with bone blocks is limited; number and size of perforations did not appear to matter.
f.funding_coi: No funding source declared
f.limitations: Moderate to high risk of bias; studies not comparable.

f.population: Murine bone marrow cell cultures exposed to conditioned medium from porcine fresh cortical bone and demineralized bone matrix
f.intervention: Conditioned medium from fresh bone (BCM, also heated to 85°C) and from demineralized bone matrix (DCM) added to RANKL and M-CSF induced osteoclastogenesis
f.comparison: Cultures with RANKL and M-CSF alone, and unheated BCM
outcomes: osteoclast marker and fusion gene expression
f.main_result: Unheated BCM did not change osteoclastogenesis, heated BCM approximately doubled TRAP-positive multinucleated cells, and DCM significantly stimulated osteoclastogenesis irrespective of heating.
f.sample_size: Experiments repeated at least four times in duplicate
materials_brands: Porcine cortical bone chips (BCM) and demineralized bone matrix (DCM)
f.limitations: Most but not all preparations of heated BCM supported osteoclastogenesis, and the resorption assay was not quantified because of large variation.

f.population: Patients with a single tooth gap in the anterior maxilla and a horizontal alveolar defect, bucco-palatal bone at least 6 mm
f.intervention: Single implant with CTG in a buccal envelope to re-establish buccal convexity (test)
f.comparison: Single implant with GBR using DBBM (Bio-Oss) and a collagen membrane (control)
f.main_result: PES did not differ (10.11 GBR vs 10.48 CTG, p=0.577) but MSI was lower with CTG (1.10 vs 2.53, p=0.017); GBR had more oedema, hematoma and painkillers (7.10 vs 4.86).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; implants and prosthetic components supplied free by Nobel Biocare; Prof. Cosyn has agreements with Nobel Biocare and Straumann.

f.population: Patients with severe vertical alveolar atrophy and missing teeth needing vertical bone augmentation for implants
f.intervention: Self-inflating hydrogel tissue expander (TissueMax) placed subperiosteally for ~4 weeks, then tunneling vertical bone graft without full flap reflection
f.comparison: Conventional vertical GBR with full flap and periosteal releasing incisions
outcomes: radiographic vertical bone gain and retention
f.main_result: Vertical bone gain was higher with the expander (5.12 vs 4.22 mm, P<0.05) and 6-month vertical bone reduction was smaller (30.7% vs 55.0%); mean soft tissue gain was 6.88 mm vertically.
f.follow_up: 6-month retention after grafting, then mean 10.2 months of prosthetic loading
materials_brands: Cytoplast RTM collagen membrane (Osteogenics) and OssMem (Osstem)
Cytoplast Ti-250XL d-PTFE titanium reinforced membrane
Straumann bone level SLActive and Osstem TS III SA implants
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared; supported by a Korea Health Technology R&D Project grant (Ministry of Health & Welfare); some authors affiliated with Osstem Bio R&D Center.
f.limitations: Studies comparing the two techniques without tissue expanders are needed to elucidate the net effect of tissue expansion.

f.population: In vitro: bone chips from fresh pig mandibles and human mesenchymal cells (oral fibroblasts)
f.intervention: Preparation of bone-conditioned medium from native, pasteurized, autoclaved or demineralized pig bone and a bioassay on TGF-b regulated gene expression
f.comparison: Un-stimulated controls and medium from autoclaved (121 °C) bone
outcomes: expression of ADM, PTX3, IL11, IL33, NOX4 and PRG4 in oral fibroblasts
f.main_result: BCM from fresh, pasteurized or demineralized bone changed target gene expression (ADM and PTX3 down to 0.4-fold, IL11, IL33, NOX4, PRG4 up to 200-fold), whereas medium from autoclaved bone did not.
f.funding_coi: Authors have nothing to disclose; one author received a scholarship from the Foundation of Dental Research and Education, Basel.
f.limitations: BCM cannot be fully standardized because of variations between donors and harvesting techniques.

f.population: Four young adult mongrel dogs, membranes placed subperiosteally in the maxilla
f.intervention: Subperiosteal placement of three membranes: bovine collagen (GenDerm), collagen (Genoss, Dentium) and porcine dermis (Kytinon M.O.R.)
f.comparison: The three membranes compared with each other, and with normal gingival tissue samples
f.main_result: Absorption was <35% at 15 days for all membranes; at 90 days GenDerm bovine collagen was completely absorbed, Dentium collagen >65% and porcine dermis only 35-65%.
f.funding_coi: Self-supported; authors declare no conflicts of interest.

f.population: 40 clinical studies of lateral ridge augmentation (simultaneous, staged or ridge expansion) pooling 1,242 patients and 1,881 implants
f.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation (GBR with particulate grafts and membranes, or autogenous bone blocks) staged or simultaneous with implant placement
f.comparison: Comparisons between grafting materials and membrane types (RCTs/CCTs); otherwise baseline vs final
f.main_result: Simultaneous approach gave a significant defect height reduction (WMD -4.28 mm) and staged approach a bone width gain (WMD 3.90 mm); implant survival and success were high (>95%).
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest declared.
f.limitations: Case series did not meet the quality categories and well-designed long-term RCTs are lacking.

f.main_result: Buccal bone augmentation of more than 2 mm beyond the implant platform and vertical augmentation to a line joining adjacent interproximal bone peaks are needed for stable esthetic soft tissue around multiple implants; strategic pontics help preserve papilla height.
f.follow_up: 2-year periapical radiograph of the illustrated case
f.limitations: Very few long-term studies exist on compromised cases with multiple implants.

f.main_result: Osteoinduction, osteoconduction and osseointegration are interrelated but distinct; osteoinduction produces most new bone in healing, while osseointegration is stable direct bone anchorage of an implant maintained over time.

Collagen membranes show advantageous biological and clinical features versus non-resorbable and other resorbable membranes but need graft support and fixation, and cross-linked types have higher exposure rates.
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared.

f.population: One 43-year-old woman with a hopeless maxillary left central incisor (palatal root fracture) and a thin periodontal phenotype
f.intervention: Surgical veneer grafting: flapless extraction, immediate implant (Tapered Screw-Vent) with dual-zone allograft packed to the gingival margin, partial-thickness epithelial connective tissue graft, screw-retained provisional
f.main_result: At 24 months CBCT showed optimal amount and stability of peri-implant marginal bone and the facial ridge contour was stable at 18 months (single case, no measurements).
f.funding_coi: Authors reported no disclosures
f.limitations: Long-term clinical data for this technique are not yet available and it is technique-sensitive

f.population: 10 patients with severe horizontal alveolar ridge atrophy (under 3 mm), mean age 46.6 years
f.intervention: Staged horizontal augmentation with mandibular (external oblique ridge) bone laminae plus particulated autograft, then at implant placement relining with anorganic bovine bone mineral (Bio-Oss) and a collagen membrane
outcomes: horizontal ridge width before and after augmentation
f.main_result: Ridge width rose from 2.1 to 6.9 mm after grafting, remodeling over 4 months was 0.25 mm (6.6 mm), and after ABBM/membrane relining the width was 7.7 mm at abutment connection.
f.follow_up: 8 months (4 months to implant placement, 4 more to abutment connection)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Short-term data; long-term outcomes are needed to confirm the volume-maintenance effect

f.population: 12 fresh human cadaver heads with bilateral posterior mandibular edentulism (11 analyzed)
f.intervention: Novel lingual flap advancement preserving the mylohyoid muscle attachment (retromolar pad lifting, blunt separation, semiblunt periosteal release)
f.comparison: Classic lingual flap release technique detaching the mylohyoid muscle
outcomes: vertical lingual flap release in zones I, II and III (mm)
f.main_result: The preserving technique gave 8.273, 10.09 and 10.273 mm more vertical flap release than the classic technique in zones I, II and III (P < .0001).
f.sample_size: 11 heads, 22 surgical sites analyzed (one specimen excluded)
f.funding_coi: Osteology Foundation grant; no financial interests declared
f.limitations: Examiners were not blinded to the technique and ridge anatomy was not perfectly symmetric between sides

f.population: Four adult male foxhound dogs with surgically created mandibular premolar-region bone defects (about 8 x 12 x 10 mm)
f.intervention: Defects covered with a standard e-PTFE membrane or a prototype reinforced e-PTFE membrane, fixed with screws, sacrificed at 2 and 4 months
f.comparison: Nonmembrane control defect
outcomes: histomorphometry of regenerate (cortical layer vs spongiosa)
f.main_result: Membrane sites healed significantly better than controls, but regeneration was incomplete at 4 months; the cortical layer made up 38% of the regenerate at 4 months vs under 1% at 2 months and reinforced membranes kept their form while standard ones partially collapsed.
materials_brands: GoreTex Augmentation Material e-PTFE membrane (W.L. Gore)
Reinforced prototype e-PTFE membrane (r-GTAM, W.L. Gore)
f.funding_coi: Grants from W.L. Gore and Associates and the Swiss AO/ASIF Foundation

f.population: 25 patients needing sinus augmentation (21 treated, 24 sinuses, 20 sinuses analyzed)
f.intervention: Lateral window sinus augmentation with particulated allograft, with CBCT-measured bucco-palatal distance at 8, 10 and 12 mm and bone core biopsy at about 6 months
f.main_result: Mean vital bone was 22.71 +/- 19.08% and was inversely related to bucco-palatal distance (r = -0.376, P < 0.001); 96% graft success.
f.sample_size: 25 recruited; 21 patients, 24 sinuses grafted; 20 sinuses analyzed
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by BioHorizons and ICOI foundation; several authors report research support or fees from BioHorizons, Zimmer, OraPharma, Straumann
f.limitations: Limited sample size per category prevented establishing a BPD cutoff

f.population: 24 patients (28 sites) with horizontally deficient maxillary ridges (residual width under 5 mm)
f.intervention: Two-stage horizontal augmentation with autogenous ramus block graft (RBG), 13 sites, covered with deproteinized bovine bone and collagen membrane
f.comparison: Guided bone regeneration (GBR), 15 sites, with autogenous particles plus DBB and a tacked resorbable collagen membrane
f.main_result: Mean volume reduction was 12.48 +/- 2.67% with GBR vs 7.20 +/- 1.40% with RBG (P < 0.001); horizontal gain was greater with GBR; insertion torque was similar.
f.funding_coi: No relevant financial relationships declared

f.population: 48 randomized patients with atrophic alveolar ridges (width 4 mm or less) needing 3D augmentation before implants
f.intervention: Expanded autologous iliac crest-derived mesenchymal cells seeded on a synthetic biphasic calcium phosphate substitute (MBCP) covered with a titanium-reinforced non-resorbable membrane
f.comparison: Autogenous bone block graft
outcomes: bone volume change by CBCT at 5 months
f.main_result: The cell therapy group gained more bone volume, mean difference 480.01 mm3 (p = 0.032), with change from baseline of 1066.91 vs 586.9 mm3; all implants integrated in both groups.
f.sample_size: 48 randomized (36 test, 12 control); 7 test patients could not be treated for insufficient expanded MSCs
f.follow_up: 5 months to CBCT and implant placement
materials_brands: MBCP biphasic calcium phosphate granules (Biomatlante), HA/beta-TCP 20/80
f.funding_coi: EU H2020 Maxibone project; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Phase 2 trial was underpowered and baseline augmentation volume may have been higher in the test group

f.population: Human gingival fibroblasts from two donors seeded onto collagen membranes pre-soaked in porcine bone-conditioned medium
f.intervention: Collagen membranes incubated with bone-conditioned medium from fresh or demineralized bone chips
f.comparison: Recombinant human TGF-b1 as control
outcomes: expression of adrenomedullin, pentraxin 3, interleukin 11, proteoglycan 4
f.main_result: Membranes incubated with BCM for at least one minute made fibroblasts decrease ADM and PTX3 and increase IL-11 and PRG4 expression, showing rapid adsorption of TGF-beta activity, with viability and morphology unchanged.
f.sample_size: Fibroblasts from two donors; two independent BCM preparations

f.population: Partially dentate patients with horizontal alveolar ridge defects
f.intervention: Prosthetically guided horizontal bone augmentation protocol (diagnosis, defect classification, augmentation techniques)
f.main_result: Review concludes that prosthetically guided regeneration allows reconstruction of lost alveolar and soft-tissue contours and implant placement in positions permitting optimal functional and esthetic restorations.

f.population: Full or partially edentulous patients with vertical alveolar defects needing augmentation for implant rehabilitation
f.intervention: Vertical augmentation by onlay bone grafting or guided bone regeneration
outcomes: description of initial defect features (site, edentulism type, dimensions)
f.main_result: 40 studies (528 vertical cases) met inclusion; defect features were inconsistently reported, so a classification by number of bony walls and base width was proposed
f.limitations: Information on the initial vertical defect characteristics was not comprehensively reported in most included studies

f.population: Patients with implants in the anterior maxilla (canine to canine) after buccal bone augmentation
f.intervention: Buccal augmentation by guided bone regeneration, autogenous block grafting, or both, followed by implant placement
f.comparison: Three augmentation protocols compared descriptively and in a mixed model
outcomes: esthetic parameters (Pink Esthetic Score, Papilla Presence Index)
f.main_result: Baseline buccal bone volume correlated strongly negatively with volume change (r = -.80); baseline volume above 105 mm3 predicted volume loss with 100% specificity and 96% sensitivity
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Small sample size, underpowered for intergroup comparison, and augmented volume not standardized because of the retrospective design

f.population: Eleven patients with at least two lateral bone defects, eight re-examined
f.intervention: Implants placed with GBR using a xenogenic bone substitute loaded with rhBMP-2 (test) under a collagen membrane
f.comparison: Same GBR without rhBMP-2 (control, split-mouth)
f.main_result: Implant survival was 100% after at least 17 years; marginal bone levels did not differ significantly between rhBMP-2 test and control sites
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared; funding not stated
f.limitations: Small sample of eight patients and a 27% drop-out rate

f.population: 21 patients with three-dimensional bone defects reconstructed with patient-specific titanium meshes at least 5 years earlier
f.intervention: Customized bone regeneration with patient-specific titanium mesh and 1:1 autogenous bone and xenograft
f.comparison: Flap designs compared: crestal incision, crestal incision with vertical release, poncho flap
f.main_result: Crestal incision without vertical release gave significantly better esthetics and mesial/distal bone levels than poncho flaps or crestal incision with release; mean PES 11.09
f.funding_coi: No specific funding
f.limitations: Pink Esthetic Score is a subjective measurement tool

f.population: Six beagle dogs with two-wall-damaged mandibular premolar extraction sockets (36 sites)
f.intervention: Grafting deproteinized porcine bone mineral with or without collagen membrane coverage
f.comparison: Ungrafted socket (no graft)
f.main_result: Grafted sites kept ridge dimensions similar to pristine ridge while ungrafted sites collapsed; membrane increased mineralized tissue proportion and BG + M gave a larger regenerated ridge area than no graft (p < .05)
materials_brands: THE Graft (Purgo Biologics), deproteinized porcine bone mineral
f.funding_coi: Funded by the National Research Foundation of Korea and Korean government ministries; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Patients with horizontally deficient alveolar ridges receiving narrow-diameter implants (272 patients) or standard-diameter implants with augmentation (83 patients)
f.intervention: Narrow-diameter implants (3.3 mm, Straumann) placed in pristine bone
f.comparison: Standard-diameter implants (4.1 mm) placed with horizontal augmentation
f.main_result: Survival 96.1% for NDI and 95.6% for SDI+A, with no significant difference (p = .89); success 84.3% vs 81.3% (p = .79)
f.sample_size: 597 NDI in 272 patients and 180 SDI in 83 patients
materials_brands: Straumann narrow-diameter (3.3 mm) and standard-diameter (4.1 mm) implants
f.funding_coi: Authors report grants and personal fees from implant and biomaterial companies including Dentsply, Geistlich and Straumann

f.population: 18 minipigs with established horizontal/vertical alveolar crest defects in the maxilla
f.intervention: PDLLA/CaCO3 carrier loaded with 400 µg rhBMP2/50 µg rhVEGF165 on one side and 800 µg rhBMP2 on the other
f.comparison: Blank carriers and unfilled sham-operated defects in six control animals
f.main_result: rhBMP2 alone (800 µg) did not significantly increase bone over blank carriers, whereas 400 µg rhBMP2 plus 50 µg rhVEGF165 significantly increased bone at 13 weeks (p = .024)
f.funding_coi: Supported by a grant from KLS Martin

f.population: 39 of originally 72 patients (147 of 265 implants) treated 1994-1996 for dehiscence defects with GBR or in pristine bone
f.intervention: Simultaneous GBR with Bio-Oss and a resorbable collagen membrane (BG) or a nonresorbable ePTFE membrane (GT)
f.comparison: Implants placed in pristine bone (CT)
f.main_result: Implant survival was 89.3% (BG), 90.2% (GT) and 93.8% (CT) after a median 23.5 years without significant differences; smoking reduced survival
f.funding_coi: Supported by a grant from Geistlich Pharma AG and the University of Zurich clinic; several authors report Geistlich grants or fees
f.limitations: Heterogeneous group sizes, no power analysis, implant-based analysis, and non-standardized intraoral radiographs

f.population: 50 male Wistar rats with two calvarial critical-size defects each
f.intervention: Defects filled with autogenous bone, bioglass, hydroxyapatite or bovine xenograft, each with or without e-PTFE membrane
f.comparison: Blood clot (negative control) and autogenous bone (positive control); with versus without e-PTFE
f.main_result: New bone was similar across groups and with versus without e-PTFE; autogenous bone gave the best new bone formation and final biomaterial volume
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Pre-clinical rat model; no collagen membrane group or allograft tested; short observation period

f.main_result: Titanium mesh offers an excellent solution for GBR over other membrane types, though pore size and frequency need adjustment; no ideal membrane has been established for clinical use
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Evidence on barrier membranes comes mainly from preclinical studies

f.population: One partially dentate 43-year-old woman with a maxillary and a mandibular vertical defect
f.intervention: Computer-guided harvesting of a mandibular bone block from the external oblique ridge using a CAD/CAM surgical guide and piezoelectric cutting
outcomes: accuracy of the osteotomy versus plan
f.main_result: Superimposition of pre- and postoperative CT showed a procedure accuracy of 0.25 mm and one block repaired both defects.
f.funding_coi: Authors LDS and AF are inventors of the patent for the bone-harvesting surgical guide
f.limitations: Advantages are theoretical and need validation by well-designed studies.

f.population: 25 male 6-month-old albino Wistar rats with calvarial or ischiac bone grafts on the mandibular inferior border
f.intervention: Autogenous calvarial (membranous) and ischiac (endochondral) onlay bone grafts covered with an e-PTFE membrane (GBR), healing 5 or 11 months
f.comparison: Same bone grafts without membrane
f.main_result: Membrane-treated grafts of both types kept volume near baseline at 11 months, whereas non-membrane control grafts resorbed significantly at 5 and 11 months, ischiac grafts more than calvarial in width and length.

f.population: 20 patients with single-tooth postextraction sites in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Early implant placement with simultaneous contour augmentation by GBR using a 2-layer composite graft (autogenous chips plus DBBM, collagen membrane)
f.main_result: At 10 years median peri-implant bone loss between 1 and 10 y was 0.35 mm, success rate 95%, median Pink Esthetic Score 8, and facial bone wall thickness rose from 0 mm at surgery to 1.67 mm.
f.funding_coi: Departmental funds of Universities of Bern and Geneva and a research grant from Straumann AG; no conflicts declared

f.population: Patients with horizontal alveolar ridge deficiencies receiving implants after/with lateral bone augmentation
f.intervention: Lateral bone augmentation procedures (GBR, bone blocks), simultaneous or staged
f.comparison: Other lateral augmentation procedures or no treatment
f.main_result: Lateral ridge augmentation maintains peri-implant health; BOP changes minimal and no significant differences among modalities; peri-implantitis incidence 16-26% at 6-8 years.
f.funding_coi: Consensus meeting supported by Osteology Foundation grant; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Few studies in meta-analyses, not powered for peri-implant health outcomes, limited to English controlled studies.

f.population: In vitro, in vivo and human studies on GBR (MEDLINE/PubMed search, up to 16 June 2016)
f.intervention: GBR barrier membranes (synthetic polymers, natural polymers, metals, inorganic) and their property modifications
f.main_result: Experimental data suggest the membrane plays an active role in promoting regeneration in the underlying defect rather than being a purely passive barrier, while the role of membrane porosity remains contradictory.
f.funding_coi: Supported by BIOMATCELL VINN Excellence Center, Swedish Research Council, Osteology Foundation and others

f.population: Rat femoral epiphysis trabecular bone defects (84 male Sprague-Dawley rats)
f.intervention: Defects filled with deproteinized bovine bone, hydroxyapatite or strontium-doped hydroxyapatite granules and covered with an extracellular matrix membrane
f.comparison: Membrane-covered empty defects (sham)
f.main_result: At 6 days the strontium-doped HA defects showed more new bone with reduced osteoclastic and RANKL gene expression and fewer osteoclasts than DBB or HA.
f.sample_size: 84 rats, defects at 12 h, 3 d and 6 d
f.funding_coi: Supported by BIOMATCELL VINN Excellence Center, Swedish Research Council and others; conflict of interest none declared

f.population: 37 patients with maxillary anterior extraction and loss of the buccal plate
f.intervention: IVAN technique: FDBA, GBR barrier membrane and pediculated connective tissue graft with delayed (25) or immediate (12) implant placement
f.main_result: All 37 sites healed uneventfully; 36 implants osseointegrated and were successful at 6 and 12 months, overall success rate 97.3% (immediate group 91.6%).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: Patients with severe vertical ridge deficiency in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Four-type flap design classification (vestibule depth and periosteum quality) for tension-free closure in vertical ridge augmentation with GBR
f.main_result: The authors propose four flap-design types (shallow or deep vestibule, healthy or scarred periosteum) with matching flap and suturing management to achieve tension-free closure in vertical ridge augmentation.
f.funding_coi: Honoraria from Osteogenics Biomedical and Geistlich Pharma for some authors; partially supported by University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund
f.limitations: Lack of clinical data to validate the proposed guidelines

f.population: 49 patients with dehisced single implant sites
f.intervention: Simultaneous implant placement and GBR with the novel resorbable non-cross-linked collagen membrane creos xenoprotect (CXP) over bone chips and Bio-Oss
f.comparison: Bio-Gide (BG) collagen membrane
outcomes: implant cumulative survival and success rate
f.main_result: Implant survival and success were 100% at 1 year with no bone loss between prosthetic delivery and 1 year; mean PES rose to 8.10 (CXP) and 7.48 (BG) and group differences were not significant.
f.follow_up: 1 year after prosthetic delivery (implant follow-up about 23 months)
f.funding_coi: Supported by Nobel Biocare Services AG (grant T-186); no other conflicts declared

f.intervention: Contour management (critical and subcritical contour) of immediate and delayed implant provisional restorations
f.main_result: For immediate implants the critical contour should support the gingival margin (facially 0.5-1 mm reduced) and the subcritical contour be as concave as possible to give regenerative space; in delayed cases contours are modified during conditioning of mature tissues.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: Human clinical trials of GBR for alveolar bone defects (at least 10 patients, follow-up at least 6 months)
f.intervention: Guided bone regeneration classified as Type I (membrane with particulate), Type II (block graft with membrane and particulate), Type III (cortical block tenting)
f.main_result: Of 25 trials, 17 used conventional GBR I, 7 GBR II and 1 GBR III; heterogeneity prevented conclusions on the superiority of one technique.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
f.limitations: High heterogeneity among studies

f.population: 17 patients with 19 complex three-dimensional defects of maxillary and mandibular edentulous ridges
f.intervention: Guided bone regeneration with a digitally planned, laser-sintered customized titanium mesh covering autologous/bovine bone particulate
outcomes: mesh position match with virtual plan
reconstructed bone volume vs planned volume
f.main_result: Mean mesh position match was 82%, exposures occurred in 52.3% (15.8% infected), 26.3% failed; reconstructed volume was 65% of planned including failures and 88.2% without failures.
materials_brands: EOSINT M270 printer (laser-sintered titanium Ti64 mesh)
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest and no financial support

f.population: Adult hound dogs (4 animals, 31 experimental sites)
f.intervention: Tibial corticocancellous bone graft to the lateral mandible protected by macroporous or microporous titanium mesh or resorbable mesh
f.comparison: Grafts without mesh (controls); cortical perforations vs none
f.main_result: New bone area was highest with the macroporous titanium mesh (66.26 mm2) versus microporous (52.82), resorbable (46.76) and no mesh (29.80).
materials_brands: Stryker-Leibinger macroporous and microporous titanium meshes

f.population: 15 patients with aggressive periodontitis, two intrabony defects each
f.intervention: GTR with xenogenic graft plus modified perforated collagen membrane
f.comparison: Xenogenic graft plus standard collagen membrane
f.main_result: PPD, CAL, DD and ACP improved in both groups without between-group differences; MPM sites gained additional LDF 0.4 mm and %DF 6.4% from 6 to 12 months.

f.population: Atrophic alveolar ridges in maxilla and mandible (case presentation)
f.intervention: In situ shell technique: autogenous bone plate, allograft plus injectable PRF, bioresorbable membrane
outcomes: osseous regeneration sufficient for implant placement
f.main_result: Sufficient osseous regeneration was achieved to place dental implants in an ideal position.
f.follow_up: 6 months of healing before second-stage surgery
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Learning curve; outcomes may differ for less experienced clinicians; further clinical and histological trials needed

f.population: Eight mongrel dogs with standardized buccal dehiscence-type defects at implants in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: DBBM with or without autogenous bone chips and with or without collagen membrane
f.comparison: DBBM alone vs the other graft/membrane combinations
f.main_result: Autogenous bone chips and the collagen membrane increased bone formation around DBBM particles; wound protection early may be critical.
f.funding_coi: Funded by a grant from Geistlich Pharma AG; materials provided by Straumann and Geistlich; one author consults for Straumann

f.population: 21 included articles on barrier membrane characteristics
f.intervention: Barrier membranes for GBR (criteria an ideal membrane should fulfil)
outcomes: membrane criteria: biocompatibility, space maintenance, occlusiveness, handling, bioactivation
f.main_result: Ideal GBR membranes need biocompatibility, space maintenance, occlusive function, easy handling and bioactivation-friendly properties; biocompatibility matters most.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: 37 patients needing implants with bony defects in posterior maxilla or mandible
f.intervention: Defects grafted with bovine bone mineral and covered with PEG hydrogel membrane
f.comparison: Collagen membrane (control)
f.main_result: Mean vertical defect fill was 5.63 mm (PEG) versus 4.25 mm (collagen); fills 94.9% and 96.4%; more soft tissue complications with PEG.

f.population: 58 of 72 original patients with implants placed with or without simultaneous GBR
f.intervention: Implants with simultaneous GBR using DBBM and collagen or e-PTFE membrane
f.comparison: Implants fully surrounded by bone without GBR (control)
f.main_result: Cumulative implant survival was 93.2% (control 94.6%, collagen 91.9%, e-PTFE 92.6%), not significantly different.
f.sample_size: 265 implants in 72 patients originally; 58 patients examined

f.population: Human peri-implantitis lesions (>10) in 6 included studies
f.intervention: Regenerative surgical treatment of peri-implantitis
f.main_result: Weighted mean radiographic bone fill was 2.41 mm and PD reduction 3.06 mm after at least 36 months.
f.limitations: Limited long-term evidence; hard to discern grafting material from new bone

f.population: Clinical studies of implants in augmented ridges or with simultaneous peri-implant grafting
f.intervention: Peri-implant hard-tissue augmentation prior to or with implant placement
f.main_result: Augmentation procedures seem to give stable peri-implant tissues, but long-term buccal bone stability is assessed by few studies; the performance of meta-analysis was impossible.
f.limitations: Heterogeneous outcome measures, methods, grafts and implants prevented meta-analysis

f.intervention: Collagen-based biomaterials for tissue engineering

f.population: Adults (>=18 y) with a bone dehiscence or fenestration at implant placement
f.intervention: Technical, material and pharmacological aspects of lateral bone augmentation/GBR performed with implant placement
f.comparison: Any of the other interventions, or no treatment for pharmacological protocols
f.main_result: Eleven studies were included; no meta-analysis was possible, and the conclusions favour membrane fixation, resorbable non-cross-linked collagen membranes, double flap or lingual flap advancement, and avoiding routine antibiotics in ASA 1-2 patients.
f.sample_size: 11 studies (6 RCTs, 2 SRs, 2 prospective case series)
f.funding_coi: Supported by the Research Centre in Ferrara; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Too few studies per outcome for a robust heterogeneity estimate or publication bias assessment, so no meta-analysis was done.

f.population: Adults with at least one intraosseous periodontal defect and a pocket of 4 mm or more after phase I-II therapy
f.intervention: Access flap surgery of different designs and with different regenerative devices, plus perioperative/postoperative protocols, assessed for invasiveness
f.comparison: Any flap surgery differing in flap design or in number/type of regenerative devices; placebo or no treatment for protocols
f.main_result: Single-flap designs reduced postoperative pain and improved early healing; adding a membrane increased chair time and pain, while enamel matrix derivative or graft did not increase invasiveness; single-flap open flap debridement reduced chair time and costs.
f.funding_coi: Open Access funding by Universita degli Studi di Ferrara (CRUI-CARE); no COI statement in text
f.limitations: Differences in design, outcome measures and intervals precluded meta-analysis; all studies had some concerns for risk of bias.

f.population: 20 box-shaped peri-implant bone defects in 10 pig mandibles (ex vivo)
f.intervention: GBR with particulated xenograft + collagen membrane, with fixation pins, or block xenograft + collagen membrane, followed by blinded flap suturing
f.comparison: Granulate alone vs Granulate + Pins vs Block
outcomes: horizontal thickness of the augmented region (HT0-HT5 mm)
change in thickness during flap suturing
f.main_result: Wound closure significantly reduced horizontal thickness in all groups, and the reduction was significantly larger for particulated graft alone than with pins or block.

f.population: 12 beagle dogs with healed mandibular ridges
f.intervention: Implants placed in sites with thin (<1.5 mm) or thick (>=1.5 mm) buccal bone wall, followed by 8-week healing or ligature-induced peri-implantitis episodes
f.comparison: Thick buccal bone wall (>=1.5 mm) vs thin (<1.5 mm)
f.main_result: A buccal bone wall of at least 1.5 mm at placement was associated with significantly less physiologic and pathologic bone loss than a thinner wall; no implants failed.
f.follow_up: 8 weeks after placement; then three ligature-induced peri-implantitis episodes
materials_brands: TiCare Inhex Mini 3.3 x 8 mm implants (rough and hybrid designs)
f.funding_coi: Research funding/grants from Mozo-Grau to the first author; no conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 27 patients with single-tooth gaps in the esthetic area needing implants with buccal dehiscence/fenestration defects
f.intervention: GBR with DBBM and a resorbable collagen membrane (RES)
f.comparison: Titanium-reinforced non-resorbable ePTFE membrane (N-RES)
f.main_result: Both membranes regenerated bone with similar defect fill at 6 months, but the non-resorbable membrane lost significantly less horizontal thickness (0.14 vs 2.23 mm).
f.funding_coi: Swiss Dental Association grant; implants from Dentsply, bone substitute and membranes from Geistlich; no conflict of interest reported

f.population: In vitro, in vivo (animal) and clinical studies on cellular and molecular events in guided bone regeneration
f.intervention: Guided bone regeneration with barrier membranes, including incorporation of growth factors and cells
outcomes: cellular and molecular activity in membrane and defect
f.main_result: The membrane contributes bioactively to defect regeneration, with membrane-associated cellular and molecular activity linked to bone regeneration in the underlying defect.
f.funding_coi: Swedish Research Council, ALF agreement, Osteology Foundation and other Swedish foundations
f.limitations: Only English papers in MEDLINE/PubMed before October 2018 were included in a narrative survey.

f.intervention: Vertical ridge augmentation techniques: guided bone regeneration, bone blocks and distraction osteogenesis
f.main_result: Vertical ridge augmentation is feasible and effective; GBR with bone block is technically demanding, while distraction osteogenesis is faster with less morbidity but cannot add lateral augmentation simultaneously.
f.funding_coi: No direct financial interests with the products and instruments listed

f.population: 6 patients (3 men, 3 women) whose bone curettage biopsies contained retained collagen membrane
f.intervention: Histopathologic examination (H&E and Masson trichrome) of biopsies containing resorbable collagen membrane
f.main_result: Retained collagen membranes appeared as hyalinized, paucicellular eosinophilic fibrils without foreign body reaction, persisted longer than expected (2-6 weeks) in 3 cases and may have retarded healing in 5 cases.

f.population: 11 patients (16 retromolar onlay grafts; 4 maxilla, 12 mandible) with atrophic alveolar ridges
f.intervention: Autogenous cortico-cancellous onlay grafts from the ascending ramus fixed with two titanium screws; graft volume measured on CBCT with automated image registration at T0, T1 (post-op) and T2 (12 months)
outcomes: graft volume change on CBCT over 12 months
f.main_result: Mean augmented volume fell from 372.2 mm3 to 230.2 mm3 at 12 months, a resorption of 43.7% +/- 19.0% (maxilla 60.2%, mandible 37.6%).
f.funding_coi: Supported by the university departments; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: No sample size calculation was performed; all available patients with a 12-month CBCT were used.

f.population: Undifferentiated mouse ST2 stromal bone marrow cells cultured on membranes (in vitro)
f.intervention: BioGide collagen barrier membranes pre-coated with 20% bone conditioned media (BCM) from porcine bone chips
f.comparison: Uncoated BioGide collagen membranes
outcomes: Runx2, ALP, OCN, BSP mRNA at 5 days
f.main_result: BCM pre-coating increased osteoblast attachment over 4-fold, raised ALP, OCN and BSP mRNA and gave a 5-fold increase in alizarin red staining at 14 days; proliferation and Runx2 were unchanged.
f.sample_size: Triplicate wells, three independent experiments per condition
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Oral Cell Biology Laboratory, University of Bern; no competing interests declared
f.limitations: In vitro only; animal testing is still required.

f.population: 214 patients with severely atrophied jaws receiving onlay block grafts and implants
f.intervention: Autologous intraoral block onlay grafts combined with Bio-Oss mixed with PRP and covered by PPP, followed by implant placement
f.main_result: 216 of 224 grafts succeeded (96.4%); 591 of 633 implants survived (93.4%); cumulative implant survival was 83% at 137 months.

f.population: Patients with dehiscence-type defects at titanium implants treated by GBR; 31 of 37 completed the 4-year follow-up
f.intervention: GBR with natural bone mineral and a randomly assigned cross-linked or native collagen membrane; outcomes grouped by residual defect height at re-entry
f.comparison: Residual defect height 0 mm (control) vs 1 mm vs more than 1 mm
f.main_result: At 4 years PD was similar across groups, while BOP was higher with RDH above 1 mm than in controls (54.1% vs 29.1%, P=0.02) and mucosal recession tended to be higher.

f.population: Patients with Class II-IV horizontal or horizontal/vertical alveolar ridge defects (372 cortical plate cases)
f.intervention: Shell technique with allogeneic cortical bone plates, space filled with autogenous or allogeneic granules or a mixture; implants after 4-6 months
outcomes: bone remodeling and graft resorption (histology, SEM)
f.main_result: Of 656 implants 4 failed (all peri-implantitis); 30 of 372 plate cases (8.1%) had complications, and implants could still be placed in 26.
f.funding_coi: All authors received speaker fees and research support from Straumann and botiss; stated to have had no influence

f.population: Rabbit skulls, and 10 consecutive patients with highly resorbed edentulous upper jaws
f.intervention: Pre-shaped stiff occlusive titanium barrier placed subperiosteally over the rabbit skull and the atrophic maxilla
f.main_result: Rabbit tissue augmentation reached 6 mm; 75.3% and 59.4% of new tissue volume remained 3 and 9 months after barrier removal; in 5 of 10 patients with unexposed barriers, jaw height and width increased up to 16 mm and 30 of 33 implants osseointegrated.
f.follow_up: up to 5 years after implant placement

f.population: Eight adult male Japanese white rabbits (calvarium)
f.intervention: Hemispherical titanium cap without holes (fully occlusive) placed on the calvarium after marrow penetration
f.comparison: Titanium cap with 1.5 mm holes
outcomes: percentage area of newly generated tissue
