f.comparison: The four materials compared with each other (e.max CAD, Suprinity, Cerasmart, Enamic)
f.main_result: Glass-ceramic crowns fractured at higher loads (e.max 4100 N, Suprinity 3659 N) than hybrids (Enamic 2003 N, Cerasmart 1562 N); flexural strength was LD 289 > ZLS 230 > HPP 141 > PICN 103 MPa.
f.sample_size: 10 crowns and 10 bars per material (40 crowns, 40 bars)
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq; no conflict of interest reported

f.population: Published studies on zirconia-reinforced lithium silicate (ZLS) CAD/CAM ceramics (in vitro and clinical)
f.intervention: ZLS glass-ceramics (Vita Suprinity PC, Celtra Duo) for CAD/CAM restorations
f.comparison: Other glass-ceramics such as lithium disilicate
f.main_result: There is no undisputed evidence that ZLS is stronger than lithium disilicate; its fracture resistance withstands physiological occlusal forces and internal marginal gaps are clinically acceptable (<=150 um).
f.funding_coi: No competing interests declared
f.limitations: Data on ZLS biocompatibility are scarce and controversial

f.population: Partially edentulous patients and edentulous patients receiving implants (consensus of four systematic reviews)
f.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement and loading
f.comparison: Conventional (delayed) placement and loading protocols
f.main_result: Different timings of implant placement/loading gave high survival rates; further research is needed for detailed guidelines.
f.limitations: Further research is required to provide detailed guidelines for the different protocols

f.population: Adults with maxillary single-tooth implants in the aesthetic zone (upper incisors and canines)
f.intervention: Immediate/early implant placement and immediate/early loading
f.main_result: Pooled data from 29 studies (965 implants) and 7 controlled trials showed no differences in survival or marginal bone remodelling between timing protocols up to 5 years.
f.limitations: Insufficient data for meta-analytic comparison of all placement and loading combinations

f.population: Patients with implant-supported multiple-unit fixed dental prostheses (>=10 patients, >=2 implants, >=3 years)
f.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement and loading
f.comparison: Delayed/conventional placement and loading
f.main_result: High survival rates (>90%) for all studied combinations except IPIL; a meta-analysis of 3 RCTs found no difference in survival between DPIL and DPDL (p = .227).
f.funding_coi: Departmental funding only; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Heterogeneity of the data did not allow conclusions on biological complications

f.population: Patients treated with implant-supported single, short-span, full-arch or overdenture reconstructions
f.intervention: Immediate or early implant placement or loading
f.comparison: Traditional delayed placement and/or loading
f.main_result: There is no strong evidence that timing of placement or loading affects patient discomfort or satisfaction; full-arch patients are more satisfied with immediate loading in the short term but not after one year.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest to disclose
f.limitations: The quality evaluation showed some concerns among most studies

f.population: Extracted human molars mounted for crown preparation
f.intervention: Preparation refinement with a dental operating microscope up to x10 magnification
f.comparison: Preparation refinement with x3.0 loupes
f.main_result: Mean marginal gap was 145.0 um with loupes vs 35.6 um with the microscope (P<.001); gap volume 0.975 vs 0.250 mm3 (P=.023).
f.sample_size: 18 extracted molars (2 groups); 24 gap points per specimen
f.funding_coi: Supported by the Department of Endodontics, University of Pennsylvania

f.population: Five dogs; second mandibular premolars hemi-sected, distal roots extracted
f.intervention: Root extraction after elevation of full-thickness flaps
f.comparison: Flapless root extraction on the contralateral side
f.main_result: After 6 months the coronal ridge lost about 35% of its dimension, with no significant difference between flap and flapless extraction.

f.population: 92 adult patients with single implants placed immediately into extraction sockets in the maxilla (15-25)
f.intervention: Multilevel multivariate modelling of factors affecting bone changes after immediate implant placement (cylindrical vs tapered implants in the source RCT)
outcomes: implant surface to outer bony crest distance
f.main_result: Residual gap size depended on initial gap and bone crest thickness, buccal crest resorption depended on implant position, and age affected vertical gap reduction.

f.population: 28 freshman dental and hygiene students without signs of mandibular dysfunction
f.intervention: Interocclusal centric relation registrations with the Williamson leaf gauge technique, two operators, repeated 30 days later
f.comparison: Roth power centric bite technique
outcomes: number of matching bite registrations on split-cast mountings
condylar displacement from centric occlusion to centric relation on the Mandibular Position Indicator
f.main_result: No significant difference between operators or between techniques for any MPI measurement; the leaf gauge appeared less reliable over 30 days than the power centric bite.

f.population: 42 healthy dentate adults (20 men, 22 women, 21 to 40 years) with normal occlusion and no TMD
f.intervention: Lucia jig on the upper central incisors for 0, 5, 10, 15, 20 and 30 minutes with surface EMG of masseter and temporalis
outcomes: RMS electromyographic activity of masseter and temporalis muscles at rest
f.main_result: No statistically significant difference in masseter and temporal EMG activity across 0 to 30 minutes; the jig changed EMG activity, mostly lowering it.
materials_brands: Duralay chemically activated acrylic resin (Reliance Dental Mfg Co.)
f.funding_coi: Authors declared no commercial or associative interest

f.population: 10 asymptomatic subjects with intact dentitions (6 women, 4 men)
f.intervention: Photographic comparison of wire angulation on acrylic overlays on the mandibular right first molar and left central incisor, closed versus maximum open
f.comparison: Most closed versus maximum open mandibular position
outcomes: angular (rotational) change between molar and incisor
f.main_result: Mean linear flexure was 0.0028 inches and mean angular change about 3.1 degrees, significant at the 0.01% level.

f.population: 20 in vivo and in vitro studies on mandibular flexure and implant-framework systems
f.intervention: MEDLINE and PubMed literature search (1950 to May 2010)
outcomes: effect of mandibular flexure on the implant-framework system
f.main_result: Mandibular flexure is multifactorial and the effect of the implant-framework system is unclear; sectional prosthesis designs may minimize its effect.
f.limitations: No randomized, nonrandomized controlled or case-control studies were found, and no studies addressed long-span unilateral implant fixed prostheses.

f.intervention: Posterior bilateral implants supporting the distal cantilevers through unconnected cantilever rests (gold cylinders) on a framework attached only to the anterior implants
f.main_result: Author proposes that unconnected posterior abutments support the cantilevers, reducing torque on anterior implants and avoiding flexure-induced microdamage (no data reported).

f.population: 3D finite element model of a human edentulous mandible
f.intervention: Six implant-prosthesis designs (six or four implants, with or without distal cantilevers, cross-arch or midline-divided bar) loaded with 10 N at the condyles
f.comparison: Mandible with implants but no prosthetic superstructure
outcomes: relative displacement at the condylar level
von Mises stress in implants and superstructure
f.main_result: Cross-arch bridges restricted mandibular flexure (relative displacement 0.53 with six implants) while midline-divided superstructures restored flexibility (0.83) and were less stressed.
materials_brands: Titanium implants 3.25 mm x 13 mm with gold-ceramic superstructure
f.limitations: Linear static analysis assuming complete osseointegration and an arbitrary 10 N load.

f.population: 25 patients with 77 implants placed in healed posterior sites
f.intervention: Concave (Slim) screw-retained abutments on 4x10 mm hexagonal internal connection implants
f.comparison: Cylindrical (Straight) abutments
outcomes: early marginal bone loss at 8 weeks and 6 months
f.main_result: Early global MBL was -0.6 ± 0.7 mm with cylindrical versus -0.4 ± 0.6 mm with concave abutments (p=0.030).
f.follow_up: 6 months after loading (8 months after implantation)
materials_brands: IPX hexagonal internal connection implant (Nueva Galimplant)
f.funding_coi: Supported by Nueva Galimplant and the University of Santiago de Compostela; nothing to declare
f.limitations: Results must be confirmed by a study with a longer follow-up.

f.population: Published reports on platform switching: human radiographic studies, animal histology and finite element analyses
f.intervention: Platform switching (abutment narrower than the implant platform)
f.main_result: Most reports conclude that platform switching prevents crestal bone loss, but the evidence is limited in quantity and quality.
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by a JSPS Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research
f.limitations: Scientific evidence is lacking in both quantity and quality.

f.population: 60 titanium implants in edentulous mandibular areas of 5 hounds
f.intervention: Two-piece non-submerged implants with microgaps of <10, 50 or 100 µm, abutments screwed on
f.comparison: Laser-welded abutments allowing no movement between components
outcomes: distance from the interface to the first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: Bone-to-implant contact lay more apically with screwed than welded abutments (about 1.7 vs 1.2 mm from the interface), independent of microgap size.
materials_brands: Straumann titanium test implants with SLA surface
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grants and Swiss society and foundation stipends

f.population: 130 dental implants placed and restored by 24 post-graduate students
f.intervention: C1 implants placed and restored by inexperienced post-graduate students
outcomes: 24 patient, site, implant and prosthetic variables
f.main_result: Five implants failed before loading; survival 96.15%, success 94.62%, mean MBL 0.53 mm at 1 year, affected by diabetes, implant depth, KT and probing depth.
f.funding_coi: Funded by MIS Implants Technologies; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Authors describe it as a short-term cohort study.

f.population: 115 patients with 417 dental implants placed with static computer-assisted implant surgery
f.intervention: Clinical and radiographic assessment of implant and prosthetic parameters (implant connection, loading, CIR, surface, prosthesis type, emergence angle, cantilever, etc.)
f.main_result: Peri-implantitis OR 2.16 for removable versus fixed prostheses; marginal bone loss linked to higher interproximal contact level, greater emergence angle, shorter abutment height, longer cantilever and anodized surface.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Cross-sectional design

f.population: 87 patients with missing incisors receiving 108 zirconia cantilever RBFDPs
f.intervention: Single-retainer zirconia ceramic cantilever resin-bonded FDPs bonded with Panavia 21 TC or Multilink Automix
f.comparison: Groups by reason for missing incisors: congenital, trauma, other
f.main_result: 10-year survival rate 98.2% and success rate 92.0%; reason for missing incisors had no significant influence.
f.limitations: Few debondings and only one failed RBFDP in the trauma group limited statistical analysis

f.main_result: Single-retainer zirconia RBFDPs: 5-year complication-free rate 93.3% and 100% survival in a cited randomized trial.
Cited evidence: RBB survival 87.7% at 5 years (systematic review) and 80.4% at 10 years (771 bridges); case selection and design drive longevity.
Contemporary cp grade 4 titanium, TiZr and micro-rough zirconia implants are well tolerated and osseointegrate quickly (mostly animal data).

f.population: 9 studies of deep-learning identification of dental implant systems on panoramic and periapical radiographs
f.intervention: Deep-learning algorithms identifying and classifying dental implant systems
f.main_result: Pooled sample 46,645 with overall accuracy 92.16%; range 70.75% to 98.19%.
f.funding_coi: Funded by a National Research Foundation of Korea grant; no conflict of interest reported
f.limitations: High risk of bias and applicability concerns in most studies

f.main_result: PFM, veneered Zr and monolithic Zr iFDPs and splinted crowns had similarly high short-term survival; veneered restorations chipped more often than monolithic ones.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: Patients with 3-4 mm subantral residual bone (case reports)
f.intervention: 6 mm short Anyridge implants with deep threads placed without sinus augmentation
f.main_result: Short deep-thread implants engaged in 3-5 mm of ridge bone without sinus augmentation gave successful rehabilitation in the reported cases.

materials_brands: MegaGen AnyRidge healing abutments, impression copings and EZ Post final abutments

f.population: Two edentulous mandible patients with narrow ridges (61- and 73-year-old women) in the ridge-split report, plus posterior mandible narrow-ridge cases
f.intervention: Ridge split with Piezo and AnyRidge implant placement, grafted with FDBA
f.limitations: Authors note ridge splitting needs experience and bone fracture of the buccal plate can occur

f.population: Seven clinical cases of single-tooth replacement, including extraction sites, a compromised molar and a ridge needing GBR
f.intervention: AnyRidge implant placement, with provisional restorations and in some cases GBR with titanium mesh or Bio-Oss
Bioactive approaches for GTR membranes and the use of polycaprolactone
f.funding_coi: Faculty of Dentistry Research Fund, Chulalongkorn University
f.limitations: Authors state further investigations are required

f.population: Healthy adults (18-82 years, smokers excluded) needing vertical bone augmentation with GBR or GTR before dental implants
f.intervention: Eleven barrier membrane types used for vertical GBR/GTR
f.comparison: Other membranes in a network comparison, with non-crosslinked collagen membrane the most frequent comparator
f.main_result: A titanium-reinforced e-PTFE membrane may be the best choice for vertical GBR/GTR; membrane exposure and soft tissue complications were relatively common
f.sample_size: 27 articles in the review, 19 in the network meta-analysis, 530 patients

f.population: Laboratory cell cultures and an ex-ovo chick chorioallantoic membrane assay
f.intervention: A bilayer PCL barrier membrane: 250 µm photocurable PCL polyHIPE layer plus an electrospun nanofibrous PCL layer
f.main_result: The electrospun PCL layer limited cell infiltration for at least four weeks, while the PCL polyHIPE supported cell infiltration, mineral deposition and blood vessel ingrowth
f.funding_coi: Turkish Ministry of National Education, EPSRC and MRC grants; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Authors say in vivo performance of the membrane still needs to be explored

f.population: Maxillary bone lesion model with human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells on membranes
f.intervention: PCL biomembrane functionalized with BMP-2 and seeded with hBM-MSCs
f.comparison: Non-functionalized PCL membrane
outcomes: filling of the lesion by new bone
f.main_result: The PCL membrane with BMP-2 and hBM-MSCs gave faster bone regeneration in the maxillary lesion
f.funding_coi: Fondation des Gueules Cassées and INSERM; no conflict of interest

f.intervention: Selective review of new resorbable GBR membrane materials: modified collagen, aliphatic polyesters, platelet rich fibrin and silk
f.main_result: Resorbable membranes with new materials aim to improve physical properties and bone regeneration, but clinical data are limited
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Authors note clinical research data remain limited

f.population: Partially edentulous healthy human subjects who received or were to receive dental implants (edentulous ridges and peri-implant dehiscence sites)
f.intervention: GBR for horizontal ridge augmentation or for peri-implant dehiscence defects, analysed by membrane exposure
f.comparison: GBR sites without membrane exposure versus sites with exposure
outcomes: percentage of horizontal bone gain at edentulous ridges
percentage of peri-implant dehiscence defect reduction
f.main_result: Sites without membrane exposure achieved 74% more horizontal bone gain at edentulous ridges and 27% more defect reduction at peri-implant dehiscence defects than sites with exposure.
f.limitations: All included studies were judged to have moderate to high risk of bias.

f.population: Rabbit bone marrow-derived MSCs in vitro and rabbit calvarial defects in vivo
f.intervention: Electrospun PBSGL (poly(butylene succinate-co-glycolate)) membranes with increasing glycolate ratio (PBSGL10, 20, 40)
f.comparison: PBSGL0 membrane without glycolate
f.main_result: Higher glycolate ratios gave better MSC attachment, metabolic activity and osteogenic potential, and more bone formation in rabbit calvarial defects with no adverse inflammatory response.
f.sample_size: 5 rabbits per time point, 4 calvarial defects each

f.population: 13 patients, each with 2 maxillary premolars scheduled for orthodontic extraction
f.intervention: e-PTFE membrane over the extraction socket, flap replaced so the membrane remained intentionally partially exposed (Group II), removed at 4 weeks
f.comparison: Group I: flap rotated to completely cover the e-PTFE membrane
outcomes: radiographic alveolar depth, width and area
f.main_result: Covered membranes (Group I) gave significantly higher clinical and radiographic bone gain than intentionally exposed ones (Group II) for all parameters (p<0.05), e.g. alveolar depth 12.01 vs 10.23.

f.population: Patients needing alveolar ridge augmentation before or with implant placement (review topic)
f.intervention: GBR with barrier membranes with or without particulate bone grafts or bone substitutes
f.main_result: GBR can be achieved with particulate autogenous grafts, allografts, xenografts or alloplasts combined with resorbable or non-resorbable barrier membranes in 1-2 tooth defects.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared.

f.population: Macor dental ceramic specimens
f.intervention: Rotary ultrasonic machining varying spindle speed, feed rate, coolant pressure and ultrasonic power (response surface methodology)
f.main_result: Best surface roughness was 0.5130 um at run 17 (lower feed rate, moderate other parameters); feed rate was the most influential factor.

f.population: Sintered pellets of mica glass ceramic with 0-20 wt.% yttria-stabilised zirconia (laboratory specimens)
f.intervention: Addition of 3 mol% YSZ (5-20 wt.%) to fluorophlogopite mica glass ceramic
f.comparison: Pure mica glass and commercial IPS e.max Press lithium disilicate
f.main_result: With 20 wt.% YSZ: hardness 9.2 GPa, elastic modulus 125 GPa, indentation toughness 3.6 MPa·m1/2 and solubility about 30 µg/cm2, within ISO limits.
f.sample_size: At least 5 specimens per composition (10 for solubility)
f.funding_coi: Wellcome Trust DBT India Alliance fellowship; Department of Biotechnology, Government of India

f.population: Workpieces: Macor-M and Bioram-M machinable glass-ceramics, composite resin typodont tooth enamel and bovine enamel
f.intervention: Weight-load cutting with a diamond point in an air-turbine handpiece at applied loads of 20 to 80 g
f.comparison: Composite resin typodont tooth enamel and bovine enamel
f.main_result: Macor-M showed the second-most reduced cutting speed and the maximum cutting volume, whereas Bioram-M showed the least reduced cutting speed and the minimum cutting volume.
materials_brands: Nissin A20-500 composite resin typodont teeth
f.funding_coi: Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research, Ministry of Education, Science and Culture, Japan

f.population: Macor machinable glass ceramic bars used as the cutting substrate
f.intervention: Mouthwash (Scope) added to handpiece coolant water at 1:1, 1:2.5, 1:5 and 1:10 with medium-grit diamond and cross-cut carbide burs
f.comparison: Distilled water coolant
outcomes: change in cutting rate over prolonged cutting
f.main_result: Mouthwash:water 1:5 and 1:10 mixtures raised carbide bur cutting rates from 0.21 to 0.64 and 0.66 mm/s, and also raised diamond bur rates, versus water alone.
f.sample_size: 6 burs per irrigant mixture, 3 cuts each

f.population: Mandibular edentulous patients rehabilitated with implant-retained overdentures
f.intervention: Mini-implants retaining mandibular overdentures
f.comparison: Standard-diameter implants retaining mandibular overdentures
f.main_result: Mini-implants had fewer abutment adjustments (RR 0.23), retentive-element replacements (RR 0.41), occlusal adjustments (RR 0.53) and overdenture fractures (RR 0.46), with similar pain, probing depth, bone loss and survival.
f.funding_coi: Supported by CNPq, CAPES and FAPESP grants
f.limitations: Certainty of evidence was mostly very low to low.

f.population: 71 primary studies (in vitro and in vivo) testing mouthwashes against viruses of the oral cavity
f.intervention: antimicrobial mouthwashes (CHX, PVP-I, essential oils, CPC, H2O2, others) used to reduce viral load
f.main_result: Essential oils, cetylpyridinium chloride and povidone-iodine showed antiviral potential with no significant side effects in short-term use; other solutions need further studies.
f.funding_coi: No specific funding; no competing interests declared
f.limitations: Other solutions need further randomized clinical studies with larger patient numbers and more controlled situations.

f.population: 100 patients with congenitally missing maxillary lateral incisors, one implant each
f.intervention: Ø2.9 mm narrow-diameter Roxolid SLActive implant with cement-retained bi-layered zirconia crown
f.comparison: Ø3.3 mm implant of the same type
f.main_result: 1-year implant survival was 99%; CBL change was -0.19 ± 0.25 mm (Ø2.9) vs -0.25 ± 0.31 mm (Ø3.3), not significantly different.
f.sample_size: 100 implants in 100 patients (50 per group); 7 dropouts
f.funding_coi: ITI Foundation grant; implants and components supplied free by Straumann AG; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Non-randomized allocation by mesio-distal space, cemented crowns only, soft tissue dehiscence not assessed, short 12-month follow-up.

f.intervention: computer-assisted/guided implant surgery (CT-based planning, image-guided navigation, RP-CT surgical guides)
f.comparison: conventional implantation techniques
f.main_result: Image-guided templates and RP-CT-based surgical guides give similar accuracy and allow precise implant positioning, at higher cost and training demands than conventional implantology.
f.limitations: Little has been done regarding patient demands, including cost; techniques are complex and need training.

f.intervention: mill, polish and adhesively seat n!ce glass-ceramic restorations (crowns, partial crowns, inlays, onlays, veneers)
materials_brands: Straumann n!ce fully crystallized glass-ceramic blocks
Twist Step Drills and Screw Taps

f.intervention: Minimally invasive nonsurgical therapy (MINST) with magnification, minicurettes and thin ultrasonic tips, plus the periodontal endoscope
f.comparison: Conventional scaling and root planing, and minimally invasive surgery (MIST)
f.main_result: MINST gave PPD reduction of 3.13 mm and CAL gain of 2.56 mm at 6 months in intrabony defects, similar to MIST (3.51 mm and 2.85 mm), with half the chair time
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Limited evidence; histological and biologic-mechanism data on MINST healing are lacking

f.intervention: Description of occlusal patterns, jaw movements and posterior occlusal morphology in the class III (macrognathic mandible) patient
f.main_result: Class III patients lack anterior guidance, so occlusal morphology is dictated by condylar movement and mandibular size, balancing contacts are physiologic, and 0.5 to 1 mm rest interocclusal distance suffices
Lecture slides review the history and concepts of complete denture occlusion, favouring a balanced articulation while noting no occlusal scheme is proven superior

Overview of occlusal concepts for full mouth rehabilitation (gnathologic, freedom in centric, PMS, Hobo twin-stage, Wiskott-Belser); authors favour posterior disclusion and cusp-to-fossa contacts, with no single rule for all patients

f.population: 43 squirrel monkeys (Saimiri sciureus), wild-raised on tough natural foods versus laboratory-raised on soft artificial diet
f.intervention: Rearing on a soft artificial diet
f.comparison: Rearing on naturally tough (hard) foods
f.main_result: Soft-diet monkeys had occlusal deviations in 14 of 18 versus 3 of 22 on hard diets, with more tooth displacement and narrower arches
f.sample_size: 43 squirrel monkeys (24 hard diet, 19 soft diet)
f.funding_coi: NSF grants and Wright State University research services

f.population: 413 subjects in 11 experiments: bruxism, temporomandibular disorders, headache with TMD, chronic cervical pain
f.intervention: Occlusal adjustment therapy
f.comparison: Mock adjustment or a comparison treatment
f.main_result: Data from the 11 experiments did not show greater efficacy of occlusal adjustment than control or contrasting therapy
f.limitations: Included studies were small, mostly unblinded or uncalibrated examiners, mixed disease groups

f.population: A 79-year-old man missing maxillary left first and second molars
f.intervention: Digital functionally generated path (FGP) technique with intraoral scanner, FGP wax table and design software to design an implant-supported fixed prosthesis
f.main_result: The method designed an interference-free prosthesis and can reduce chairside time

f.population: Fellows of the Academy of Prosthodontics
f.intervention: CR Attributes Survey on definitions of centric relation (5 domains, agree-uncertain-disagree)
f.main_result: 100 of 146 fellows responded (68.5%); strong agreement that CR is clinically determined, repeatable, independent of tooth contact and a starting point for movements; insufficient evidence on condyle and disk position
f.limitations: Attributes with weak agreement indicate need for further research

f.population: 17 Rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta), 5 on soft diet, 11 analysed as hard-diet controls
f.intervention: Soft diet mixed to the consistency of fudge for 4 to 14 months before sacrifice
f.comparison: Hard diet (Purina Monkey Chow biscuits)
f.limitations: Small samples, and dietary differences were not maintained over the animals' lifetime

f.population: 62 subjects with single-tooth implants opposed by natural teeth
f.intervention: Active tactile sensibility test with interocclusal copper foils of 0 to 200 µm, analysed by logistic regression
f.comparison: Implant surfaces: titanium plasma-sprayed, sandblasted/acid-etched, machined
f.main_result: Mean 50% tactile threshold was 20.2 ± 10.9 µm; sandblasted/acid-etched implants were more sensitive than plasma-sprayed (mean difference 8 µm, P = .016)

f.population: Eskimos in Alaska and Indians in northern and central Canada at various stages of modernization
f.main_result: No dental caries occurred in Eskimo and Indian groups living on a diet adequately reinforced with minerals and activators; caries rose to 30 to 50 per cent of teeth with liberal contact with modern foods.

f.intervention: Four-stage Dawson Academy protocol: functional-esthetic analysis, three-dimensional treatment planning, prototype restorations, definitive restorations
f.main_result: Predictable, durable, esthetic restorations are said to come from a reproducible four-stage protocol.

f.population: 89 patients with unilateral posterior missing teeth (38 men, 51 women)
f.intervention: Unilateral posterior tooth loss analyzed on panoramic and cephalometric radiographs
f.comparison: 20 patients without missing posterior teeth or orthodontic treatment
f.main_result: Patients with unilateral missing teeth had lower articular eminence inclination, smaller cranio-cervical angle and fewer occlusal planes passing through the C1-C2 intersection.
f.sample_size: 178 joints from 89 patients, plus 40 control joints
f.funding_coi: Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau

f.intervention: Gnathological method versus Pankey-Mann-Schuyler technique for oral rehabilitation
f.main_result: The two methods achieve similar results via different routes.

f.population: Clinical human studies with at least 10 implants
f.main_result: Seven articles were identified; occlusal overloading was positively associated with peri-implant marginal bone loss.
f.funding_coi: No financial interest declared
f.limitations: Significant heterogeneity among study methodologies, mostly retrospective

f.population: 8 New Zealand white rabbits, 12 weeks old
f.intervention: Unilateral molar extraction
f.comparison: Non-extraction side of the same rabbit
f.main_result: At 12 weeks bone metabolism was 39.96% on the extraction side versus 60.04% on the non-extraction side (P < .05); calcium and osteoclast differences were not significant.
f.funding_coi: National Research Foundation of Korea

f.population: 109 consecutive patients with mandibular implant-supported fixed prostheses opposing maxillary complete dentures
f.intervention: Mandibular implant-supported fixed prostheses (Branemark system)
f.main_result: Occlusal factors were of limited importance for patient satisfaction and treatment outcome; 61% had bilateral balanced occlusion and mean bone loss was 0.5 mm.

f.population: 100 Eskimo children aged 11 to 20 from Kotzebue, Alaska
f.comparison: Average values for a white population
f.main_result: 82 per cent of the children had malocclusion; Class I predominated and arch widths did not differ between normal and malocclusion groups.
Little scientific evidence supports a direct cause-effect relationship between occlusal factors and deleterious biological outcomes for osseointegrated implants.
f.limitations: Most articles reviewed were descriptive, so findings were reported descriptively rather than as a systematic review

f.main_result: There is currently no evidence-based, implant-specific concept of occlusion; guidelines are based on biomechanics and limited in vitro, animal and retrospective data.
Gnathological concepts offer a structured methodology for prosthodontic procedures, but further research is needed to corroborate current occlusal treatment approaches.
Published data suggest that a peripheral sensory feedback pathway can be restored with osseointegrated implants (osseoperception).

f.funding_coi: Course made possible through an unrestricted educational grant

f.population: Human in vivo studies of crowns, removable prostheses and implant-borne reconstructions
f.main_result: There is little scientific evidence specifying occlusal and superstructure design for fixed prostheses on teeth or implants, and no evidence that a particular design is superior.
Subjects with a history of TMD adapt less well to experimental occlusal interferences than subjects without, and individual vulnerability differs.
f.limitations: Human studies are limited by small sample size, short observation time and low interference intensity.

f.population: One test patient with deflective occlusal contacts
f.main_result: Analysis of stress direction in centric versus eccentric closures discloses one of the important causes of pathologic wear of teeth and effects on supporting structures.
The occlusal perception threshold is higher for implant-supported prostheses than for natural dentition, so clinicians should not rely on patient perception when checking occlusion.

f.population: 741 individuals aged 21-60 years with missing posterior teeth, 386 with and 355 without TMD
f.comparison: TMD group versus prosthetic group without TMD signs or symptoms
outcomes: presence of TMD signs and symptoms
association with gender, age, number of missing posterior teeth and number of quadrants with missing posterior teeth
f.main_result: Fewer missing posterior teeth but spread over more quadrants, plus younger age and female gender, were associated with higher TMD prevalence (OR 0.51 for number missing, 7.71 for quadrants).
f.funding_coi: National Nature Science Foundation of China (NSFC) No. 30540130469

f.population: 20 complete denture wearers (46 to 80 years) with clinically unsatisfactory dentures
f.intervention: Occlusal correction of gross prematurities, denture adhesive, and soft tissue-conditioning reline, applied in sequence
f.comparison: Original dentures before modification
outcomes: ipsilateral and contralateral masseter EMG activity
f.main_result: The three denture modifications did not significantly change masseter EMG activity or masticatory performance (maximum improvement 2.4% after occlusal correction; p > .05).
f.funding_coi: Supported by the Medical Service of the Veterans Administration
f.limitations: Testing was done at the same sitting, so patients had no time to adapt neuromuscularly to each modification, and the order of conditions could not be randomized.

f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest
No financial support; no conflict of interest
Author denies any conflicts of interest

f.population: Patients in RCTs of osseointegrated dental implants placed in 1- versus 2-stage procedures (5 RCTs, 239 patients)
f.intervention: 1-stage (non-submerged) implant placement
f.comparison: 2-stage (submerged) implant placement
f.main_result: No statistically significant differences in prosthesis or implant failures between 1- and 2-stage placement, with trends favouring 2-stage implants in fully edentulous patients.
f.limitations: The number of patients in the trials was too small to draw definitive conclusions.

f.population: 84 partially dentate patients needing 115 fixed partial dentures, implants in posterior load-carrying regions
f.intervention: Astra Tech implants placed with a one-stage non-submerged protocol
f.comparison: Two-stage submerged installation protocol
outcomes: radiographic bone-level change from FPD placement to 1 and 2 years
f.main_result: Bone-level change during function was small and unrelated to submerged versus non-submerged healing (year-1 bone loss 0.02 mm group A vs 0.17 mm group B).

f.population: 40 edentulous patients (Cawood & Howell class V-VI) receiving mandibular overdenture treatment
f.intervention: Two IMZ two-part implants inserted in a one-stage procedure
f.comparison: Two-stage surgical procedure
f.main_result: No striking clinical differences between groups; mean bone loss in the first year was 0.6 mm in both.

f.population: 30 consecutive patients with extremely resorbed maxillae
f.intervention: Iliac crest (ala iliaca) onlay bone graft with endosseous implants in a one-stage procedure
f.comparison: Development group (first 10 patients) versus routine group (following 20 patients)
f.main_result: Marginal bone loss averaged 4.6 mm up to the 3-year examination in the routine group with no significant change to 10 years; implant success rate was 83.1% in the routine group.

f.population: Extensive alveolar bone deficiency (technique description; number of patients not stated)
f.intervention: Two-tier intraoral autogenous block graft (ramus, then ramus or symphysis 5 months later) before implant placement
f.main_result: A multitier intraoral block graft technique is described as an option for extensively atrophic alveolar bone augmentation; no outcome data are reported.
f.funding_coi: No financial interest declared
f.limitations: The technique requires several operations, which could cause patient discomfort.

f.population: 70-year-old woman on bisphosphonates (alendronate, then ibandronate) with right maxillary sinusitis and oroantral communication after implant placement
f.intervention: Functional endoscopic sinus surgery plus two-layer closure with pedicled buccal fat pad and buccal advancement flap
f.main_result: Healing was uneventful and complete after 4 months, with no new oroantral communication or oral lesions at 12 months.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: The buccal fat pad can only be used once and the size of defects it can cover is limited.

f.population: Three patients with large oroantral defects
f.intervention: Reconstruction with a pedicled buccal fat pad
f.main_result: Follow-up photography and imaging showed successful closure of the oroantral defects, with no operative site complications and no patient-reported discomfort.
f.funding_coi: Funding not applicable; no competing interests

f.population: Patients with chronic orofacial pain (head and neck cancer, MS-related trigeminal neuralgia-like symptoms, post-herpetic neuralgia, TMD, burning mouth syndrome)
f.intervention: Cannabis and cannabinoid medications (self-administered cannabis, topical PEA, topical cannabis extract, cannabis sativa oil, nabiximols, nabilone)
f.main_result: Of 8 included sources, 6 concluded the cannabinoid treatment gave some therapeutic benefit for chronic orofacial pain and all concluded it was safe.
f.funding_coi: No specific grant funding; no competing interests declared
f.limitations: The included studies are few, small and have significant limitations preventing definitive conclusions.

f.population: Partially or fully edentulous patients (14 included studies)
f.intervention: Implant-supported prostheses
f.comparison: Conventional prostheses or no therapy
f.main_result: Meta-analyses showed no benefit of implant-supported over conventional prostheses for alveolar bone resorption, but a significant benefit for masseter muscle thickness.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no competing interests
f.limitations: Only one included study was an RCT.

f.main_result: Osseointegration is proposed to be the lack of a negative tissue response rather than an advantageous biological response.

f.population: One male foxhound (18 months, 38 kg) with an unintentionally retained palatal root of the first molar
f.intervention: One sandblasted, acid-etched titanium implant placed next to the retained root, 8 weeks non-submerged healing
f.main_result: Mean contact of osteodentin/osteocementum to the implant was 67.4% versus 63.5% bone-to-implant contact at the vestibular aspect.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded by the authors’ department; no conflict of interest

f.population: Clinical studies using RFA and/or Periotest
f.intervention: Resonance frequency analysis and Periotest
outcomes: validity and prognostic value for detecting implants at risk of failure
f.main_result: Single readings with either technique are of limited clinical value, and their prognostic value for predicting loss of implant stability remains to be established in prospective studies.
f.sample_size: A limited number of clinical reports
f.funding_coi: One author is affiliated with Nobel Biocare
f.limitations: No randomized controlled trials or prospective cohort studies were found for validity testing.

f.population: 20 implants in 20 patients lost before loading, from 3,786 implants placed
f.intervention: ISQ by resonance frequency analysis at placement (immediate) and at 4 months (delayed)
f.comparison: 56 randomly selected stable implants
f.main_result: Immediate and delayed ISQ were significantly related to early failure (OR 4.27 and 9.20), but ISQ was judged unreliable for predicting it.
f.sample_size: 3,786 implants evaluated; 20 early failures in 20 patients; 56 controls
f.funding_coi: Supported by FEDICOM and Junta de Andalucía; no financial interests in listed products

f.population: 158 patients with edentulous mandibles receiving a single midline implant
f.intervention: Immediate loading of a single midline implant with a ball-attachment overdenture
f.comparison: Delayed (conventional) loading three months after implant placement
f.main_result: Immediate loading had significantly lower 5-year implant survival (9 failures vs 2 in delayed loading; p=0.011) and non-inferiority was not shown.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft; one author reports grants and fees from Camlog, Straumann and others
f.limitations: Results of the 5-year follow-up should be interpreted exploratively.

f.population: Studies of CAD-CAM removable partial denture frameworks: 2 clinical and 5 in vitro studies
f.intervention: Digital (CAD-CAM) fabrication of RPD frameworks
f.comparison: Conventional lost-wax cast frameworks / conventional impressions
f.main_result: The digital technique for RPD frameworks is accurate, with clinically acceptable discrepancies (<311 µm); PEEK frameworks fitted better than cast metal and Co-Cr made by laser melting showed the highest discrepancies.
f.limitations: Results were heterogeneous because studies used different measurement methods; only 2 clinical studies assessed frameworks.

f.population: Edentulous patients wearing a maxillary complete denture opposed by a mandibular implant overdenture or a complete denture
f.intervention: Maxillary CD opposing a mandibular 2-implant overdenture (IRO)
f.comparison: Maxillary CD opposing a mandibular complete denture
outcomes: blood flow in anterior maxillary mucosa (laser Doppler)
f.main_result: IRO produced greater blood flow disturbance (103 vs 183 BPU initially) and about three times more anterior maxillary bone volume loss than CD (7.3% vs 2.6% at 1 year).
f.funding_coi: Funded by Universiti Teknologi MARA and a Malaysian research grant; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Unequal group sizes (9 vs 4) due to ethical limits on repeat CBCT

f.intervention: ACP classification system for partial edentulism (Class I to IV) based on four diagnostic criteria: edentulous area, abutment condition, occlusion, residual ridge
f.main_result: The ACP defines a four-class diagnostic classification of partial edentulism, from uncomplicated (Class I) to complex (Class IV).
f.funding_coi: Funded by the American College of Prosthodontists
f.limitations: The system is not a predictor of treatment success.

f.population: 41 edentulous maxilla patients receiving implant prostheses (193 implants)
f.intervention: CAD/CAM titanium-bar overdenture and CAD/CAM implant fixed prosthesis
f.comparison: Conventional soldered gold-bar overdenture
f.main_result: Maintenance rates were 1.24 (gold OD), 1.36 (Ti OD) and 0.98 (IFP) events/year, not significantly different; OHIP was significantly better for the fixed prosthesis.
f.limitations: Randomization was not used; patients chose their prosthetic option.

f.population: Completely edentulous patients rehabilitated with implant-supported fixed complete dentures or implant overdentures (28 studies, 1457 patients)
f.intervention: Implant-supported fixed complete dentures (IFCDs)
f.comparison: Implant overdentures (IODs)
f.main_result: Both prosthesis types produced large positive effects on dPROs (IFCD ES 1.68, IOD ES 1.26, no significant difference); only denture stability was rated higher for IFCDs, and two implants beat one for mandibular IODs.
f.funding_coi: Open access funding by Universitat Bern; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Findings should be interpreted cautiously given high heterogeneity and limited direct comparisons.

f.population: 103 patients with mandibular two-implant overdentures (206 implants)
f.intervention: Mandibular overdentures on two implants with Dolder bar with cantilever (36), Spherblock ball (58) or Locator (9) attachments
f.comparison: Splinted cantilever bar versus unsplinted ball/Locator attachments
outcomes: gingival and plaque index, pocket depth, BOP
f.main_result: Implant survival was 100% with 0.22 mm mean bone loss at 5 years; ball attachments had more complications (wear, fracture) while bar attachments needed fewer replacements and appointments.
materials_brands: Straumann tissue-level implants and Dolder bar
f.funding_coi: Funded by Isfahan University of Medical Sciences; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Only two practitioners, no randomization, small Locator group (n=9) and retrospective design.

f.population: Edentulous patients with 2-implant mandibular overdentures (16 RCTs, 599 participants, 1198 implants)
f.intervention: Different overdenture attachments (ball, bar, LOCATOR, telescopic, magnet) with delayed or immediate loading
f.main_result: All attachment types with immediate or delayed loading had similar effects on peri-implant health; bar+immediate loading ranked best for bone loss and ball+delayed loading for probing depth.

f.population: 12 completely edentulous patients (aged 50-70) receiving two mandibular canine implants
f.intervention: Two-implant mandibular overdenture on a Co-Cr bar with 7 mm bilateral distal extensions
f.comparison: Co-Cr bar with no distal extensions
outcomes: posterior ridge resorption on panoramic radiographs at 6 and 12 months
f.main_result: No significant difference in posterior ridge resorption between bars with and without distal extensions (12-month mean ratio 0.310 vs 0.381, p=0.236).
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 40 disks of one CAD-CAM PMMA denture base resin (Polident)
f.intervention: Milling with a new tungsten carbide bur set
f.comparison: Milling with a used tungsten carbide bur set (250 PMMA crowns previously milled)
f.main_result: New-bur specimens had higher Ra (about 1.3 vs 0.93 micrometer) and lower contact angle (70 vs 80 degrees) than used-bur specimens (P<.05); thermocycling lowered the contact angle of used-bur specimens to 66 degrees.

f.population: 19 in vitro studies of 3D-printed resins (provisional, denture base, occlusal device, orthodontic, denture teeth, surgical guide)
f.intervention: Factors affecting flexural strength (fillers, printing orientation, layer thickness, post-polymerization, rinsing)
f.main_result: Most factors (fillers or nanofillers, printing orientation or angulation, layer thickness, post-polymerization time and temperature) significantly affected flexural strength; no meta-analysis was possible.

f.population: 74 edentulous patients with mandibular overdentures retained by four titanium-zirconium mini implants (296 implants)
f.intervention: Four Ti-Zr mini implants (Straumann Mini Implant System) retaining a mandibular overdenture, placed flapless or flapped and loaded immediately or delayed
f.comparison: 2x2 factorial: immediate vs delayed loading and flapless vs flapped surgery
f.main_result: 1-year implant survival/success was 100% with no major biological complications; mean marginal bone loss was 0.68 mm at 3 months and 0.89 mm at 1 year, slightly higher with flapless surgery.
materials_brands: Straumann Mini Implant System (Roxolid Ti-Zr, SLA)
f.funding_coi: ITI grant 1447_2019; implants and components supplied by Institut Straumann AG; three authors received other Straumann/ITI funding
f.limitations: Short 1-year timeframe; longer follow-up and patient-centered outcomes are needed.

f.population: Edentulous patients treated 2006-2015 in a Dutch general practice with 2, 3 or 4 implants and a mandibular overdenture (295 treated)
f.intervention: Two, three or four interforaminal implants with a bar-clip attachment and mandibular overdenture
f.comparison: 2-implant vs 3-implant vs 4-implant groups (non-randomized)
f.main_result: Cumulative implant survival was 100%, 99.1% and 97.8% in the 2-, 3- and 4-implant groups with mean bone loss of 0.53, 0.61 and 0.40 mm; satisfaction was high.
materials_brands: Dyna Helix implant system (Dyna Dental Engineering)
f.funding_coi: No funding was acquired

materials_brands: LOCATOR R-Tx removable attachment system (ZEST Anchors)

f.population: 31 edentulous-maxilla patients aged 50+ with a dentate or implant-restored mandible
f.intervention: 5-6 flaplessly placed one-piece mini dental implants with provisional denture, final overdenture connection at 6 months
f.main_result: 164 of 204 MDIs (78.4%) were in situ at 3 years; OHIP-14 fell from 21.3 at baseline to 7.3 at final connection (p=0.006), improving less with multiple implant losses.
f.funding_coi: MDIs provided by Southern Implants

f.population: 18 patients with maxillary complete dentures opposing mandibular implant-retained overdentures and 4 with conventional dentures
f.intervention: Mandibular two-implant (Ankylos) overdenture opposing a maxillary complete denture
f.comparison: Conventional maxillary and mandibular complete dentures (4 patients)
outcomes: anterior maxillary bone volume change on CBCT at 1 year
f.main_result: Anterior maxillary bone volume fell 7.25% with the overdenture versus 2.60% with conventional dentures (p=0.011).
f.funding_coi: Funded by Universiti Teknologi MARA and Malaysian FRGS grant; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Pilot study with a very small control group because repeat CBCT in controls was deemed unethical

f.population: 40 edentulous participants with maxillary complete dentures and mandibular two-implant overdentures
f.intervention: CAD-CAM milled titanium bar with long distal extensions plus gold clip
f.comparison: Retentive anchors with gold matrices
f.main_result: At 1 year implant survival was 100% and peri-implant bone level change did not differ (p=.754); bite force, OHIP-EDENT and satisfaction index were equal, with subjective chewing better in the milled-bar group (p=.022).
f.funding_coi: ITI research grant 767_2011; authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: No sample size calculation was possible because of lack of reference data.

f.population: 67-year-old edentulous woman (single case)
f.intervention: Two freestanding mandibular implants with a metal-reinforced overdenture on stock abutments and hinge-type resilient attachments, attachments incorporated in the laboratory

f.population: Edentulous participants with maxillary denture complaints and insufficient bone volume, treated with sinus augmentation
f.intervention: Maxillary bar overdenture on four posterior implants
f.comparison: Maxillary bar overdenture on six posterior implants
f.main_result: Implant survival was 100% (4 implants) vs 96.7% (6 implants); marginal bone loss 0.41 vs 0.70 mm; no significant group differences
materials_brands: Straumann Standard SLA implants, 2.8 mm polished collar, 4.1 x 12 mm RN
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from Institut Straumann AG for the 1-year trial; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Loss of power for marginal bone change after 10 years, and university-based setting with selected participants

f.population: Edentulous maxilla participants with opposing mandibular two-implant overdentures (mean age 68.3 years)
f.intervention: Four maxillary implants loaded asynchronously: two unsplinted cylindrical attachments, then the other two
f.comparison: Two anterior (canine) versus two posterior (molar) implants carrying the overdenture, in a cross-over
f.main_result: Implant survival after loading was 93.8% at a mean 3.1 years; denture survival 100%, denture success 95.8%; 23 of 24 preferred four implants
f.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI; no conflict of interest

f.population: In vitro studies of 3D-printed dental prosthetic materials (ceramics, polymers, metals)
f.intervention: 3D additive manufacturing (AM) of prosthetic materials
f.comparison: Subtractive milling and conventional processing
f.main_result: Milling showed higher flexural strength than AM (Hedge g -3.88, 95% CI -7.20 to -0.58, P=.02); marginal discrepancy was similar

f.intervention: Milled bar implant overdenture with OT Equator attachments and an internal cast metal framework
materials_brands: Vitapan Plus anterior and Lingoform posterior teeth

f.main_result: Post selection depends on many factors including root length, tooth anatomy, remaining tooth structure and function; post length improves retention and stress distribution

f.population: Wearers of mandibular free-end removable partial dentures
f.intervention: Two 6 mm short implants bilaterally in mandibular molar sites with retentive ball abutments
f.comparison: Non-retentive dome abutments (crossover)
f.main_result: Implant survival 100% and success 90.9% at 12 months; mean bone loss 1.2 mm; 82% finally chose the ball abutment
f.funding_coi: Innosuisse and SIC invent AG funding; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Small number of participants and short follow-up

materials_brands: Straumann LOCATOR FIXED housing and inserts
ZEST Anchors LOCATOR implant, bar and root attachments

f.population: Five male cynomolgus monkeys with 4 implants per mandibular side
f.intervention: Repetitive mechanical trauma on implants, with or without ligature-induced peri-implantitis
f.comparison: Healthy implants without repetitive mechanical trauma
f.main_result: Repetitive mechanical trauma showed no histologic effect on peri-implant bone loss in healthy or diseased implant sites
f.funding_coi: Supported in part by Nobel Biocare

f.main_result: Fracture healing depends on both host biology and the mechanical environment; NSAIDs, bisphosphonates, smoking, diabetes and age can impair it.
f.funding_coi: No financial disclosures

f.main_result: Mucositis can progress to peri-implantitis with circumferential bone loss while the implant stays osseointegrated; BOP, probing depth and radiographs are the sensitive diagnostic parameters and CIST is proposed for maintenance.

When strain falls below the resorption threshold osteocytes undergo apoptosis followed by bone resorption; loading maintains osteocyte viability and strains above the formation threshold release anabolic factors and drive bone formation.

f.population: Periodontally treated, partially dentate patients with free-standing implant-supported FPDs
f.intervention: Implant-supported FPDs with distal cantilever extensions (Astra Tech implants)
f.comparison: FPDs without cantilever extensions
outcomes: Change in peri-implant bone level from FPD placement to 5 years
f.main_result: Mean marginal bone loss was 0.4 mm over 5 years with no significant difference between FPDs with and without cantilevers; maxillary FPDs lost more bone than mandibular (0.6 vs 0.2 mm).
f.sample_size: 50 FPDs in 45 patients (24 with, 26 without cantilever)

f.population: Animal studies (dogs) of non-splinted titanium dental implants
f.intervention: Occlusal overload on osseointegrated implants
f.comparison: Implants without overload, with or without plaque control
outcomes: Radiographic and histologic distance from implant base to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: Two high-risk-of-bias trials: overload caused no tissue breakdown without plaque but, with plaque, increased peri-implant breakdown (PD change 5.3 mm; DIB 6.0 mm); overload tended to increase bone density.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Few studies, no RCTs, high risk of bias, heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis

f.population: Human and animal studies on occlusal trauma, excessive occlusal forces, abfraction and gingival recession
f.main_result: Occlusal trauma does not initiate periodontitis and only weakly, if at all, alters its progression; there is no credible evidence for abfraction as a cause of gingival recession.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Occlusal trauma can only be confirmed histologically, so clinical trials rely on surrogate indicators; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis

f.population: Six Labrador dogs with 45 titanium implants (TPS and SLA) in the mandible
f.intervention: Gold crowns in supra-occlusal contact on implants for 8 months (excessive occlusal load) with plaque control
f.comparison: Unloaded implants on the control side
f.main_result: After 8 months of excessive occlusal load all implants stayed osseointegrated with no marginal bone loss versus unloaded implants (BIC 74% test vs 73% control).
materials_brands: ITI Dental Implant System (TPS and SLA implants), gold crowns

f.population: 4 monkeys (Macaca fascicularis) with 5 Astra Tech titanium screw implants each in the mandible
f.intervention: Fixed partial prosthesis in supra-occlusal contact causing lateral occlusal overload on 2 implants (18 months)
f.comparison: Non-cleaned implants with cotton cord to promote plaque accumulation
f.main_result: Plaque-accumulation implants stayed osseointegrated with 2.4 mm mean histologic bone loss; overloaded implants mostly became loose, with 2 losing osseointegration completely and 2 only apically.
f.sample_size: 4 monkeys; 8 overloaded implants (6 histologically analysed) and plaque-accumulation implants
materials_brands: Astra Tech titanium screw implants (TiO2-blasted and machined)
Pallorag silver-palladium alloy fixed partial prosthesis
f.limitations: Statistical analysis not performed because few overloaded implants were available

f.population: Ten 18-month-old male Gottingen minipigs, 80 implants in maxilla and mandible
f.intervention: Experimental implant design with high insertion torque (wide thread, limited marginal bone contact)
f.comparison: Astra Tech OsseoSpeed 3.5S control implant
outcomes: Distance from shoulder to first bone-to-implant contact
f.main_result: The experimental high-torque implant caused significantly more marginal bone loss than the control (first BIC 2.94 vs 1.7 mm), with excessive marginal strains suggesting osseocompression.

f.population: Peri-implant bone of osseointegrated dental implants under excessive occlusal load (14 animal and clinical studies)
f.main_result: Evidence on excessive load on osseointegrated implants is limited and conflicting; overload may rarely cause loss of osseointegration, while functional load increases remodeling, BIC and bone density.
f.limitations: No RCTs or meta-analyses available; evidence limited and conflicting

f.population: Four beagle dogs with 32 machined titanium implants in the mandible
f.intervention: Supra-occlusal contact (overloaded) versus infra-occlusal (unloaded) abutments, with or without ligature-induced peri-implant inflammation
f.comparison: Unloaded implants and uninflamed (brushed) sides
f.main_result: Overloading in healthy mucosa increased BIC% and slightly increased crestal bone resorption, while with inflammation overloading significantly increased thread exposure from bone loss.
materials_brands: Hi-Tec Implant machined titanium implants (3.75 x 10 mm)
f.funding_coi: Funded by a Shauder grant
f.limitations: Limited sample size; load was not quantified directly

f.population: 38 partially edentulous patients (21-71 years) with 49 partial cantilever fixed prostheses on 100 implants
f.intervention: Implant-supported partial fixed cantilever prostheses (mesial or distal cantilever) on ITI and Branemark implants
f.comparison: Opposing dentition (natural teeth or tooth-supported fixed prostheses versus implant-supported fixed prostheses); mesial versus distal cantilever
f.main_result: Seven years after loading, overall cumulative implant survival was 97% and prosthesis success 98%, with mesial cantilevers 97.1% versus distal 100%.

f.population: 75 potential implant sites in the posterior mandible from CT scans of 34 patients; used to build finite-element models
f.intervention: Finite-element models with low/high cancellous-bone density, crestal cortical-bone density and thickness, loaded with 200 N oblique load on a Straumann implant
f.comparison: Low vs high bone-density and thin vs thick cortical-bone models
outcomes: maximum von Mises equivalent strain in crestal cortical bone
maximum von Mises equivalent strain in cancellous bone
f.main_result: Maximum strains in low-density cancellous-bone models were 1.56-2.62-fold (cortical) and 3.49-5.31-fold (cancellous) higher than in high-density models.
f.sample_size: 75 implant sites in 34 patients (CT); finite-element models
materials_brands: Straumann threaded implant, 4.1 mm x 10 mm

f.population: Literature on forces on oral implants and surrounding bone (animal experimental and clinical studies)
f.main_result: Animal studies show occlusal load may increase marginal bone loss, but in clinical studies a causative relationship with overload has not been established.
f.sample_size: 607 papers found in initial PubMed search
f.limitations: No randomized controlled or prospective cohort studies were found; a small number of experimental animal studies underlies much of the knowledge.

f.population: Five beagle dogs with 30 tissue-level implants (SLA and SLActive) in the mandible
f.intervention: Excessive occlusal load on implants restored with a crown plus cantilever unit
f.comparison: Single crown with stable occlusal contacts and non-loaded implants
outcomes: clinical parameters (BoP, attachment level, mucosal margin)
f.main_result: Excessive load did not cause loss of osseointegration or significant clinical or radiographic changes, but SLA implants gained peri-implant bone density and technical complications were more frequent.
materials_brands: Straumann SLA and SLActive tissue-level implants (8 x 3.3 mm)
f.funding_coi: Supported by ITI Foundation and Clinical Research Foundation; authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: Literature on early crestal bone loss around endosteal dental implants
f.main_result: Reformation of biologic width, microgap at or below the crest, occlusal overload and implant crest module are the most likely causes of early implant bone loss; surgical trauma and peri-implantitis may also contribute.
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by the University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund
f.limitations: Little evidence on the mechanism; no studies compare the possible causative factors, so randomized controlled trials are needed.

f.population: Clinical and animal studies on osseointegrated oral implants subjected to overload
f.intervention: Overload (e.g. supra-occlusal contacts)
f.comparison: No overload
f.main_result: Overload in uninflamed peri-implant tissue did not negatively affect osseointegration in animals, while with inflammation it increased plaque-induced bone resorption; clinical evidence was too biased to answer the question.
f.sample_size: 726 titles screened; 41 full texts (16 clinical, 25 animal)
f.funding_coi: Authors report no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: High risk of bias in many papers and lack of quantification of overload at the implant level

f.population: Preclinical and clinical literature on occlusal overload and peri-implant bone loss
f.main_result: Evidence does not support avoiding higher crown-to-implant ratios, cantilevers and non-splinted designs for fear of overload, and the impact of overload on peri-implantitis remains unknown.
f.funding_coi: No funding; author declares no competing interests
f.limitations: Non-systematic review; no randomized or prospective human trials exist on overload for ethical reasons

f.population: Edentulous jaws of all stages of atrophy; series of 100 consecutive arches
f.intervention: Complete arch immediate function with 4 implants (all-on-4) planned by a proposed site and jaw bone classification
outcomes: classification of edentulous jaw bone sites for immediate function
f.main_result: A functional-descriptive classification (Class A to D mandible and maxilla) based on cortical bone fixation sites guides angled implant placement for immediate function and mostly avoids grafting.
f.limitations: The minimum A/P spread acceptable for immediate loading has not been established

f.population: Implant-supported fixed prostheses in edentulous maxilla or mandible (29 studies, 26 datasets)
f.intervention: Different numbers of implants supporting a fixed prosthesis
f.main_result: The majority of studies plan 4 to 6 implants per prosthesis, with average survival rates between 90% and 100% and similar outcomes regardless of implant number.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: Twenty adult male Japanese white rabbits with 80 implants in the femurs
f.intervention: Abutment screw preload with recommended (35 Ncm) or high (70 Ncm) tightening torque
f.comparison: Control implants without abutment, and temporary tightening group without preload
f.main_result: Bone-to-implant contact, bone volume and bone area were significantly lower in recommended- and high-torque preload groups than in control and temporary-tightening groups.
materials_brands: Straumann Roxolid SLActive Bone Level implants (8 x 3.3 mm) and Narrow Connection Anatomic Straight abutments
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by Straumann Japan; authors affirm no conflicts of interest

f.population: Patients with osseointegrated dental implants (clinical human studies)
f.intervention: Implant occlusal overload assessed by digital occlusal analysis and/or occlusal wear
f.comparison: Absence of implant occlusal overloading
f.main_result: Of 7 included studies, only one used a digital device to assess occlusal forces; four of seven reported a positive correlation between overload and crestal bone loss, and all had moderate to serious risk of bias.
f.follow_up: At least 1 year after prosthetic loading in included studies
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: All included studies had moderate to serious overall risk of bias and methods for assessing overload were not standardized.

f.main_result: Peri-implant mucositis is a host response like gingivitis, whereas peri-implantitis may differ from periodontitis in lesion extent, cell composition and progression rate.
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted educational grant from Colgate; participants declared no conflicts of interest.

f.main_result: Fracture healing is a complex physiological process involving a well-orchestrated series of biological events.

f.population: 130 patients with 193 edentulous arches restored with 4 (or 5) implants
f.intervention: Immediately loaded full-arch implants (posterior tilted) with interim acrylic prostheses, then definitive CAD/CAM titanium-framework hybrid prostheses; cantilever length and AP spread measured
f.comparison: CL/AP ratios of definitive versus interim prostheses
f.main_result: Implant survival was 99.5% (770/774), mean CL/AP ratios were 0.84-0.90, and CL/AP ratio was not significantly associated with prosthetic repairs.
f.funding_coi: Author denies any conflicts of interest; no funding stated
f.limitations: Lack of recording of other clinical issues; AP-spread measurement accurate only to about 0.5 mm.

f.population: 514 Japanese patients with 1535 implants in function for at least 4 years
f.intervention: Analysis of systemic, intraoral and implant-related factors as risk indicators for marginal bone level change
outcomes: marginal bone level change (MBLC) on intraoral radiographs
f.main_result: Mean annual MBLC was 0.048 mm; functional time, plaque control record >20%, Eichner C1-3, maxilla, cement-retained superstructure and keratinized mucosa width <2 mm significantly affected MBLC.
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflicts of interest

f.main_result: The evidence is weak and does not indicate that overload causes peri-implant bone loss except with inflammation; micromotion compromises osseointegration whereas efficient force transfer may stimulate bone formation.
f.funding_coi: No additional funding; authors declare no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Overload has not been quantified at the implant level in the intra-oral setting.

f.population: Osseointegrated dental implants in animal and human studies
f.intervention: Static loading of implants (prosthesis misfit/passive fit, overload, orthodontic forces)
f.comparison: Controls (human trials with or without controls; animal studies with controls)
f.main_result: No apparent detrimental effect of static loading on osseointegrated implants across 36 studies (28 animal, 8 human).
f.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: No randomized controlled trials in humans were found; only eight human case series or retrospective reviews.

f.population: Four monkeys (Macaca fascicularis) with experimental implants
f.intervention: Supraocclusal superstructures with excess occlusal height of 100, 180 and 250 µm on inflammation-free implants
outcomes: peri-implant bone level change on histology
f.main_result: Bone resorption around implants tended to increase at 180 µm or more excess height, suggesting a threshold of about 180 µm.

f.population: 10 adult New Zealand black rabbits (tibiae)
f.intervention: Static (29.4 N transverse) or dynamic (14.7 N, 1 Hz, 2,520 cycles) loading of Brånemark implants for 14 days
f.comparison: Unloaded control implant
outcomes: bone density lateral to the implant
f.main_result: Dynamic loading produced crater-shaped marginal bone defects and significantly less peri-implant bone density (P<0.007), while static loading resembled unloaded controls.
f.funding_coi: Nobel Biocare Scholarship Grant 1996 and a Flanders scientific-research grant

f.main_result: Fracture healing should be understood through tissue deformation (strain, gap movement divided by gap width) rather than fracture mobility alone.

f.population: 98 bruxers identified among 2670 implant patients, plus a matched group of non-bruxers
f.intervention: Bruxism (graded possible/probable/definite) in patients with implant-supported prostheses
f.comparison: Matched group of non-bruxers
f.main_result: The odds ratio of implant failure in bruxers versus non-bruxers was 2.71 (95% CI 1.25-5.88), with more mechanical complications in bruxers.
f.sample_size: 98 bruxers of 2670 patients, matched with non-bruxers
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interests declared
f.limitations: Other risk factors may also have influenced the results.

f.population: Patients treated with dental implants at one specialist clinic in Malmo, Sweden; bruxers vs non-bruxers
f.intervention: Dental implant placement; exposure variable was bruxism
f.comparison: Bruxers versus non-bruxers
f.main_result: Bruxism was a significant risk factor for implant failure (HR about 3.4; failure 13.0% in bruxers vs 4.6% in non-bruxers).
f.funding_coi: Funded by Region Skane research funds, Swedish Research Council, Folktandvarden AB and CNPq; no conflicts declared

f.population: 1,052 students at Wayne State University (544 men, 508 women, mean age 19 years)
f.intervention: Questionnaire on present and past clenching or grinding, diurnal and nocturnal
outcomes: incidence of diurnal, nocturnal and combined bruxism
f.main_result: 30.7% of the sample reported present or past bruxism; diurnal bruxism was more common than nocturnal, men reported more diurnal and women more nocturnal bruxism
f.funding_coi: National Institute of Dental Research grant DE04536

f.population: Patients with implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses (ICFDPs) in five cohort studies
f.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed dental prostheses followed at least 5 years
f.comparison: Short-span implant-supported end-abutment fixed dental prostheses (for bone level changes)
f.main_result: Estimated 5- and 10-year ICFDP survival was 94.3% and 88.9%; veneer fracture and screw loosening were the most common complications
f.sample_size: 5 studies; 420 implants and 180 ICFDPs (354 and 155 available for analysis)

f.population: 14 participants missing 2 maxillary central incisors and 1 lateral incisor (6 men, 8 women, mean age 40 years)
f.intervention: Implant-supported cantilever fixed partial denture (ICFPD), 2 implants per participant
f.comparison: Implant-supported conventional fixed partial denture
f.main_result: Marginal bone loss was significantly higher for the implant near the cantilever (1.8 mm at 2 years); stability, gingival and plaque indices did not differ
f.funding_coi: Not funded by any institution
f.limitations: Small sample size

f.population: 30 patients with 34 FDPCs (31 SUCs and 3 FDPs) on 37 implants in posterior areas
f.intervention: Screw-retained full-zirconia implant-supported FDPs with cantilever extension
f.main_result: No implants lost; marginal bone levels (0.92 to 0.96 mm) and PPD (2.99 to 3.27 mm) did not change significantly; peri-implant mucositis in 22 cases
f.funding_coi: Funded by the authors' own institution; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 21 participants missing a single tooth (except canine), abutment teeth
f.intervention: Zirconia (Y-TZP) ceramic cantilever FDP retained by 2 complete crown abutments
f.comparison: Metal ceramic cantilever FDP
f.main_result: Survival was 100% in both groups; 6 complications in 5 participants (4 ZC, 2 MC); periodontal indices similar
f.limitations: Exploratory pilot with small sample; P values exploratory

f.population: 55 clinical cases of fixed complete implant-supported arch prostheses (3 to 8 implants)
f.intervention: Calculation of maximum permissible cantilever length with the Skalak model under a 143 N vertical load
f.comparison: Clinicians' optimal cantilever lengths
f.main_result: Predicted satisfaction was 100%, 56%, 33%, 8% and 0% for 8 and 7, 6, 5, 4 and 3 implants; 98% of cases with AP spread above 11.1 mm were satisfied

f.population: 192 partially edentulous patients with 454 implants in 2 included prospective cohort studies
f.intervention: Implant-supported reconstructions at different crown-implant (C/I) ratios
f.main_result: Survival was 94.1% for C/I ratio above 2; crestal bone loss seemed not influenced by C/I ratio except in one study
f.limitations: Diversity among studies in data collection and study design

f.population: Single-tooth, nonsplinted implant restorations in the posterior maxilla or mandible (8 studies)
f.intervention: Restoration with high crown-to-implant ratio
f.comparison: Similar restorations with a normal ratio
f.main_result: Implant survival above 99% per year and peri-implant bone change below 0.1 mm per year; few complications

f.population: Partially edentulous patients receiving at least 1 dental implant (15 studies)
f.intervention: Higher crown-to-implant ratio (>1.5)
f.comparison: Lower crown-to-implant ratio (<=1.5)
f.main_result: No significant correlation between anatomical C/I ratio and survival (P = .905), marginal bone loss (P = .33) or prosthetic complications (P = .67)

f.population: Adjacent dental implants (literature on splinted vs nonsplinted restorations)
f.intervention: Splinted restorations of adjacent implants
f.comparison: Nonsplinted (single-unit) restorations
f.main_result: No evidence that either splinted or nonsplinted design gives higher implant survival; splinted restorations have fewer technical complications
f.limitations: Very weak evidence available to support either choice

f.population: Patients with three adjacent external-hex implants in the posterior maxilla
f.intervention: Implants splinted with cemented metal-ceramic restorations (left maxilla)
f.comparison: Nonsplinted cemented single crowns (right maxilla)
f.main_result: At 10 years median bone loss was 1.2 mm splinted vs 1.3 mm nonsplinted (P = .0042); the 0.1 mm difference was judged not clinically meaningful.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: Photoelastic block model with three implants
f.intervention: Splinted cement-retained restorations at increasing crown-to-implant ratios and crown height spaces, loaded at 30 degrees
f.comparison: 1:1 crown-to-implant ratio group
f.main_result: Buccal microstrain rose from 1,911.65 to 3,252.06 as C/I went from 1:1 to 1:1.5 (P<.001); at 1:1.75 and 1:2 the abutment screw fractured and crowns dislodged.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare external hex implants 3.8 x 12 mm
f.limitations: Conclusions are limited to this biomechanical model

f.population: 660 partially edentulous patients with 1655 Brånemark implants loaded with fixed prostheses
f.intervention: Implants supporting single crowns, implant-tooth connected or free-standing fixed partial prostheses
f.comparison: Single crowns vs implant-tooth connected vs free-standing fixed partial prostheses
outcomes: effect of jaw, site, membrane or graft, dehiscence, prosthesis material
f.main_result: No significant difference in bone level change among the three restoration types; estimated loss was 1.23 mm/year in the first 6 months then 0.025 mm/year.

f.population: 660 partially edentulous patients with 1956 Brånemark system implants
f.intervention: Single crowns, implant-tooth connected and free-standing fixed partial prostheses
f.comparison: Implant-tooth connected vs free-standing prostheses
f.main_result: Cumulative 16-year survival was 91.4% for implants and 95.8% for restorations; implant-tooth connected 93.6% vs free-standing 97.2% from loading.
f.limitations: Exploratory study without multiple-testing correction; non-splinting finding needs replication

f.population: One 25-year-old woman with a failed implant at the maxillary left lateral incisor and lost papilla
f.intervention: Vertical ridge augmentation, implant, papilla CTG with EMD, zirconia abutment with convex subgingival contour

f.main_result: Rebuilding the interimplant papilla remains unpredictable; no technique is recommended over another because no long-term studies exist.

f.population: Patients with single tooth implants, immediate provisionalization or delayed 2-stage
f.intervention: Immediate provisionalization of single implants
f.comparison: Delayed 2-stage approach
f.main_result: No difference in papilla or bone levels between immediate and delayed protocols; vertical distance from contact point to bone, especially to adjacent tooth bone, predicted papilla score.
f.funding_coi: Grants from Nobel Biocare, Zimmer Dental, a university chair and the AAOMS Foundation

f.population: 26 patients with nonadjacent missing teeth in the esthetic zone
f.intervention: Curved (grooved) abutment
f.comparison: Conventional divergent abutment
f.main_result: No significant PES or VAS differences between curved and divergent abutments at baseline or 1 year; PES and VAS correlated significantly.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; Nobel Biocare supplied implants and abutments free

f.population: 48 patients with implant-supported fixed prostheses; 96 implant-implant and 80 tooth-implant interproximal sites
f.intervention: Measurement of vertical (contact point to bone crest) and horizontal (inter-implant or tooth-implant) distances against papilla presence
f.main_result: Papilla was absent 100% of the time at 2-2.5 mm lateral spacing and mostly present at 3-4 mm; ideal contact-point-to-bone distance was 3 mm between implants and 3-5 mm tooth-implant.
f.follow_up: fixed prostheses in function 18 months to 6 years

f.population: Patients with deficient interdental papillae (213 participants, 696 sites) in clinical studies
f.intervention: Injection of hyaluronic acid gel into the deficient interdental papilla
f.comparison: Mostly before-after (uncontrolled); some RCTs used saline, HA plus chitosan or a calcium hydroxide filler
f.main_result: Single-arm meta-analysis found complete papilla reconstruction in 47% (CI 35-59%) and partial reconstruction in 49% (CI 40-59%) of sites after HA injection.
f.funding_coi: No competing interests; MSc scholarship for one reviewer from CAPES
f.limitations: Short-term evidence, mostly uncontrolled studies; further long-term controlled studies needed

f.population: Three patients (cases 1-3) with maxillary single-tooth implant sites and soft tissue deficiency
f.intervention: Modified roll technique: papilla-sparing incisions and a pedicle connective tissue graft rolled facially without sutures on the graft, with implant placement
