f.main_result: LZS showed higher fracture toughness, Young's modulus and osteoblast proliferation and mineralization than alumina-containing LZSA.
f.sample_size: 5 disc specimens per group for mechanical tests; n=9 for cell assays
f.funding_coi: Supported by FCT, FEDER, CAPES and CNPq; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Authors acknowledge limitations of these in vitro studies and call for further bioactivity and mechanical study.

f.main_result: For posterior root filled teeth, all-ceramic crowns, onlays and endocrowns appear as predictable as metal-ceramic crowns, while minimally invasive concepts remain unproven clinically.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to validate restoration performance.

f.population: Endodontically treated permanent teeth with no more than two coronal walls remaining, restored with posts and cores
f.intervention: Prefabricated or custom fiber posts followed by indirect fixed restorations (crowns or FPDs)
f.comparison: Prefabricated or custom metal posts followed by indirect fixed restorations (crowns or FPDs)
f.main_result: Fiber posts had significantly higher 3-7 year survival than metal posts (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.97, P = .04), with no difference in success, debonding or root fracture.
f.funding_coi: National Natural Science Foundation of China
f.limitations: Only medium-term studies (3 to 7 years) with few included studies and small samples; conclusions should not be extrapolated to long-term.

f.main_result: The main purpose of a post is to prevent the tooth/core/post complex under a ferrule from separating from the root at the crown-margin level, not to retain the core.

f.population: Two-dimensional finite element models of a maxillary central incisor with weakened root
f.intervention: Restoration with glass fiber post or cast post and core, metal-ceramic or alumina-reinforced ceramic crown, with 2 mm ferrule or none
f.main_result: Cast post-and-cores concentrated stress at the post-dentin interface while glass fiber posts gave homogeneous dentin stress; a 2 mm ferrule improved stress distribution regardless of crown and post type.
f.sample_size: A sound tooth model and eight 2D numerical models
f.limitations: Authors state conclusions are valid within the limitations of this study (2D static load).

f.population: Thirty decoronated endodontically treated bovine incisors with a 2-mm ferrule plus 15 without ferrule
f.intervention: Direct composite buildup with a glass-fiber-reinforced post, under bonded e.max CAD glass ceramic crowns
f.comparison: Direct composite buildup without a post (ferrule group); no-ferrule group with post
f.main_result: Ferrule groups survived significantly more cycles than the no-ferrule group (p=0.001); adding a fiber post made no significant difference with a ferrule (p=0.884), and post groups had 100% unrestorable failures.
f.funding_coi: CAPES Foundation Brazil; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Within the limitations of this in vitro study

f.population: Forty endodontically treated lower first premolars restored with quartz fiber posts
f.intervention: Core build-up with one of four composite materials: Clearfil Photo Core, MultiCore Flow, LuxaCore Z-Dual, or nanohybrid Tetric N-Ceram
f.main_result: Fracture load was highest with Clearfil Photo Core (699.1 N), then MultiCore Flow (587.1 N), LuxaCore Z-Dual (483.1 N) and Tetric N-Ceram (451.4 N); core flexural modulus followed the same ranking.
f.funding_coi: Chulalongkorn University, Faculty of Dentistry Research Fund
f.limitations: Within the limitations of this study

f.population: Forty single-rooted human mandibular premolars (decoronated)
f.intervention: Cast post-and-core or glass-fiber post, with or without ferule
f.comparison: Groups without ferule and post type against each other
f.main_result: Fracture strength did not differ between cast post-and-core and fiber post, and the presence of ferule increased fracture strength with both post types.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 14 systematic/meta-analytic reviews of prosthetic restorations on endodontically treated teeth
f.main_result: Per low-risk reviews, fiber posts had higher success than metal posts, root fracture rates were alike, and endocrowns likely performed better than intracanal posts or direct composite.
f.sample_size: 14 systematic/meta-analytic reviews (9 low risk of bias, 5 moderate)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: More consistent studies are required to present the findings more confidently.

f.main_result: Adhesively luted glass fiber posts are the gold standard when a post is needed; fiber post is recommended in premolars with three or more coronal surfaces lost, and a ferrule is required when crowning.

Review proposes a risk-assessment classification of broken-down teeth based on achievable ferrule effect, with clinical guidelines; evidence for restoring extensively destroyed endodontically treated teeth is deficient.
f.limitations: Evidence on restoring extensively destroyed endodontic treated teeth is deficient.

f.funding_coi: Manfred Friedman declares no disclosures

f.population: Seventy-two bovine incisors restored as endodontically treated teeth
f.intervention: Fiber post versus cast post and core with 0 mm or 2 mm remaining coronal height and thickness above or below 1 mm, restored with metallic crowns
f.comparison: Cast post and core vs fiber post; groups without vs with remaining coronal structure
f.main_result: Groups without remaining coronal structure had lower survival (0.75 cast post, 0.83 fiber post) and thickness above 1 mm gave higher load to fracture (p=0.0043).

f.funding_coi: No competing interests declared

f.population: 24 extracted single-rooted human teeth, endodontically treated with 8 mm post space
f.intervention: Glass fiber posts cemented with Multilink Automix (phosphonic acid acrylate)
f.comparison: RelyX Unicem 2 Automix (phosphoric acid acrylate)
f.main_result: Degree of conversion was 67% for Multilink vs 26% for RelyX Unicem 2, and push-out strength was higher coronally than apically.
f.sample_size: 24 teeth, 12 per group, 3 slices per tooth
f.funding_coi: Authors declared no commercial interest in materials used

f.population: 50 endodontically treated permanent maxillary central incisors
f.intervention: Fiber-reinforced composite resin dowels molded to the root canal
f.comparison: Prefabricated fiberglass dowels (RelyX Fiber Post)
f.main_result: Fiber-reinforced composite dowels had thinner cement (apical 57.3 vs 131.6 µm) and higher push-out strength (22.98 vs 16.49 N/mm2) than prefabricated dowels.
f.funding_coi: No specific grant received

f.population: 50 extracted maxillary anterior teeth, endodontically treated
f.intervention: Residual axial tooth structure limited to half the circumference (palatal, labial or proximal), restored with quartz fiber posts, composite cores and metal crowns
f.comparison: Complete 360-degree axial structure versus level (no axial structure) groups
f.main_result: Median failure load was 607 N (complete), 782 N (palatal), 358 N (labial), 375 N (proximal) and 172 N (level).
materials_brands: Bisco quartz fiber post and composite resin core
f.funding_coi: Companies provided material contributions (Bisco, Dentsply Ceramco, Dentsply Tulsa Dental, Kerr)

f.population: 60 intact human maxillary central incisors, endodontically treated
f.intervention: Cast metal post-and-cores with 2-, 3- or 4-mm incomplete ferrules missing one interproximal wall, plus metal crowns
f.comparison: No ferrule and 2-mm complete ferrule groups, and a 6-mm incomplete ferrule control restored without post
f.main_result: An incomplete 2-mm ferrule reduced fracture resistance (697 N) versus complete ferrule (932 N); 3 to 4 mm walls restored it (844 N and 853 N).
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by the Dominican Republic Ministry of Higher Education Science and Technology

f.main_result: Residual tooth volume under 30% and fewer than two residual walls raise failure risk; indirect cuspal coverage outperforms direct restorations in posterior teeth; fibre posts survive comparably to metal posts.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.main_result: VRFs are most prevalent in root filled molars and high-level evidence on their prevalence, diagnosis and management is lacking.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: Adults with sufficient endodontic treatment needing a core or post
f.intervention: Post-endodontic treatment using posts with or without ferrule support
f.comparison: Post-endodontic treatment without posts, with or without ferrule support
f.main_result: Two of 3 studies support the ferrule effect, while 7 of 8 studies show no post effect.
f.sample_size: 7 randomized controlled trials and 1 prospective clinical trial
f.follow_up: minimum 5 years of observation in included studies
f.funding_coi: No specific grant; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Cochrane rating showed high risk of bias in 5 included studies

f.population: Extracted human mandibular first premolars, endodontically treated, decoronated to oblique residual roots
f.intervention: Simulated surgical crown lengthening or orthodontic forced eruption giving 1.0 or 2.0 mm buccal ferrule, restored with glass fiber post-and-core and Co-Cr crown
f.comparison: Control group with incomplete ferrule (0.0 mm buccal, 2.0 mm lingual)
f.main_result: Fracture resistance decreased with longer ferrule: control F0 1.01 kN highest, CL/F2 0.73 kN lowest, regardless of crown lengthening or forced eruption method.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Jiangsu Provincial medical youth talent grant; funder had no role; no competing interests

f.population: Extracted endodontically treated maxillary canines with thinned radicular dentin walls
f.intervention: Restoration with cast post, glass-fiber post (Radix) or I-TFC post
f.comparison: Composite resin only, no post
f.main_result: Cast post gave the highest fracture resistance (all non-restorable fractures), glass-fiber and I-TFC posts lower, no post lowest; fiber post fractures were repairable.
f.funding_coi: No financial support; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Participants with endodontically treated teeth with no remaining coronal wall
f.intervention: Glass fibre posts (White Post DC) with a single metal-ceramic crown
f.comparison: Cast metal (CoCr) posts
f.main_result: Survival rates of glass fibre and cast metal posts were similar after up to 3 years (97.1% and 91.9%; p = 0.682).
f.limitations: Longer follow-up is needed to detect possible differences between post systems over time

f.main_result: No single post-and-core system gives the perfect solution; fiber-reinforced posts are replacing metal posts because bonding adds strength.
f.funding_coi: Dr. Terry reports no conflicts of interest

f.population: Extracted single-rooted upper premolars, endodontically treated
f.intervention: Build-up with or without a 2 mm ferrule and with or without a fibre post, then all-ceramic crown and fatigue loading
f.comparison: No ferrule, no post group (NF–NP)
f.main_result: Ferrule significantly enhanced fracture resistance regardless of post use (p = 0.003); F–NP 758.52 N, F–P 647.58 N, NF–NP 361.52 N.
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by Research Foundation Flanders grant; materials donated by manufacturers

f.population: Human non-vital weakened roots
f.main_result: Remaining dental thickness was the preponderant factor in maintaining fracture resistance.

f.population: Patients treated with implant-supported rehabilitation at one clinic, with or without chronic intake of PPIs, SSRIs, antihypertensive or anti-inflammatory drugs
f.intervention: Chronic use of PPIs, SSRIs, antihypertensive and anti-inflammatory drugs (exposure)
f.comparison: Subjects not taking the specific drug
f.main_result: Anti-inflammatory drug use was associated with peri-implantitis (p = .04; 2.7-year drop in mean survival time); no correlation for the other drugs.
f.limitations: Retrospective design implied substantial heterogeneity in subjects, restorations and follow-up length

f.population: Patients with implants placed with low primary stability (manual rotation)
f.intervention: Implants placed with low primary stability, with protected unloaded healing
f.comparison: Simple versus advanced surgery groups
f.main_result: Cumulative survival was 94.74% at implant level and 94.33% at patient level; all 7 failures were in the advanced surgery group (p = 0.005).
f.funding_coi: Supported by National Research Foundation of Korea grant; no conflict of interest

f.population: Consecutive SLA Straumann implants placed in two private clinics
f.intervention: Classification of primary stability by rotation on tightening the healing cap (A–D) and RFA (Osstell)
f.main_result: Survival was 99.1% for stable (A) and 97.2% for unstable (B–D) implants; only secondary stability RFA values predicted outcome.

f.population: Patients with single implant-supported restorations (53 patients, 212 measurements)
f.intervention: Cementation of metal-ceramic crowns with margins at tissue level or 1, 2, 3 mm subgingival, then cleaning
f.comparison: Margin at tissue level
f.main_result: Undetected cement increased as the margin was located deeper subgingivally, and radiographs missed remnants.

f.population: 945 partially edentulous subjects with 1010 cemented implant restorations (26 publications, 21 study groups)
f.intervention: Excess cement as risk indicator for peri-implant disease around cemented implant restorations
f.comparison: Cemented versus screw-retained restorations
outcomes: prevalence of peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis
proportion of diseased sites with excess cement
f.main_result: Excess cement was a possible risk indicator for peri-implant disease; 1.9-75% of implants with cemented restorations were diseased, 33-100% of them with excess cement.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Pronounced heterogeneity of study designs made meta-analysis inappropriate.

f.population: 39 consecutive patients with 42 cemented implants showing signs of peri-implant disease, plus 20 healthy control implants in 12 of them
f.intervention: Dental endoscope examination and removal of excess cement
f.comparison: Implants without signs of inflammation served as controls
outcomes: clinical and endoscopic signs of peri-implant disease at 30 days
f.main_result: Excess cement was found at 34 of 42 diseased implants and no controls; 25 of 33 had no inflammation 30 days after cement removal.
f.sample_size: 20 controls and 42 test implants in 39 patients
f.funding_coi: Funded solely by the author; no conflicts of interest

f.population: 55 patients (partially edentulous, adults) with 134 implants
f.intervention: Implant placed at equicrestal, subcrestal or supracrestal apico-coronal position
f.comparison: Subcrestal versus equicrestal or supracrestal placement
f.main_result: Subcrestal placement reduced odds of exposed threads but linear crestal bone loss was similar to equicrestal or supracrestal placement.
f.limitations: Conclusions hold within the limits of a retrospective chart review.

f.population: 139 individuals with 394 implants (192 single crowns, 202 fixed partial dentures) at a German university
f.intervention: Cement-retained implant restorations
f.comparison: Screw-retained implant restorations
f.main_result: No association between retention type and peri-implant disease (crude OR 1.43 for peri-implantitis, 0.89 for mucositis).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Relatively few peri-implantitis cases in the cement-retained group.

f.main_result: Smoking and previous periodontitis raise peri-implant disease risk; no gold standard treatment exists and continuous assessment with individualised supportive care is key.

f.population: 14 dental 3D printers (resin LCD/DLP/SLA) reviewed by Australian and New Zealand clinicians
Partial or totally edentulous patients undergoing dental implant surgery
f.intervention: Systemic antibiotic prophylaxis of any type, dose or timing
f.comparison: Placebo, no antibiotic, or a different regimen
f.main_result: Antibiotics reduced early implant failure (RR 0.30, 95% CI 0.19-0.47); a single preoperative dose was enough (RR 0.34 vs no antibiotic).
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: 20 subjects aged 30-50 with posterior single-tooth implants opposed by natural teeth
f.intervention: Active tactile perception testing by biting on shim stock foils of 8-56 micrometers
f.comparison: Contralateral natural tooth versus natural antagonist
f.main_result: Implant threshold was 24 ± 8 µm versus 12 ± 4 µm for natural teeth, with no difference by age, sex or jaw.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest

f.main_result: Implant-supported prostheses give better tactile discrimination and motor function than complete dentures, though not matching dentate individuals.

f.population: Animal and human studies on osseoperception and tactile sensibility of dental implants
f.comparison: Patients wearing complete dentures
outcomes: neurophysiological and histological evidence of osseoperception
f.main_result: Patients with implant-supported prostheses reported improved tactile and motor function compared with complete denture wearers.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Literature on osseoperception in dental implants is very scarce.

f.main_result: Most cited studies favor PRF over controls across oral and maxillofacial uses, but there is no standard PRF protocol.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures
f.limitations: Standard protocols and more randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm surgical indications.

f.main_result: The authors conclude PRF is the best of PRP, PRGF and PRF, mainly for simpler preparation and higher leukocyte share (about 65%).
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.main_result: PRP gels lost credibility in oral surgery, while L-PRF membranes fit periodontal and dentoalveolar surgery and enabled the NTR and NBR concepts.
f.funding_coi: Supported by the LoB5 Foundation for Research; no competing financial interests declared
f.limitations: Contradictory literature on poorly characterized products; validated protocols are lacking.

f.main_result: Low-dose oral bisphosphonate intake for osteoporosis is not associated with increased implant loss or complications; high-dose antiresorptive therapy is a contraindication to implants and bone grafting.
f.limitations: Knowledge on low-dose subcutaneous and intravenous antiresorptive drugs is insufficient to draw conclusions.

f.main_result: PRF lacks occlusivity, stiffness and space maintenance, so it does not qualify as a barrier membrane, though it improves wound healing.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: PRF resorbs within about 7 to 28 days, shorter than the 4-6 weeks needed, which compromises space maintenance.

f.population: Human patients with periodontal intrabony defects in prospective clinical trials
f.intervention: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) for regeneration of intrabony defects
f.comparison: Other conventional periodontal regeneration treatments such as bone grafts and barrier membranes
f.main_result: Pooled attachment level gain with PRP was 0.58 mm (P=.0008) and bone level gain 0.76 mm (P=.007); pocket depth difference was 0.55 mm (not significant).
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by the Department of Periodontics and Oral Medicine, University of Michigan
f.limitations: High heterogeneity among studies made clear conclusions difficult.

f.population: 60 included studies: 18 in vitro, 5 animal, 6 case reports, 31 clinical studies on I-PRF
f.intervention: Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (I-PRF) in regenerative dentistry
f.main_result: Of 60 included studies, I-PRF showed anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and regenerative effects on wound, periodontal, bone, cartilage and pulp tissue, and faster orthodontic tooth movement; periodontal parameters in vivo lack consensus.
f.funding_coi: Funding stated as none; part of the research supported by NIDCR/NIH grants; no competing interests declared
f.limitations: Only English-language studies included; further randomized clinical trials recommended.

f.population: Humans with lack of alveolar bone and/or need of implant therapy or tooth extraction
f.intervention: PRP alone or with a graft material in guided bone regeneration and implant therapy
f.comparison: The same surgical procedure without PRP
f.main_result: Seven studies showed superior outcomes with PRP in sinus floor elevation and five showed none; no meta-analysis was possible.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interests declared; authors report grants from Osteology Foundation and Swiss bodies
f.limitations: Risk of bias was moderate to high and study designs too heterogeneous for meta-analysis.

f.population: Patients needing bone, cementum, soft tissue and/or PDL gain
f.intervention: Dental regenerative treatments combined with PRF as sole or combined biomaterial
f.comparison: Defined regenerative approaches without PRF
f.main_result: In 35 RCTs PRF was mostly favorable for intrabony defects and gingival recession soft tissue repair, but data on bone formation in GBR and sinus lifting were scarce.
f.limitations: Lack of well-conducted studies on PRF in hard tissue bone regeneration.

f.population: Abutment teeth of distal-extension removable partial dentures (technique description, no study sample)
f.intervention: RPA clasp (rest, proximal plate, Akers clasp arm) as an alternative to the RPI clasp
f.comparison: RPI clasp (rest, proximal plate, I-bar)
f.main_result: The RPA design gives essentially the same tooth release as the RPI clasp, is easier to grasp for removal, and can be used where the RPI clasp is contraindicated.

f.population: 9 partially edentulous participants (Kennedy class I, II, III) needing RPD frameworks
f.intervention: RPD frameworks made by analog, combined analog-digital and fully digital (intraoral scan, 3Shape CAD, SLM Co-Cr) workflows
f.comparison: Fully analog (PVS impression, waxed and cast) vs combined analog-digital vs fully digital
outcomes: Clinical acceptability of framework fit by 7 yes/no criteria rated by 5 clinicians
f.main_result: The fully digital framework was significantly better than analog and combined (P<.001); analog was better than combined (P=.008); 7 of 9 patients received the digital framework.
f.limitations: Authors note conclusions hold only within the limitations of this small clinical study.

f.population: Partially edentulous patients treated with implant-assisted RPDs (37 included articles)
f.intervention: Implant-assisted removable partial dentures
f.comparison: Conventional removable partial dentures (discussed qualitatively)
f.sample_size: 37 articles (4 reviews, 7 in vitro, 19 case reports, 5 retrospective, 1 RCT, 1 crossover)
f.limitations: All included studies had weaknesses in level of evidence and no statistical analysis was possible given heterogeneous designs.

f.population: 42 mandibular edentulous patients with 154 implants treated with IC-RPD or implant overdenture
f.intervention: Implant-crown-retained RPD (splinted implant survey crowns) in mandibular edentulism
f.comparison: Implant overdentures retained by magnet attachments
f.main_result: Implant survival was 98.3% for IC-RPD vs 92.5-92.6% for IOD (p=0.116); final MBL 0.93 vs 2.12 mm (p=0.554), not significantly different.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Korean government grants (NRF and Korea Medical Device Development Fund); no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Observation time and sample sizes differed between the two groups; retrospective design.

f.funding_coi: Author has nothing to disclose

f.population: One 61-year-old systemically healthy woman with Seibert Class III atrophy of the posterior left mandible
f.intervention: Inlay (interpositional) technique with an allograft block, then two implants after 2 months
f.main_result: Mean vertical bone above the canal rose to 11.5 mm (gain 5.5 mm) at 2 months; the coronal bone segment fractured at implant surgery but two implants were placed on the stable block.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Coronal bone fracture was a partial failure, likely due to the short interval before implant placement; more studies are needed.

f.population: One male patient with vertical atrophy of the left posterior mandible
f.intervention: Guided inlay block 'sandwich' osteotomy using a CBCT-based milled surgical template and allogenic block
outcomes: Safety of osteotomy near the nerve
f.main_result: The template-guided horizontal osteotomy was done close to the nerve without risk, with no neurological complications and uneventful 3-month healing; 2 implants were placed.

f.population: 11 systemically healthy patients (DO 5, inlay 6) aged 25-55 with resorbed edentulous posterior mandibles
f.intervention: Alveolar distraction osteogenesis of a segmental osteotomy, then implants
f.comparison: Inlay (interpositional) monocortical iliac crest bone graft
f.main_result: DO produced more bone height than inlay grafting (P=.003) with more complications; bone resorption (P=.088) and implant success did not differ.
f.follow_up: Median 26 months (18-48) after prosthetic loading, both groups

f.population: Six partially edentulous patients (7 sites) with resorbed posterior mandibles, 6-9 mm bone above the canal
f.intervention: Sandwich osteotomy with interpositional iliac crest graft, then implants
f.main_result: Implants could be placed at all sites; none of 21 implants failed and bone resorption was minimal at 14-16 months, with a median vertical gain of 6-7 mm.
f.limitations: The interpositional procedure corrects only vertical defects and gives minimal horizontal correction; small number of patients.

f.population: One 53-year-old woman with a severely atrophic edentulous posterior mandible
f.intervention: Bilateral inlay augmentation with inorganic bovine bone block (Bio-Oss) and collagen membrane, then implants
f.main_result: Mean mandibular bone height gain was 4.6 mm (right) and 4.3 mm (left); no implant loss, and histology showed new vital bone at the graft interface.

f.population: 20 systemically healthy patients with resorbed partially edentulous posterior mandibles
f.intervention: Inlay (interpositional) iliac crest bone graft, then implants after 3-4 months
f.comparison: Onlay (appositional) iliac crest bone graft
f.main_result: Inlay vs onlay: median bone gain 4.9 vs 6.5 mm, bone resorption 0.5 vs 2.75 mm, final augmentation 4.1 vs 4 mm (p=.190); implant survival 100% in both groups.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 10 partially edentulous patients with 5-7 mm residual crestal height above the mandibular canal (bilateral posterior mandibles)
f.intervention: Interpositional (inlay) block graft of iliac crest bone
f.comparison: Interpositional block of anorganic bovine bone (Bio-Oss)
f.main_result: Significantly more residual graft (10-13%) in the Bio-Oss group; after loading both groups lost marginal bone (0.82 mm autogenous, 0.59 mm Bio-Oss) without a significant difference between them.
f.funding_coi: Geistlich (Italy) donated Bio-Oss blocs and resorbable barriers

f.population: 6 patients with inadequate bone in the posterior maxilla and at least one impacted maxillary third molar
f.intervention: Lateral sinus elevation with particulate autogenous impacted third molar tooth material (mixed with scraped bone)
f.main_result: No bleeding on probing, probing depth about 1.9-2.1 mm, peri-implant bone stable up to 5 years; histology showed osteoconductive osteogenesis with encapsulation of enamel and dentin particles.
materials_brands: BioOss (Geistlich) bovine bone substitute, added in two patients
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Small number of patients, preliminary results

f.population: A 30-year-old woman with bilateral severely atrophic posterior mandible
f.intervention: Inlay augmentation with allograft block (left side)
f.comparison: Inlay augmentation with allograft particulate (right side)
f.main_result: Mean vertical bone gain was 3.9 mm (right, particulate) and 4.4 mm (left, block); histology showed newly formed bone without inflammation and a tight block-to-basal bone connection.
f.follow_up: 3 months from grafting to implant placement; no longer follow-up reported
materials_brands: OraGraft allograft block and particulate (LifeNet Health)
Mectron Piezosurgery inserts OT8R, OT8L, OT7
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 10 partially edentulous patients needing bilateral vertical augmentation of the posterior mandible (5-7 mm residual height)
f.intervention: Interpositional (inlay) iliac crest bone block
f.comparison: Interpositional anorganic bovine bone block (Bio-Oss)
outcomes: time to recover mental nerve sensitivity
f.main_result: Both procedures gave significant bone gain without significant difference; Bio-Oss sides recovered nerve sensitivity faster (4 vs 6.3 days) and patients preferred Bio-Oss.
f.follow_up: up to 1 month after delivery of final restorations
materials_brands: Gebrüder Martin titanium miniplates and miniscrews
f.funding_coi: Geistlich (Italy) donated Bio-Oss blocks and barriers
f.limitations: Small number of patients

f.population: 62-year-old man with Seibert class II atrophy of the right posterior mandible, over 10 mm thick, 5.6 mm residual height above the canal
f.intervention: Two-stage inlay: buccal and lingual corticotomies, then inlay with equine bone block 1 month later
f.main_result: Mean vertical bone gain of 11.5 mm at 2 months (9.9, 12.2 and 12.3 mm at the three measuring points) with no neurosensory disturbance.
f.funding_coi: No financial interest declared

f.population: 5 patients (3 partially, 2 totally edentulous) with vertical bone over 10 mm but ridge width of 3 mm or less
f.intervention: Split-crest (greenstick fracture) technique with immediate implants covered by e-PTFE membranes
f.main_result: Ridge width gain of 1-4 mm, larger in maxillary (3-4 mm) than mandibular (1.0-1.5 mm) sites; histology showed bone regeneration between the split crest portions.
f.follow_up: 6 months of healing to stage-two surgery

f.intervention: Surgical and combined prosthetic-surgical approaches to cover peri-implant soft-tissue dehiscence
outcomes: factors affecting peri-implant soft-tissue margin stability
f.main_result: Incorrect implant placement, thin buccal soft tissue and bone and reduced buccal bone height are most associated with dehiscence; coronally advanced flap with connective tissue graft is the recommended surgical technique.
f.limitations: Most studies on dehiscence coverage are case reports or case series

f.population: Two stone master casts (mandibular and maxillary), eight stone replicas each, with simulated gingival recession marks
f.intervention: 3D optical scanning with superimposition to compute gingival recession volume
f.main_result: Volumetric measurement of simulated recession was highly reproducible, with intraclass correlation coefficients between 0.997 and 0.999.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: In vitro on stone replicas; clinical trials are needed to confirm

f.population: Three patients: two with multiple Miller class I recessions, one needing extraction of a root-fractured upper lateral incisor with immediate implant
f.intervention: Anchored vertical and horizontal mattress sutures on splinted contact points with tunnel technique
f.main_result: One week after suture removal, favorable soft tissue relocation and integrity were observed (qualitative, no measurements).
materials_brands: N'Durance Dimer Flow (Septodont) flowable resin for splinting
f.funding_coi: No sources of funding declared

f.population: 3 patients (12 bicuspids) with surgically created Miller Class I and II gingival recession, teeth planned for orthodontic extraction
f.intervention: EMD+CAF (enamel matrix derivative with coronally advanced flap) for root coverage
f.comparison: CTG+CAF (connective tissue graft with coronally advanced flap), one tooth per patient
outcomes: histologic periodontal regeneration (new bone, cementum, inserting fibers)
f.main_result: 7 of 9 EMD+CAF teeth showed histologic periodontal regeneration (corroborated by micro-CT) versus none of 3 CTG+CAF teeth; clinical measurements were comparable.
f.funding_coi: Supported by Straumann USA, LLC; two authors give company-sponsored lectures
f.limitations: Few patients, not statistically powered, surgically created recession defects, possible root resorption and ankylosis

f.population: Gingival recession at single and multiple teeth, and soft-tissue deficiencies at implants
f.intervention: Surgical root coverage and soft-tissue augmentation procedures (CAF with CTG, EMD or other adjuncts)
f.comparison: CAF alone and CAF plus GTR
f.main_result: Moderate-strength evidence that adding CTG or EMD to CAF improves outcomes at single recessions; evidence for implant soft-tissue procedures too heterogeneous for conclusions.
f.sample_size: Multiple recession review: 8 trials, 188 subjects, 719 recessions
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted educational grant from Geistlich AG; participants declared industry fees and grants
f.limitations: Heterogeneity among studies prevents conclusions for implant soft-tissue deficiencies

f.population: 50 gingival recessions (36 incisors, 7 canines, 5 premolars, 2 molars) in 29 females and 6 males aged 10 to 60
f.intervention: One-stage free autogenous gingival graft (about 1.5 mm thick) with a specific multi-suture adaptation technique to cover denuded roots
f.main_result: In 50 recessions, root coverage averaged 95.5% for recessions under 3 mm and 76.6% for those over 5 mm; 39 of 50 covered 80% or more and 22 covered 100%.
f.sample_size: 50 recessions selected randomly from 200 clinical cases
f.limitations: Authors note the suturing procedures are demanding and histology of graft attachment is unavailable

f.population: Forty young systemically and periodontally healthy subjects (20-38 years) with isolated Miller class I or II upper-jaw recessions
f.intervention: Modified coronally advanced flap (altered flap thickness and surgical papilla dimension, split-full-split)
f.main_result: Mean root coverage was 98.6% of baseline recession depth at 1 year and 96.7% at 3 years, with keratinized tissue increasing by 1.78 mm.
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: 60 subjects with single Miller class I or II upper-jaw gingival recessions of 3 mm or more
f.intervention: CAF plus extraoral de-epithelialized free gingival graft of reduced size (thickness under 2 mm, height 4 mm)
f.comparison: CAF plus larger graft (thickness 2 mm or more, height equal to bone dehiscence)
f.main_result: Small grafts gave less analgesic use (1100 vs 2520 mg) and better color match with no difference in root coverage; gingival thickness gain was greater with big grafts.
f.funding_coi: No funding; no conflict of interest, self-supported by the authors

f.population: Adults with single or multiple gingival recession defects or keratinized tissue deficiency (RCTs on root coverage)
f.intervention: Biologics (autologous blood-derived products/PRF, EMD, rhPDGF-BB) as adjuncts to coronally advanced flap
f.comparison: CAF alone and SCTG + CAF
f.main_result: SCTG+CAF gave significantly higher mean root coverage (+13.41%) than CAF alone, whereas EMD+CAF (+6.68%) and PRF+CAF (+1.03%) did not differ significantly.
f.sample_size: 48 RCTs (55 articles), 24 in the network meta-analysis; 1114 participants
f.funding_coi: Consensus meeting sponsored by BioHorizons, Geistlich, Lynch Biologics and Straumann; authors report no conflicts
f.limitations: Only four trials were at low risk of bias

f.population: Gingival augmentation and root coverage procedures in periodontal plastic surgery
f.intervention: Minimally invasive approaches to gingival augmentation and root coverage
f.main_result: Key influencing factors for minimal invasiveness are control of flap tension, proper flap design without unnecessary incisions, graft dimensions limited to site needs, and wound stability.
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared

f.population: Fifty patients with Miller class I or II gingival recession at first molars
f.intervention: Laterally moved coronally advanced flap (LMCAF)
f.comparison: Bilaminar technique (CAF plus connective tissue graft)
f.main_result: Complete root coverage was achieved in 48% (12/25) with the bilaminar technique versus 4% (1/25) with LMCAF (odds ratio 22.1), while mean recession reduction did not differ significantly.
f.sample_size: 50 patients, one molar recession each (25 per group)
f.funding_coi: Self-funded; no conflict of interest

f.population: Single and multiple recession-type defects (Miller Class I or II, 3 mm or more)
f.intervention: Root coverage periodontal plastic surgery procedures (SCTG, ADMG, EMP, GTR, xenogeneic matrix, PRF, each with CAF)
f.comparison: SCTG + CAF and CAF alone as main comparators
f.main_result: SCTG + CAF gave greater recession reduction than GTR rm + CAF (MD -0.37 mm) and greater keratinized tissue gain than EMP + CAF (MD -1.06 mm); evidence mostly low quality.
f.limitations: Only 1 of 48 RCTs at low risk of bias; evidence mostly low quality

f.population: 30 non-smoking patients with Miller Class I or II recessions on single-rooted teeth
f.intervention: Coronally positioned flap plus enamel matrix derivative (Emdogain)
f.comparison: Coronally positioned flap alone
f.main_result: At 18 months, root coverage was 2.66 mm with CPF+EMD versus 1.73 mm with CPF alone; complete coverage in 13 versus 5 cases.
f.sample_size: 30 patients, one tooth each (15 test, 15 control)
f.limitations: Authors note the clinical value of the advantages is subjective

f.population: Patients with single and multiple gingival recession defects with esthetic demands
f.intervention: Emdogain and mucoderm adjunctive to a coronally advanced flap for root coverage
Subpapillary continuous sling suture combining graft suture and pouch advancement in tunnel grafting
f.funding_coi: Author is a consultant for Biohorizons, Hu-Friedy and Harvest Technologies

f.population: A 35-year-old female with Miller class I recessions at teeth 23 and 24
f.intervention: Zucchelli modified coronally advanced flap with envelope technique
f.main_result: Healing satisfactory with adequate root coverage and increased keratinized tissue, stable at 3 and 6 months

f.intervention: Vision rubber dam isolation kit
materials_brands: Vision kit (Asa Dental / Style Italiano) black mint-flavored rubber dam

f.intervention: Review of advances in rubber dam materials, frames, clamps and alternatives for endodontics

f.population: Denture bearing areas (edentulous and partially edentulous arches, palate) in clinical and laboratory studies
f.intervention: Intraoral scanner (IOS) digital impression
f.comparison: A reference model or alternative impression techniques
f.main_result: IOS accuracy was comparable to conventional impressions for bony structures with attached mucosa but not for mobile tissues
f.funding_coi: No conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Within the limitations of the review, current IOS systems are not appropriate alternatives where tissue movement must be recorded

f.population: Master model of an edentulous maxilla with six implant scan bodies (in vitro)
f.intervention: Intraoral scanning with a universal 3D-printed scan aid in three designs and three materials
f.comparison: Unsplinted intraoral scans without the scan aid
f.main_result: The beige irregular scan aid had the highest trueness and improved trueness over unsplinted scans, while precision decreased with the aid
f.sample_size: 10 scans per scan aid (100 test scans, 10 reference scans)
materials_brands: Camlog implant analogs and scan bodies
f.limitations: Only one intraoral scanner and the manufacturer-recommended scan path were used

f.population: Edentulous arches with at least 3 implants in 22 patients (6 maxillary, 16 mandibular)
f.intervention: Intraoral scanning of implant scan bodies with a universal scan aid using CS3600 and TRIOS3
f.comparison: Intraoral scanning without the scan aid
f.main_result: The scan aid reduced mean deviation for CS3600 (189 to 135 μm) but not TRIOS3, and raised the share of recognized scan bodies
f.funding_coi: Open Access funding by Projekt DEAL
f.limitations: Heterogeneity of samples with different scan bodies and implant distributions

f.population: 30 patients needing a posterior onlay/inlay with supra-gingival margins
f.intervention: Chairside intraoral scanning with Aadva, True Definition or Trios
f.comparison: Conventional impressions poured in stone and scanned in the laboratory
outcomes: distance from adjacent tooth at which the margin became unclear
f.main_result: No significant difference between the three IOS; all performed similarly and all control margins were clearly visible

f.population: Patients requiring 3D intraoral scanning for dental treatments (software manual, no study population)
f.intervention: i500 intraoral scanner with Medit Scan for Clinics 1.5 software

f.population: Intraoral scanner operator factors (literature review)
f.funding_coi: No specific grant; authors declare no financial interest in the companies whose materials are included

f.population: Patient intraoral conditions affecting scanning accuracy (literature review)
Fifty Neoss implants in composite resin (in vitro)
f.intervention: Five abutment screw tightening protocols to 32 Ncm (twice with 10-min interval, twice without interval, once, tighten-counter-tighten-tighten, and two counter-tightening cycles)
f.comparison: Single tightening (Group 1T)
f.main_result: Mean reverse tightening values of the first 4 groups were 21.49 to 22.57 Ncm versus 25.51 Ncm for the tighten-counter-tighten-counter-tighten group, a significant difference.

f.population: Twenty patients needing a single implant-borne restoration
f.intervention: Screw-retained monolithic lithium disilicate hybrid abutment crown on Ti-base
f.comparison: Cement-retained monolithic lithium disilicate crown on bonded hybrid abutment
f.main_result: One cement-retained restoration failed at 6 months from Ti-base debonding; no significant difference in survival (p = .317), FIPS, OHIP, treatment time or satisfaction.
f.funding_coi: Research grant from Ivoclar Vivadent and Oral Reconstruction Foundation; no conflicts declared

f.population: 94 patients with 99 documented posterior endocrowns
f.intervention: Ceramic and composite endocrowns bonded with immediate dentin sealing
f.main_result: Survival 99.0% and success 89.9% after mean 44.7 months; 10-year Kaplan-Meier survival 98.8% and success 54.9%.
f.limitations: Few failures prevented statistical correlation with clinical parameters.

f.population: 24 extracted maxillary premolars with large standardised MOD cavities, 3 groups of 8
f.intervention: Single-increment bulk-fill flowable bases (SDR, x-tra base) under GrandioSO
f.comparison: GrandioSO placed in oblique increments
f.main_result: Bulk-fill flowable bases significantly reduced cuspal deflection versus incremental GrandioSO (SDR P=0.007, x-tra base P=0.005) with no difference in cervical microleakage.

f.population: 15 subjects with unilateral atrophic posterior mandibles
f.intervention: Short dental implants (SDI)
f.comparison: Standard-length implants with inferior alveolar nerve lateralization (IANL)
f.main_result: No implant was lost, marginal bone loss did not differ between groups at 1 year, and 2 IANL patients had transient paraesthesia.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: 20 patients with free-end situations in the mandible, two adjacent 7 mm implants per site
f.intervention: Splinted crowns on two adjacent short implants
f.comparison: Non-splinted single crowns
f.main_result: At 3 years implant survival was 100% in both groups; splinting did not affect marginal bone loss, implant health, survival or success.
f.funding_coi: Funded by the Oral Reconstruction Foundation (CF41102)

f.population: Sixty-six mice with titanium alloy implants in healed maxillary first molar sites
f.intervention: Hyper-loading by extracting remaining molars after implant crown placement
f.comparison: Normally loaded implants with remaining dentition intact
f.main_result: Hyper-loaded implants had a 3.6-fold increase in occlusal force and higher peri-implant strain, with elevated bone formation and resorption and a net gain in BV/TV.
f.funding_coi: Foundation for the National Institutes of Health, NSFC and Sichuan science grants; no conflicts declared

f.population: 95 patients with 2-3 missing posterior premolars/molars in maxilla or mandible, 209 implants
f.intervention: 6-mm short implants (diameter 4 mm) supporting splinted fixed prostheses
f.comparison: 11-mm standard-length implants supporting splinted fixed prostheses
outcomes: plaque, bleeding on probing, probing depth
f.main_result: At 5 years survival was 96.0% (6 mm) vs 98.9% (11 mm) and mean marginal bone change +0.01 vs -0.12 mm, with no significant differences.
f.sample_size: 95 patients, 209 implants (108 of 6 mm, 101 of 11 mm)
f.funding_coi: Fully sponsored by Dentsply Sirona Implants; investigators declare no financial interest

f.population: Patients with at least 2 splinted implants in the posterior maxilla (Astra Tech internal conical connection implants)
f.intervention: Prosthetic abutment height analyzed as predictor of marginal bone loss (0 to 4 mm abutments)
outcomes: marginal bone loss rate (mm/month) at 6 and 18 months post-loading
f.funding_coi: Supported by Junta de Andalucía research groups; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Retrospective design prevented sample homogenization; panoramic radiographs are less sensitive than periapical ones.

f.population: Healthy patients with 5-8 mm residual bone height receiving implants with fixed reconstructions
f.intervention: Short implants (<= 8 mm) supporting fixed reconstructions
f.comparison: Implants >8 mm placed in vertically augmented bone
f.main_result: Implant survival was similar in vertically augmented bone and short implants (95.09% vs 96.24%), with more surgical complications after augmentation (56 vs 18 patients).
f.limitations: Only four RCTs with small samples (15 to 30 per group), limited follow-up, all from the same research group.

f.population: Generally healthy subjects with completely edentulous arch(s)
f.intervention: Implant-supported full-arch fixed dental hybrid prostheses
outcomes: cumulative survival of prostheses and implants
f.main_result: Short-term survival was high for full-arch hybrid prostheses (93.3-100%) and supporting implants (87.89-100%); long-term survival could not be determined.
f.follow_up: Mean follow-up of 5-10 years (short-term) and 10 years or more (long-term)
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Few true long-term studies and potential publication, reporting and attrition bias.

f.population: 34 patients with extra-short implants (<=6.5 mm) supporting a fixed denture in the posterior mandible
f.intervention: Extra-short implants supporting fixed dentures, analyzed by crown height space, crown-to-implant ratio and offset placement
f.main_result: No implants were lost over a mean of 2 years; bone loss was greatest opposite a partial denture (1.28 mm) and correlated with crown height space.
f.funding_coi: Authors reported no conflicts of interest

f.population: Patients with implants in the posterior maxilla
f.intervention: Short implants (<=8 mm)
f.comparison: Standard length implants (>8 mm) with maxillary sinus floor augmentation (lateral window)
f.main_result: Meta-analyses found no significant differences in implant survival or marginal bone loss between short implants and standard implants with sinus augmentation.
f.funding_coi: One author received Astra Tech implants from Dentsply (2016)

f.population: Photoelastic block model with three implants (external hex, 3.8 x 12 mm)
f.intervention: Cement-retained crowns with crown/implant ratios 1:1 to 1:2 (crown height space 10-20 mm), loaded at 0 and 30 degrees
f.comparison: Axial vs 30-degree load; 1:1 ratio as reference
outcomes: microstrain at implant neck (buccal and lingual)
abutment screw fracture and crown dislodgment
f.main_result: Strain rose significantly from C/I 1:1 to 1:1.5 under 30-degree load; ratios 1:1.75 and 1:2 caused abutment screw fracture, with failures at crown height space >15 mm.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare external hex titanium implants

f.population: Published research papers and 14 popular implant manufacturers
f.intervention: Proposed length-and-diameter-based implant classification scheme
outcomes: terms used for implant length and diameter
f.main_result: Literature uses inconsistent terms for implant length and diameter ("long", "short", "standard", "wide", "narrow" most common), so a classification scheme was proposed.
f.funding_coi: Funded by King Saud University research center; authors deny conflicts of interest

f.population: 52 patients with a single missing tooth in the posterior mandibular molar region
f.intervention: Immediately loaded short single implants (5.5 x 6.6, 7.3, 8.5 mm) with fully digital workflow
f.comparison: Long implant (5.0 x 10 mm)
f.main_result: No significant group differences in insertion torque, ISQ (except week 3), marginal bone loss or soft tissue parameters; 48-week bone loss was 0.06 (long) and 0.05 mm (short).
f.sample_size: 52 patients randomized; 19 long and 27 short implants analyzed
f.funding_coi: Korea Health Technology R&D grant; no conflict of interest declared

f.population: Patients with partial edentulism in the posterior maxilla
f.intervention: Short (6-mm) implants
f.comparison: Sinus floor elevation (lateral technique) with simultaneous standard-length (>=10-mm) implants
f.main_result: At 3 years survival was 100% (short) vs 95.0% (SFE), not significant; marginal bone loss differed significantly, and surgery was shorter and cheaper with short implants.
f.sample_size: 33 test and 20 control patients; 45 implants per group
f.funding_coi: Authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: 59 patients with 4 x 7 mm short implants in premolar/molar positions supporting fixed prostheses
f.intervention: 4 mm wide, 7 mm long anodized external-connection implants with fixed prostheses, analysed by crown/implant ratio
f.comparison: C/I-R <= 2 versus > 2
f.main_result: Mean MBL was 0.67 mm; C/I-R showed only a weak nonsignificant inverse correlation with MBL (r = -0.081, P = .383).
f.funding_coi: Senior author is a consultant for Nobel Biocare
f.limitations: Conclusions drawn within stated limitations; 37 patients excluded for missing radiographs.

f.population: 13 human clinical studies (prospective or retrospective) of implants reporting C/I ratio and MBL
f.intervention: Influence of crown/implant ratio of implant-supported restorations
f.main_result: Significant negative association between C/I ratio and MBL (P = 0.012): within 0.6/1 to 2.36/1, higher C/I ratio, less MBL.
f.funding_coi: Partly supported by University of Michigan Periodontal Graduate Student Research Fund; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Conflicting and limited information on C/I ratio; most articles lacked reliability information.

f.population: Seven RCTs, 554 implants in atrophic posterior maxilla
f.intervention: Short implants (5-8 mm) without sinus lift
f.comparison: Longer implants (>8 mm) with sinus lifting
f.main_result: Survival did not differ (RR 1.00; 95% CI 0.97-1.03) while short implants had fewer complications (RR 0.58; 95% CI 0.37-0.90).
f.follow_up: at least 1 year mean follow-up (1 to 5 years in included trials)
f.funding_coi: National Natural Science Foundation of China and university funds; no conflicts declared

f.population: 55 patients with 74 six-mm tissue-level micro-rough implants placed 2000-2013
f.intervention: 6 mm micro-rough tissue-level implants in various indications
f.main_result: Survival rate 93.2% and success rate 89.2% at mean 9.1 years; smoking significantly reduced survival (HR 36.25).
f.funding_coi: Self-funded by the Department of Oral Surgery and Stomatology, University of Bern
f.limitations: Limited number of failed implants gives low statistical power in the exploratory survival models.

f.population: 19 edentulous very old (mean 85.7 y) ADL-dependent patients
f.intervention: Two interforaminal Straumann tissue-level 4.1 x 8 mm implants loaded with Locator attachments to retain mandibular overdentures
f.main_result: Implant survival up to 5 years was 94.7% with mean bone loss of 0.17 mm per year.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Tissue Level implant, Regular Neck
f.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI foundation; no conflict of interest declared
f.limitations: Few radiographs/patients available at later time points; small number of observations after year 4.

f.population: 101 patients with partial edentulism in the posterior maxilla, residual bone height 5-7 mm
f.intervention: Short 6 mm implants without grafting
f.comparison: Long 11-15 mm implants with simultaneous lateral sinus grafting
f.main_result: Implant survival was 100% in both groups at 3 years; MBL at 3 years was 0.45 mm (graft) vs 0.44 mm (short), not significant.
f.sample_size: 101 patients, 137 implants (94 patients, 129 implants at 3 years)
materials_brands: ASTRA TECH Implant System OsseoSpeed 4.0S (Dentsply Sirona Implants)
f.funding_coi: Fully funded by Dentsply Sirona Implants; no author conflict of interest reported
f.limitations: Relatively short observation period; further long-term studies required.

f.population: 30 patients with bilateral atrophic posterior mandibles (15) or maxillae (15)
f.intervention: One to three 5-mm short implants
f.comparison: At least 10-mm long implants in vertically (interpositional Bio-Oss block) or sinus (granular Bio-Oss) augmented bone
f.main_result: Three years after loading 5-mm short implants gave similar results to longer implants in augmented bone; maxillary bone loss was 1.02 mm (short) vs 1.54 mm (long), P = 0.001.
f.funding_coi: MegaGen Implant partially supported the trial and donated implants and components
f.limitations: Small sample size; 2-stage lateral window approach for sinus lift.

f.population: 30 patients with bilateral atrophic posterior mandibles (15) or maxillae (15)
f.intervention: One to three 5 mm short implants
f.comparison: At least 10 mm long implants in augmented bone (interpositional Bio-Oss blocks in mandibles, granular Bio-Oss via lateral window in maxillae)
f.main_result: At 1 year, 5 mm short implants gave similar if not better results; short implants lost 1 mm of bone versus 1.2 mm for longer implants (significant), with 3 implant failures in total.
f.funding_coi: MegaGen Implant Co. partially supported the trial and donated implants and components
f.limitations: Small sample size.

f.population: 101 patients (mean age 54.43) with 246 posterior maxillary implants
f.intervention: Internal (conical, Astra Tech) connection implants
f.comparison: External hexagonal connection implants (Microdent)
outcomes: marginal bone loss at 6 and 18 months
effect of age, smoking, periodontitis and implant width
f.main_result: MBL was significantly higher around external than internal connections (0.714 vs 0.516 mm/year); age and smoking also influenced MBL.
materials_brands: Astra Tech (Dentsply) internal conical connection implant
f.funding_coi: Partially supported by Junta de Andalucía research funding; no financial interests declared

f.population: 60 partially edentulous patients with 7-8 mm residual crestal height above the mandibular canal
f.intervention: 1 to 3 submerged 6.6-mm long short implants
f.comparison: 9.6 mm or longer implants placed in mandibles vertically augmented with interpositional Bio-Oss blocks
outcomes: radiographic peri-implant marginal bone level changes
f.main_result: At 5 years failures did not differ; augmented patients had significantly more complications (25 in 21 patients vs 6 in 6 patients) and lost more bone (2.34 vs 1.49 mm).
f.funding_coi: Biomet 3i partially supported the trial; no interference declared
f.limitations: Small sample size.

f.population: 70 patients with 100 implants in the posterior jaw supporting single crowns
f.intervention: Implants supporting single crown restorations in posterior segments, analysed by crown-to-implant length ratio
f.main_result: No significant influence of the technical or biological c/i ratio on implant survival (95.8% at 5 years), MBL or complications; smoking was the only co-factor linked to failure.
f.limitations: Findings apply only to the c/i range tested; higher c/i ratios need further study.

f.population: Patients with a posterior single-tooth gap
f.intervention: 6-mm implant (test) restored with a screw-retained single crown
f.comparison: 10-mm implant (control)
f.main_result: Implant survival at 3 y was 98% (6 mm) vs 100% (10 mm), not significant; bone-level change was -0.19 mm vs -0.33 mm, not significant.
f.sample_size: 94 implants (47 test, 47 control); 78 analysed at 3 y
materials_brands: Straumann SLActive standard plus soft tissue level implants
f.funding_coi: Grant from the International Team for Implantology (ITI Nr 517-2007); no conflicts declared

f.population: Patients rehabilitated with dental implants in the posterior jaws
f.intervention: Short implants (8 mm or less) in posterior maxilla and mandible
f.comparison: Standard implants (larger than 8 mm)
f.main_result: No significant difference in implant survival (RR 1.35, 95% CI 0.82-2.22), marginal bone loss, complications or prosthesis failures; implants shorter than 8 mm had lower survival than standard implants.
f.limitations: High risk of bias for blinding of participants and personnel.

f.population: 24 patients with atrophic edentulous free ends of a partially edentulous jaw
f.intervention: 7 mm short implants, alone or splinted to longer implants, loaded immediately or delayed
f.comparison: Delayed vs immediate loading; short-only vs mixed short and long implant bridges
f.main_result: Cumulative survival of short implants was 87% at a mean 47.72 months; immediately loaded 96.4% vs delayed 76.9% (p=0.047).
f.sample_size: 24 patients, 54 short (7 mm) and 15 longer implants
materials_brands: Brånemark System Mk III Shorty TiUnite (Nobel Biocare)
f.funding_coi: NobelBiocare provided free implants and abutments (Grant 2005-355)

f.population: Human studies of short dental implants (<10 mm) supporting fixed prostheses
f.intervention: Short dental implants (<10 mm) supporting fixed prostheses
f.comparison: Standard implants (>=10 mm)
f.main_result: Implant length had no significant effect on marginal bone loss (meta-regression P = 0.633); short and standard implants did not differ (P = 0.222).
f.funding_coi: Partly funded by the University of Michigan Graduate Periodontics Student Research Fund; no financial interests declared
f.limitations: Scarcity of long-term follow-up prospective studies.

f.population: Patients with single tooth gaps in the posterior area
f.intervention: 6 mm Standard Plus Tissue Level SLActive implant with screw-retained single crown
f.comparison: 10 mm Standard Plus Tissue Level SLActive implant
f.main_result: 5-year implant survival was 91% for 6 mm vs 100% for 10 mm implants (p=0.036); marginal bone levels did not differ.
materials_brands: Straumann Standard Plus Tissue Level SLActive implants
f.funding_coi: ITI grant (ITI Nr 517-2007); authors report no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Long-term data on short (<=8 mm) implants still lacking.

f.population: 45 patients with single-tooth sites in posterior regions
f.intervention: 6 mm long, 4.1 mm diameter moderately rough (SLA) implants loaded within 7 weeks with single crowns
f.comparison: 10 mm long, 4.1 mm diameter implants
f.main_result: After 5 years survival was 86.7% for 6 mm and 96.7% for 10 mm implants; marginal bone loss was small and similar.
materials_brands: Gold-palladium alloy and porcelain single fixed prosthesis
f.funding_coi: Funded by the ITI Research Committee; authors declare no conflict of interest

f.population: Patients needing implants in fresh extraction sockets, or in the posterior maxilla or mandible with limited bone height
f.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation; sinus elevation with grafting or vertical augmentation vs short implants
f.comparison: Unassisted socket healing; longer implants after sinus elevation or vertical augmentation
f.main_result: Short implants and implants after sinus elevation or vertical augmentation gave comparable outcomes, with fewer complications for short implants; ridge preservation reduced need for further augmentation.
f.funding_coi: Workshop funded by the European Association for Osseointegration; participant disclosures kept on file
f.limitations: Evidence derived from short-term RCTs, some from the same research group.

f.population: Patients with atrophic maxillae or mandibles
f.intervention: Short implants (<10 mm) for single or multiple units, fixed prostheses or overdentures
f.main_result: Short implants (<10 mm) can be used effectively in atrophic jaws, even with crown/implant ratios once considered excessive.
f.funding_coi: No disclosures

f.population: Human studies of 6-mm Straumann micro-rough implants
f.intervention: 6 mm micro-rough surface Straumann implants
f.main_result: Pooled early cumulative survival of 6-mm implants was 93.7% (maxilla 94.7%, mandible 98.6%); 76% of failures were early.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest; no external funding

f.population: 20 adult patients with 46 posterior single-crown implants (23 maxillary, 23 mandibular)
f.intervention: 6-mm long, 4.1-mm wide implants supporting single metalloceramic crowns in the posterior region
outcomes: risk factors (arch, bruxism, bite force, C/I ratio, occlusal table area)
f.main_result: 6-mm single-crown implants showed 91.3% survival, 28.3% screw loosening and 0.3 mm cumulative bone loss at 48 months; clinical C/I ratio and time predicted bone loss, and the mandible carried higher failure risk
f.funding_coi: ITI, CNPq and CAPES funding; no conflict of interest
f.limitations: Authors call for studies with larger sample size and longer follow-up

f.population: 33 studies of short implants (<=8.5 mm) in posterior partially edentulous jaws, 3,573 implants
f.intervention: Short implants (<=8.5 mm) placed in the posterior maxilla/mandible to support fixed restorations
f.comparison: Longer implants (>8.5 mm)
f.main_result: No significant difference in survival of short vs long implants; 5-year cumulative survival 98% (98.3% vs 97.7%)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: 95 patients with posterior partially edentulous maxilla or mandible sites
f.intervention: 6 mm (4.0 x 6) implants
f.comparison: 11 mm (4.0 x 11) standard-length implants
f.main_result: At 3 years MBL was 0.27 mm (6 mm) vs 0.44 mm (11 mm) apical to platform, favoring short implants; survival 96% vs 99%, not significant.
f.funding_coi: Fully sponsored by Dentsply Sirona Implants; two authors received lecture honoraria

f.population: Patients undergoing implant-prosthetic rehabilitation in 22 RCTs/prospective controlled studies
f.intervention: Platform-switching implant-abutment configuration
f.comparison: Platform-matching implant-abutment configuration
f.main_result: Meta-analysis of 13 RCTs: mean marginal bone loss 0.49 mm with platform switching vs 1.01 mm with platform matching (P<0.0001)
f.sample_size: 13 RCTs, 549 patients, 1035 implants in the meta-analysis
f.funding_coi: Unrestricted grant from the Camlog Foundation
f.limitations: Heterogeneous methodology, unclear or high risk of bias, short follow-up

f.population: Nine systematic reviews on the shortened dental arch in adults, covering 228 articles
f.intervention: Overview of systematic reviews with AMSTAR methodologic appraisal
f.main_result: Seven of nine SRs concluded the SDA concept is functionally sound; five were of high and four of medium AMSTAR quality
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: None of the included SRs assessed publication bias

f.population: Swedish general dental practitioners (private and public)
f.intervention: Questionnaire on attitudes toward the shortened dental arch concept
f.comparison: Private practitioners vs Public Dental Health Service; male vs female
f.main_result: Swedish GPs were generally positive toward the SDA concept (response rate 54%), with female clinicians more risk conscious and private practitioners seeing fewer advantages
f.funding_coi: Supported by the Public Dental Health Service, Skane County Council

f.population: 15 adults and 10 adolescents without stomatognathic disorder
f.intervention: Biting on Temporary Stopping to locate the main occluding area, with occlusal contact analysis
f.comparison: Adults vs adolescents
outcomes: antero-posterior position of main occluding area
f.main_result: Main occluding areas of adolescents were significantly anterior to and less stable than those of adults, and adults had larger occlusal contact area

f.population: Malaysian government dentists in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur
f.intervention: Self-administered questionnaire on SDA knowledge, perceptions and application
outcomes: clinical application of the SDA concept
f.main_result: Dentists had good knowledge and perceptions of the SDA concept (response 84.0%) but only 20.4% had applied it clinically
f.funding_coi: University of Malaya funded the study; no conflicts of interest

f.population: Tanzanian adults with shortened dental arches (725) and complete arches (125)
f.intervention: Shortened dental arches with zero to eight posterior occluding pairs
f.comparison: Subjects with complete dental arches
f.main_result: No evidence that shortened dental arches provoke TMD signs and symptoms; joint sounds were more frequent with unilateral (17%) or no (10%) posterior support
f.funding_coi: Supported by University of Nijmegen, Muhimbili University College and other bodies

f.population: Partially dentate patients treated with the shortened dental arch concept (literature review)
f.intervention: Shortened dental arch treatment approach
f.main_result: Dental arches comprising anterior and premolar regions meet the requirements of a functional dentition, with improved hygiene, comfort and possibly lower cost

f.population: General dentists in Victoria, Australia (175 respondents; 70% male, 44% rural)
f.intervention: Mailed self-administered anonymous questionnaire on awareness and opinion of the shortened dental arch (SDA) concept
outcomes: patient acceptance as judged by dentists
f.main_result: 61% of responding dentists were aware of the SDA concept and 78.4% considered it useful in clinical practice.
f.sample_size: 175 respondents from 434 dentists surveyed (40.3% response rate)
f.funding_coi: Financial assistance from the Australian Dental Research Foundation

f.population: Human studies on the relationship between dentition and oral function (83 included articles)
f.intervention: Systematic literature search (PubMed) on which dentition assures oral function
f.main_result: A minimum of 20 teeth with nine to 10 pairs of contacting units is associated with adequate masticatory efficiency and ability.
f.sample_size: 83 articles from an initial pool of 1460 citations
f.limitations: Few studies with high levels of evidence were found

f.population: Patients with residual bone height <5 mm needing unilateral sinus floor elevation for two nonadjacent implants (20 treated, 18 analysed)
f.intervention: Lateral sinus augmentation with a composite graft and bone-core biopsies at mesial and distal implant sites after 6 months
f.comparison: Mesial versus distal sites within the same sinus
outcomes: sinus width and residual bone height as predictors
f.main_result: %NFMT was higher in mesial (17.5) than distal (11.6) sites (p = .0004) and correlated negatively with sinus width but not with residual bone height.
f.follow_up: 6 months to biopsy; implants followed 7 to 31 months after loading
f.funding_coi: Self-funded
f.limitations: Single biopsy time point (6 months) and a single composite graft, so results do not extend to other bone substitutes

f.population: Ten edentulous patients with marked bilateral maxillary atrophy
f.intervention: Graftless sinus augmentation: sinus membrane lifted and held by a resorbable PDLLA membrane, space filled with blood clot
f.comparison: Conventional sinus augmentation with autograft and xenograft mixture on the contralateral side
f.main_result: Implant survival was higher on the conventional side (96.7% vs 86.2%, p<0.001) and bone gain was greater (9.69 vs 6.20 mm).
f.funding_coi: No external funding; no conflict of interest

f.population: 430 patients with transcrestal sinus floor elevation and single-implant insertion in sites with RBH ≤5 mm, seven Italian centers
f.intervention: Transcrestal sinus floor elevation with simultaneous or staged single-implant placement
f.main_result: Early implant failure occurred in 12 of 430 implants (2.8%) and was associated with large sinus width and membrane perforation.
f.follow_up: Minimum 12 months after prosthetic crown delivery
f.limitations: Retrospective design with records not designed for the study; membrane perforations may have been underestimated

f.population: 161 patients with oroantral communications treated at the University Hospital in Vienna, 2000 to 2005
f.intervention: Closure of the oroantral communication with a pedicled buccal fat pad
f.main_result: Closure was insufficient in 12 of 161 patients (7.5%); success was nearly 98% excluding severe and complicating cases.

f.population: 86 patients (92 sinus lifts, 209 implants) with residual ridge height 0.1 to 7 mm in the posterior maxilla
f.intervention: Lateral window sinus augmentation with sagittal sandwich technique (autogenous bone and ABBM, 3:7) and delayed implant placement
f.comparison: Implants in native bone (group C) versus severe (group S) and moderate (group M) residual height
f.main_result: 3 of 209 implants (1.4%) failed over 10 years and marginal bone loss did not differ between groups at 1, 2 and 5 years.
materials_brands: Nobel Biocare Branemark Mk III / Mk IV implants
f.funding_coi: Dr. Urban received honoraria for speaking for Nobel BioCare and Geistlich Pharma

f.population: 25 patients (34 Astra implants) in the posterior maxilla at 10-year follow-up
f.intervention: Osteotome sinus floor elevation with simultaneous implant placement without bone grafts
outcomes: height of residual peri-implant alveolar bone
f.main_result: Single-tooth and partially edentulous cases had 100% survival; mean marginal bone loss was 0.6 mm at 10 years.
f.sample_size: 34 implants in 25 patients (from 53 implants in 36 patients originally)
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.population: Ten patients needing bilateral two-staged maxillary sinus floor augmentation
f.intervention: Sinus augmentation with porcine bone mineral (Symbios) mixed 20:80 with autogenous bone
f.comparison: Anorganic bovine bone (Bio-Oss) mixed 20:80 with autogenous bone on the contralateral side
f.main_result: Graft resorption and histologic, histomorphometric and immunohistochemical results did not differ between bovine and porcine xenografts after 6 months.
f.funding_coi: Partially funded by Dentsply Sirona Implants; senior author is a frequent Dentsply Sirona speaker
f.limitations: Small sample size (10 cases per group) and possibly excessive graft maturation time

f.population: Patients with maxillary atrophy undergoing sinus lift (12 randomized split-mouth trials)
f.intervention: Sinus lift with autogenous bone plus growth factors or bone substitutes, or bone substitutes alone
f.comparison: Sinus lift with autogenous bone alone
f.main_result: Bone fraction was significantly higher with autogenous bone than with beta-TCP alone (P = 0.036); other substitutes and PRP showed no difference.
f.follow_up: Bone fraction at 5 months; implant survival at 1 year

f.population: 152 elevated maxillary sinuses in 76 New Zealand white rabbits
f.intervention: Bilateral maxillary sinus floor elevation with xenograft granules (Bio-Oss or Cerabone), analysed histologically for mucosal adhesion stages
outcomes: distance between elevated and undetached mucosae
f.main_result: 31 of 152 sinuses showed adhesions: 12 proximity, 15 fusion and 4 synechia stages, with epithelial hyperplasia.
f.funding_coi: Funded by ARDEC Academy; no conflicts of interest declared
f.limitations: Rabbit model has thinner sinus mucosa and faster healing than humans, and adhesions were infrequent (about 10%).

f.population: Patients undergoing lateral-window sinus augmentation with large schneiderian membrane perforations
f.intervention: Repair of large perforations with a bioabsorbable collagen membrane stabilized outside the antrostomy and folded inward to form a new roof or a pouch
outcomes: sinus health on radiographs and CT
f.main_result: No procedural failures in 20 consecutive patients; histology at 6 to 9 months showed vital bone formation (26% in one case).

f.population: Patients with a single missing tooth in the posterior maxilla
f.intervention: One 6-mm implant without grafting for a single crown
f.comparison: One 11-mm implant combined with maxillary sinus floor augmentation
f.main_result: At 10 years implant survival was 89.5% (6 mm) vs 90.9% (11 mm) and marginal bone loss 0.18 vs 0.26 mm, with no significant difference (p = .650).
f.sample_size: 21 implants in 20 patients (6 mm) and 20 implants in 18 patients (11 mm)
f.funding_coi: 1-year study partly sponsored by Dentsply Implants (materials supplied); authors declare no economic interest
f.limitations: Loss to follow-up of a number of initial participants.

f.intervention: Lateral window technique for maxillary sinus augmentation
f.main_result: The authors conclude that lateral-window sinus augmentation is a safe, reliable and predictable surgery whose risk factors can be managed with minimal trauma.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest declared

f.intervention: Classification of sinus membrane perforations into 5 classes, each with a repair technique, during crestal-approach sinus augmentation
f.main_result: The authors propose a 5-class classification and treatment planning guide for sinus membrane perforations.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported

f.population: Patients with implants placed at maxillary posterior sites with 3-6 mm residual bone height
f.intervention: Implant placement with simultaneous transcrestal sinus floor elevation (tSFE)
f.comparison: Implant placement with simultaneous lateral sinus floor elevation (lSFE)
f.main_result: At 6 years implant survival was 100%; totCON% was 96% (tSFE) vs 100% (lSFE) (p = .036) and median dMBL 0.3 vs 0 mm (p = .024), with similar peri-implant health.
f.sample_size: 43 patients at the 6-year visit (21 tSFE, 22 lSFE)
f.funding_coi: Supported by University of Ferrara research centre, Regione Emilia-Romagna, Osteology Foundation grants and a Geistlich Biomaterials donation; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Parallel-arm rather than split-mouth design did not control individual healing response.

f.intervention: Snap-On Smile removable appliance made of crystallized acetyl resin

f.population: Postextraction sockets in patients, from five included RCTs/controlled clinical trials
f.intervention: Socket preservation with deproteinized bovine bone mineral (DBBM)
f.comparison: Natural healing
f.main_result: DBBM socket preservation gave a significantly lower new bone percentage than natural healing (MD -24.75, p = 0.001), with no difference in connective tissue (MD 0.60, p = 0.83).
f.follow_up: 3 to 6 months biopsy time in included studies
f.funding_coi: No competing interest declared
f.limitations: Lack of high-quality research; further large-sample studies are needed.

f.population: Patients with large bone defects after tooth extraction (31 teeth)
f.intervention: Reactive soft tissue left in the defect and filled with collagen sheets, wound left open
outcomes: vital bone and connective tissue percentage on histomorphometry
f.main_result: Mean vertical bone gain was 12.13 mm at 3 months (P < .05), with vital bone 41.59% and connective tissue 50.37%.
f.funding_coi: No conflicts of interest reported
f.limitations: Results are not supported by a biologic explanation and need further laboratory and clinical research.

f.population: Adult patients needing extraction of at least one single- or multi-rooted tooth (third molars excluded), from 22 RCTs
f.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation modalities (socket grafting with bone substitutes, socket sealing, blood-derived products, cell therapy, rhBMP-2)
f.comparison: Tooth extraction alone (spontaneous socket healing)
outcomes: horizontal and vertical ridge dimensional change
f.main_result: ARP by socket grafting prevented horizontal (1.99 mm) and vertical mid-buccal (1.72 mm) and mid-lingual (1.16 mm) bone resorption compared with extraction alone.
f.funding_coi: Two authors declare research support or lecture fees from several implant and biomaterial companies (Geistlich, Osteogenics, Dentsply Implants and others); Chambrone declares none
f.limitations: The effect of other local and systemic factors could not be assessed quantitatively, and a superior ARP approach could not be determined.

f.population: Human subjects who required single or multiple tooth extraction
f.intervention: Alveolar ridge preservation procedures after tooth extraction
f.comparison: Tooth extraction alone without further intervention
outcomes: vertical bone height changes (buccal, lingual, mesial, distal)
f.main_result: Horizontal bone loss was reduced by 1.86 mm with ridge preservation versus extraction alone.
f.funding_coi: No financial support, no conflicts of interest

f.population: Patients needing single-rooted tooth extraction in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Ridge preservation with guided bone regeneration (Bio-Oss + Bio-Gide) or socket seal (Bio-Oss + Mucograft Seal)
f.comparison: Unassisted socket healing
outcomes: radiographic buccal and palatal ridge height
socket and alveolar process cross-sectional area
bone augmentation need at implant placement
f.main_result: Buccal ridge height rose 0.65 mm with socket seal, stayed stable with GBR (0.07 mm) and fell 0.52 mm in controls.
f.funding_coi: Military of Defence research support; no conflicts declared
f.limitations: Low statistical power for ridge width changes

f.population: Twenty patients with non-molar teeth indicated for extraction
f.intervention: Ridge preservation with autogenous whole-tooth graft, covered by collagen membrane
f.comparison: Autogenous demineralized dentin graft (0.6N HCl, 30 min)
outcomes: buccal and lingual ridge height change (CBCT)
histomorphometric new bone, graft remnant and soft tissue area
f.main_result: Ridge width fell 0.85 mm with whole-tooth graft and 1.02 mm with demineralized dentin graft, with no significant difference.
f.funding_coi: Funded by Cairo University; no conflicts of interest
f.limitations: Only non-molar sites and few histological samples (n = 4 per group); soft tissue and patient-reported outcomes not assessed

f.population: 75 patients needing single tooth extraction in the anterior maxilla
f.intervention: Early implant placement 8 weeks after extraction with ARP using DBBM-C covered by collagen matrix or palatal graft
f.comparison: Early implant placement after spontaneous healing, no ARP
outcomes: plaque, bleeding on probing, probing depth
